# Autobuilder Roadmap

## Status markers (authoritative — the overview index and every tool read these)

| marker | meaning |
|---|---|
| `[ ]` | open — not started |
| `[~]` | in progress — partially shipped, remaining scope stated in the body |
| `[>]` | deferred — not now, **no verdict reached**; carries a re-entry condition |
| `[x]` | **built** — the capability was delivered and verified |
| `[n]` | **declined** — measured, and the evidence says it does not earn its build; a re-entry condition may still be recorded |
| `[o]` | **obsoleted** — the premise dissolved, or the mechanisms the ticket names were deleted by other work |
| `[s]` | **subsumed** — folded into another ticket, which now owns the capability |
| `[r]` | **retracted** — the diagnosis was wrong; there was nothing to build |

**Why the closure kinds exist (added 2026-07-25, user direction).** `[x]` previously meant all five
closed states at once, so the census read as a capability inventory. It is not: `T4-C` was closed
because every mechanism it named had been deleted, and `T4-J`'s filed `TuningParameterStore` never
existed (an audit shipped instead) — yet both rendered identically to `T4-CA`, which is built and
field-validated. A session then read the tier as delivered capability and told the user the loop
already had "signals derived from observed behaviour" and "persistent state across runs". Neither
exists. `[n]/[o]/[r]` mark tickets where **no capability was delivered**; `[s]` means the capability
exists under another id. Declining on measured evidence is a good outcome and stays visible as one —
what the marker no longer does is disguise it as delivery.

Status is recorded ONLY here. `roadmap-overview.md` is generated from these markers and
`python3 scripts/next_work.py` reports the census by kind — never maintain a second status list by
hand ([[feedback-roadmap-is-the-queue]]).

1. **Symbol-import hallucination class** (`bf19736`, under T4-AZ/T2-DY/T4-BM): the LLM lookup answered `BookNotFoundException` with Spring's `ResourceNotFoundException` (and `LoanNotFoundException` with a nonexistent commons-lang3 FQN), cached forever, re-fired 4× because pom.xml digest churn re-cleared the T2-DY blacklist every cycle. Fixed: simple-name equality invariant (new answers + cached hits self-heal), progress-aware re-probe outcome recording (a fix whose targeted diagnostic disappeared is a success even when the build stays red), `markResolutionFailed` propagation on persistent failure, hard `MAX_TOTAL_ATTEMPTS=4` ledger cap.

**Watch item (not fixed):** consolidation's existing-wins anchored `Loan` in `com.example.demo.loan` because the first merge of the fresh run landed there — first-landing-wins can anchor a friction-maximizing layout on from-scratch runs. ### Design lens (2026-06-09): completion vs termination are two different questions

Surfaced analysing the live run `firestarter/logs/autobuilder.log` (2026-06-08 23:5x → 06-09 00:01, root `goal-df779783`). The loop conflates two distinct stop conditions into one signal — *"are there active subgoals in the tree?"* — which the planner fully controls, so neither condition actually works.

- **Completion** — *is the goal objectively satisfied?* (feature coverage + acceptance). Should be **hard to trip falsely.**
- **Termination** — *is another cycle worth spending?* (progress / budget). Must fire **even when the goal is NOT satisfied**, or an LLM that can always synthesise one more subgoal runs forever.

A healthy loop halts on **either**. Current state:

- **Completion brake — `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied` (T2-DR).** Patched repeatedly (T1-CO, T1-CQ, T1-DD, T1-DJ) but two defects survive: it is **coverage-blind** (checks only that *the subgoals that happen to be loaded* are terminal+passing, not that they cover the root's named features), and it fires on a **transient empty active-set during replan**. Live proof at 23:53:26: the planner pruned the one ACTIVE subgoal to SUBSUMED ("superseded by replanning"), T1-CN saw all-children-terminal and delegated to `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied`, which marked root COMPLETED ("evidence ledger clear: 3 subgoal(s) accounted for") and logged "loop should halt" — then the *same* replan injected four new Loans subgoals (BUILD_FIX LoanController + the three `/loans` endpoints), so `currentSubGoalId` went non-null again and the halt never took effect. Loans was demonstrably unfinished (compile errors + unimplemented endpoints). Recurred at 00:00:46. **Root cause: prune-then-inject is not atomic, and closure is coverage-blind.**
- **Termination brakes are all activity-based, and productive churn resets them.** `T1-EB` (`consecutiveZeroWorkCycles`) fires only on `BUILD_BROKEN` + zero-work; `T1-EI` (`consecutivePlannerEmptyOutputCycles`) resets on *any merge or any successful injection*; per-parent exhaustion (T2-AL/`ExhaustionPatternDetector`, T2-BJ, T2-CB) resets when the planner injects a fresh subgoal. This run is *productive churn* — 9 merges, evolution writes files, real subgoals injected each replan, build flapping (43 `COMPILE_OK` / 145 `COMPILE_ERROR`) — so every activity-based counter keeps resetting and nothing accumulates at the root. The brakes detect **absence of activity**, never **activity without convergence** (cf. line ~1272: "T1-EB fires only on BUILD_BROKEN … the planner thinks it's making progress, the destruction happens downstream").
- **The missing convergence brake is already filed: `T4-I`** (Cross-cycle behavioral pattern heuristics — "score-progress divergence: `goalProgress == PROGRESSING` but no merge in the last K cycles," file-churn-without-progress). That is the termination-side complement: a root-level progress measure the planner *can't* reset by renaming work. See T4-I body (sharpened 2026-06-09 with this run).

**Implication for fixes:** do **not** make `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied` coverage-strict in isolation — it is currently the *only* mechanism that ever halts this loop, so tightening it without a working convergence brake yields forever-busy (the failure mode the user flagged). Sequence: land the convergence/termination brake (T4-I, root-scoped) **first**, then make completion coverage-aware + atomic. See [[project-three-disciplines-lens]] (failures→priors) and [[project-introspection-as-north-star]] (a self-model would track its own convergence).

## Tier 1 — Correctness

- [ ] **T1-FS: every score read is unscoped — the evaluation prompt carries 71 runs' score history, 60% of its own context window, and 259 files that do not exist** (`agent/evaluation/history/Neo4jScoreHistoryService` reads, `protocol/evaluation/EvaluationProtocolContract` SCORE HISTORY block, `agent/evaluation/score/ScoringService`, `ScoreRegressionHeuristic` via `lastScore`) — **filed 2026-08-23, user-spotted while reading a live prompt.**
  - **Tier note:** T1 — observably wrong input to a decision, unbounded resource waste, and a silent regression. Not T2: nothing here is a defensible-but-dumb policy, the reader simply ignores a discriminator the writer sets.
  - **The defect in one line:** `recordScores` / `recordGlobalScore` STAMP `fs.runId` and `fs.lineageId` — the code comment says stamping is "what lets a lineage's history be told apart from the run currently executing" — and **all three readers drop the stamp**: `getAllScoreHistories()` (`MATCH (fs:FileScore)`), `getScoreHistory(path)` (`MATCH (fs:FileScore {path:$path})`), `getLastGlobalScore()` (`MATCH (gs:GlobalScore) ... LIMIT 2`).
  - **Measured live, run `2026-08-23_01-15-20`:**

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | FileScore nodes returned | **9,216**, across **71 runs / 70 lineages** |
    | rendered SCORE HISTORY block | **68,823 chars ≈ 17,205 tokens** |
    | context window | 32,768, less a 4,096 response reserve |
    | **share of usable prompt** | **~60%** |
    | file paths shown to the model | **269** |
    | file paths that exist on disk | **10** — so **259 are other runs' files** |
    | scores on one file (`Book.java`) | **507**, in a run that had done **17 cycles** |

  - **⚠ IT MANUFACTURES A FALSE DIAGNOSIS, AND THE LOOP ACTS ON IT.** The phantom paths span `com.example.demo`, `library`, `domain`, `web` — different package layouts chosen by different runs. The model's own words: *"severely fragmented with dozens of duplicate, conflicting implementations across multiple packages (demo, library, domain, web, etc.)"*. **It is describing the union of 71 runs' file trees and attributing it to a 10-file project.** In run `2026-08-22_00-23-46` that narrative appears **546 times** against **0 javac duplicate-class errors** — and the run still scored 23/23, so the loop spent cycles on a defect the compiler never saw.
  - **⚠ TWO QUIETER CORRUPTIONS.** `computeRecentDeltas()` takes the last two entries of a cross-run list, so a "recent delta" can be the difference between two DIFFERENT runs' scores. And `getLastGlobalScore()` gives a fresh run a `lastScore` from whatever run last wrote one — which is the input to `ScoreRegressionHeuristic`, so a new run can be penalised for "regressing" against a stranger.
  - **WHEN IT BROKE: `2026-07-26 feat(graph): T1-D — reset severs the lineage instead of wiping the graph`.** Before that, reset wiped the graph, so an unscoped reader was ACCIDENTALLY correct. Making lineages durable silently broke every reader that had not been scoped. **The general lesson is bigger than this ticket: `T4-CL` is the audit of exactly this class, and it is still open.**
  - **What this does and does NOT invalidate.** NOT affected: `smoke23.sh` (zero model/graph dependencies), so every smoke score, the 39% build/boot failure rate and the drift measurement stand; the 2026-08-22 model comparison (mocked `AgentGraphService`, no score history); `T6-M`'s failure families (compiler output). AFFECTED: the loop's evaluation inputs on every run since 2026-07-26, and any conclusion drawn from the loop's PROSE. **Corollary worth testing: the 39% failure baseline may be PESSIMISTIC**, since those runs ran on a corrupted prompt.
  - **Fix:** scope all three reads by `runId`. **Choose runId over lineageId deliberately:** a resumed run's prior scores describe the same tree and are arguably relevant, but `T4-CD` already establishes that loaded state is hypothesis and drops banked criteria reads on resume — carrying prior-run SCORES would contradict that. When `runId` is unavailable, return EMPTY rather than everything: no history is safe, a stranger's history is not.
  - **DoD:** the three queries filter on `runId`; a test proves a second run's scores are invisible to the first; the rendered block for a 10-file project lists at most those files; and a field run shows the block back at a plausible size. **Then re-measure the failure baseline** — it was taken under this.
  - **Relates to:** `T4-CL` (the open audit of per-run-disposable assumptions), `T6-M`/`T6-L` (baselines taken under the defect), `T4-AP` (prompt bloat — this dwarfs everything that audit found).

  - **Retry-policy remainder of fix direction (3) SHIPPED 2026-07-03 — closes the ticket** (not a new slice; this half of (3) was left open when slice 2 shipped the fail-fast/timed-opens half). Run 3 (2026-07-03, 271 cyc, killed in an ollama starvation storm at 05:07) measured the gap: `LLMClient` recorded ONE breaker failure only after ALL retries exhausted, so each call absorbed `retryMaxAttempts × read-timeout` (~6 min) per counted failure — ~48 min of storm before the threshold opened the circuit — and the fixed 5 s retry delay re-queued work against an endpoint still computing the aborted generation. Fix: every failed attempt records to the breaker at the moment it fails (the attempt is the unit of evidence about the endpoint); the retry loop consults `isOpen()` between attempts and abandons remaining retries the moment the circuit opens (own failures or another thread's); retry delay doubles per attempt (`retryBackoffMs`, capped 60 s). A transient single-attempt failure followed by a success still nets to closed (success resets the consecutive counter) — a healthy endpoint never opens. The old one-failure-per-call semantics was PINNED by a test ("must see exactly ONE logical failure, not three") — replaced with the run-3-grounded attempt-level pins + a mid-call-abandon test. Suite 1731 green (all 175 test classes verified present in the run).
  - **Call-site map for `advanceOrClose()` (2026-07-02, precondition for the design):** 16 loop-internal `getCurrentSubGoal()` sites in 8 classes — `CycleExecutor` ×4 (125/438/519/600 — the natural home for one explicit `advanceOrClose()` per cycle step), `PlannerAgent` ×4 (97/146/549/768 — 146 explicitly RELIES on recovery re-selection "afterRemoval"), `BlockerSubgoalInjector` ×2, `ExecutionEligibilityExplainer` ×2 (a read-mostly EXPLAINER mutating via the getter — worst offender, likely should peek), `GoalConsolidationService` ×1, `BuildBlockGate` ×1, `CycleContextCoordinator` ×1. Shape of the fix: ONE `advanceOrClose()` early in `CycleExecutor.runCycle`, everything downstream in the same cycle peeks; the open question is whether PlannerAgent's mid-cycle removal paths (146) need a second advance point or can consume the return value of their own removal call.

    2. For each, check the *current* probe diagnostics + the *current* file content. Emit a new behaviour event `build_fix_subgoal_closed` (payload: `{subgoalId, symbol, file, trigger: "diagnostic_disappeared" | "compile_ok"}`).
    3. If `currentSubGoalId` pointed at a closed subgoal, run the same `resolveNextActiveLeaf` path T1-EL uses for stale-pointer repair.
  - **Fix — secondary (stricter creation guard):** Before `BlockerSubgoalInjector` files a new BUILD_FIX subgoal, check whether the referenced `(symbol, file)` already has an ACTIVE BUILD_FIX subgoal *or* the file currently does not reference the symbol. Either condition → skip injection. Closes the "create 10 phantom siblings for the same fictional error" failure mode at the source. The closure gate handles the legacy backlog; this guard prevents new entries.

Removed subgoal-shift suppression from `ContextLineageTracker.resolveLastAuthorErrors` and `CompileDiagnosticPromptBlock.evaluate`. Carrier lifecycle now: write on probe-rejection, overwrite on next probe, clear on merge — staleness is a property of compile state, not goal state. Existing `CompileDiagnosticPromptBlockTest.subgoalShift_noBlock_noSignal` (which asserted the bug) replaced with `subgoalShift_doesNotSuppress_steeringStillFires` regression-lock. `ContextLineageTrackerTest.t2dt_subgoalChanged_clearsAuthorErrors` (also asserted the bug) replaced with `t1ew_subgoalChanged_stillCarriesAuthorErrorsForward`. ~30 LOC net change; 1399/1399 tests pass.
  - **Frame — real logic bug producing silently-wrong behaviour.** T2-DT/T2-DV's documented purpose is "after a probe rejection with author-errors, surface the diagnostics in the next cycle's evolution prompt." In practice it fires almost never because the carrier's identity is tied to the *subgoal*, which always shifts between the rejection cycle and the next cycle via T1-DM BUILD_FIX subgoal injection. Two enforcement sites then independently clear/suppress the carrier on the subgoal change, both silently (no behaviour event emitted).
  - **Mechanism (verified against `behaviour-2026-05-29_00-44-49.ndjson`):**
    1. Cycle N: probe rejects with AUTHOR_ERROR. `EvaluationAgent.tryDeferRejectedMutation` writes `lastAuthorErrors` stamped with `subgoalId = ctx.currentSubGoalId()`.
    2. `MergeAgent` → `BlockerSubgoalInjector.injectBuildFixSubgoalIfAbsent` (T1-DM) fires on the same rejection and creates a new BUILD_FIX subgoal, sets it as current.
    3. Cycle N+1: `ContextLineageTracker.resolveLastAuthorErrors` sees `subgoalChanged(...)` returns true → clears the carrier to null.
    4. `CompileDiagnosticPromptBlock.evaluate` sees null carrier → returns reason `"no-author-errors"` (suppressed=false; no event emitted).
    5. LLM sees no compile-diagnostic steering. Same shape gets re-proposed. T2-DT/T2-DV produce zero signal.
  - **Run evidence:**
    - **Day 2 treatment** (`backup/20260529_enabled_false`): 5 `REFUSED_AUTHOR_ERROR` outcomes (`authorErrorCount=2` each), **0** `evolution_steering_compile_diagnostics_fed_back`, **0** `evolution_steering_suppressed`. Every rejected cycle followed by a cycle with a different `currentSubGoalId`.
    - **Day 2 control** (`backup/20260529_enabled_true`): 0 author-error rejections (all DEFERRED), so no candidate situations existed. T2-DT silently inactive but the run didn't surface it.
  - **Root cause — category error in the carrier's identity.** `CompileAuthorErrors` describes a property of the *codebase*: "the previous compile probe produced these errors at file:line." That fact is a property of disk state, not of the goal hierarchy. Tying the carrier identity to a subgoal ID was wrong from the start. The intended subgoal-shift suppression was a defence against stale steering when the planner moves on — but in practice the planner moves on *because of* the rejection (T1-DM injection), which is exactly when steering is most valuable.
  - **Fix:**
    1. **Drop `subgoalId` from `CompileAuthorErrors`.** Record becomes `(List<ClassifiedDiagnostic> diagnostics)`.
    2. **Drop the subgoal-shift check in `ContextLineageTracker.resolveLastAuthorErrors`.** Keep the `merged() → clear` check (a successful merge resolved the errors).

  - **Shipped 2026-05-27:** `ScoreRegressionHeuristic.evaluate(...)` now short-circuits to a 0.0-confidence opinion (preserving the input states) when `outcome.mutationState() == NOT_EVALUATED`, before the Δ-vs-baseline calculation. Test added: `notEvaluatedOutcome_abstains_evenWhenScoreLooksLikeCatastrophicDrop` in `ScoreRegressionHeuristicTest`. Verified in `behaviour-2026-05-27_22-30-18.ndjson` cycle 5: the previously-rejected `llmState=NOT_EVALUATED, llmScore=0.0` case now passes through without spurious rejection.
  - **Frame:** real logic bug — heuristic compares this-cycle's `score=0.0` against the prior accepted mutation's score (e.g. 0.77) and fires Δ≈-0.7 → CRITICAL override → REJECTED, even though `llmState=NOT_EVALUATED` means the LLM explicitly declined to produce a number (typically because the proposal was a no-diff re-feed of an already-merged mutation). The 0.0 isn't a regression signal; it's a "no signal" signal.
  - **Run telemetry (consistent across two audit windows):**
    | Run | Cycles | Same bug fires | mutationId re-fed |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `2026-05-23_03-45-48` (baseline) | 38 | 2 | yes |
    | `2026-05-25_15-37-52` | 66 | 1 (cycle 4, Δ=-0.77) | `6ec32847…` (cycle 3 → re-fed cycle 4) |
    | `2026-05-27_01-45-17` | 22 | 2 (cycle 9 Δ=-0.72, cycle 10 Δ=-0.37) | `559bd364aa` (re-fed twice after cycle 8 merge) |
  - **Root cause:** in `mutation_negotiated` events the same `mutationId` is re-scored after the merged cycle that originally produced it; the evaluator returns `llmScore=0.0, llmState=NOT_EVALUATED` because evolution produced a no-diff re-proposal of work already on disk. `ScoreRegressionHeuristic` reads `currentScore=0.0` against `lastScore≈0.77` and emits CRITICAL with confidence 0.95. Override fires, mutation is REJECTED, cycle wasted. Two wasted cycles per occurrence on average.
  - **Fix:** `ScoreRegressionHeuristic.score(...)` short-circuits to a neutral opinion (no override) when the incoming `EvaluationOutcome.mutationState() == NOT_EVALUATED` OR the `llmState == NOT_EVALUATED`. The "no signal" interpretation matches `NoMeaningfulChangeHeuristic`'s domain — same proposal, same content, no new judgement. Update `EvaluationAgent.scoring` so the scoring snapshot carries the upstream `llmState` (it already carries score; the state needs to be propagated alongside).
  - **Tests:** `ScoreRegressionHeuristicTest` — new case: prior score 0.80, current score 0.0, current state NOT_EVALUATED → returns NEUTRAL opinion (no override). Regression-lock test from the verbatim cycle-9/10 cycleIds in `behaviour-2026-05-27_01-45-17.ndjson`.
  - **Effort:** ~10 LOC in heuristic + ~5 LOC plumbing + 2 tests. Tier 1 because it's a false-positive that materially drops merge rate (≥2 wasted cycles per affected run).
  - **Depends on:** Nothing. Local fix.
  - **Enables:** Removes one of the two known categories of false-rejection that drive zero-work loops into T1-EI pause; cuts ~10–15% of wasted cycles per long-form run.
  - **Filed 2026-05-27** after the post-T1-ET comparison analysis surfaced the same bug shape in three consecutive audit windows.

  ### Part A — `BlockerExtractor.classify()` missing `PACKAGE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` case (T4-BG/T4-BI half-implementation, primary)

  - **Observed (2026-05-25 01:10 run, `behaviour-2026-05-25_01-10-21.ndjson`, 12 cycles, 0 merges, 8 rejections):** 4 of 8 rejections are the *identical* `blocker_extraction_outcome` event:
    ```
    result=REFUSED_UNKNOWN  def=2  ae=0  unk=4
    shapes=[
      "[ERROR] .../MemberController.java:[14,24] package javax.validation does not exist",
      "[ERROR] .../MemberController.java:[15,36] package javax.validation.constraints does not exist",
      "cannot find symbol",
      "symbol: class ..."
    ]
    ```
    Same line, same file, 4× across 90 s. Every cycle re-proposes `import javax.validation.Valid;` etc., the probe rejects, ledger never sees it, resolver never runs, no learning.
  - **Root cause — chain of unfulfilled promises across T4-BF → T4-BG → T4-BI:**
    1. **T4-BF (shipped 2026-05-24, `BlockerExtractor.java:203-214`)** classifier explicitly punts on `package X.Y.Z does not exist` lines — see the T4-BF roadmap entry under "Design — three coherent fixes":
       > `DEFERRABLE`: `cannot find symbol`, `symbol: class|variable|method ...`, `no suitable constructor found for`, `package X.Y.Z does not exist` (**the last only when WS-2/T4-BG ships — until then `UNKNOWN`**).
    2. **T4-BG (shipped 2026-05-24, commit `48eae0b`)** ships `WellKnownPackageRegistry` for the **resolver SPI side only**. The T4-BG roadmap entry's "Pairs with" line claims:
       > **T4-BF** (when registry covers `package does not exist`, T4-BF's classifier promotes it from `UNKNOWN` to `DEFERRABLE`)
       — but **no commit in T4-BG actually touched `BlockerExtractor`.** The "WS-2" handoff that T4-BF deferred to never happened. T4-BG's commit message `"ledger records entries; javax.validation cascade ends"` is **overclaim** — it ends the cascade only for the path where the diagnostic reaches the resolver, which doesn't apply to in-cycle javax imports because the classifier blocks them at extraction.
    3. **T4-BI (shipped 2026-05-25, commit `a64d7bc`)** adds the `SymbolImportResolver` import-rewrite path (`javax.validation` → `jakarta.validation`). Same problem upstream: the rewriter only runs when a mutation reaches the **deferred-mutation ledger**, and the ledger never sees `REFUSED_UNKNOWN` outcomes. T4-BI is **unreachable for in-cycle javax imports** until Part A lands. The `package-replace:*` rule has never fired on a real run.
  - **Effect on system behaviour:** The cascade T4-BG was filed to close (run `2026-05-23_03-45-48` — 61 % of rejections naming javax.validation) is **still live** in the 01:10 run. Same shape, same cause, two ships later. When the LLM picks a goal that pulls javax-style imports (a Spring Boot 3 + Bean Validation feature), the entire feature is unreachable — the loop just re-proposes the same broken import.
  - **Why this is Tier 1, not Tier 4 completion:** T4-BF/T4-BG/T4-BI as shipped *claim* in their commit messages and roadmap entries to have closed this. They have not. A reader (or future agent) consulting the roadmap to choose what to work on next would conclude the resolver chain is complete; it is not. Tier-1 because (a) the system has a *capability already declared shipped* that is silently unreachable, and (b) the wall-clock symptom is real loss of merges. Per `feedback_one_invariant_one_home.md`: the invariant *"unresolved external packages must reach the resolver path"* has two enforcement sites (classifier + registry), but only the second was wired. One ticket to wire both ends.
  - **Fix — primary (classifier):** Add `PACKAGE_DOES_NOT_EXIST` pattern to `BlockerExtractor`:
    ```java
    private static final Pattern PACKAGE_DOES_NOT_EXIST = Pattern.compile(
            "package\\s+([\\w.]+)\\s+does\\s+not\\s+exist", Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE);
    ```
    Reclassify hits as `DEFERRABLE`. Emit a `MutationBlocker.missingPackage(name)` (new factory on `MutationBlocker`) so the deferred-mutation ledger can re-stage. New `Outcome` field is *not* needed — `blockers` already carries `MutationBlocker` shapes; this is one more.
  - **Fix — secondary (registry-aware classification, optional but matches roadmap claim):** Plumb a `WellKnownPackageRegistry` reference into `BlockerExtractor.extract(...)`. When the package matches `registry.isCovered(prefix)` *and* `registry.replacedBy(prefix, pomXml)` returns a replacement (the T4-BI rewrite path), upgrade the blocker shape to `MutationBlocker.packageRewrite(oldPrefix, newPrefix, gav)` so the restager can dispatch straight to `SymbolImportResolver.resolveMissingPackage(...)` instead of going through the LLM lookup. Honours T4-BG's "Pairs with" claim verbatim.
  - **Fix — tertiary (regression-lock test):** Verbatim stderr fixture from `behaviour-2026-05-25_01-10-21.ndjson` (the 4 cascading rejections) — assert `extract(...)` returns `DEFERRED` with one `missingPackage("javax.validation")` blocker, *not* `REFUSED_UNKNOWN`. Place in `BlockerExtractorTest` so the cascade can never silently reopen.
  - **Roadmap-entry corrections (do these in the same patch):**
    - **T4-BG entry:** strike-through the *"ledger records entries; javax.validation cascade ends"* phrasing in the description; replace with *"resolver-side WellKnownPackageRegistry shipped; classifier-side reclassification deferred to T1-ET (filed 2026-05-25)"*. Update the "Pairs with T4-BF" line to past-conditional: *"would pair with T4-BF when the classifier-side reclassification ships under T1-ET."*
    - **T4-BI entry:** add note *"`package-replace:*` rewrite path is unreachable for in-cycle javax imports until T1-ET Part A lands (the classifier blocks the mutation at extraction before the ledger or resolver run). T4-BI was correctly designed for the deferred-restage path but the deferred path is never entered for this diagnostic class. Verified zero `package-replace:*` events across runs 00:31 and 01:10 on 2026-05-25."*

  ### Part B — `promoteCurrentSubGoal` clobbers T1-DD's leaf re-point (T1-DD migration gap, exposed by the new pressure)

  - **Observed (2026-05-25 00:31 run, `behaviour-2026-05-25_00-31-18.ndjson`, 40 cycles):** From 00:44:08 to user-shutdown at 00:45:35 the system entered a tight loop on parent `goal-c1b6411c-3af3-410a-98eb-2abb20f6af94`. **16 consecutive cycles in 87 s** (~5 s each), each with `mut=null`, **zero `agent_selected` events**, `flags=[merged=false,promoted=true]`. Every cycle logged the identical four-line pattern: `T3-BL: all criteria banked for subGoalId=goal-c1b6411c... Applying FULFILLED early exit` → `applyGoalProgress: FULFILLED for currentSubGoalId=goal-c1b6411c... -> promoting branch` → `T1-DD: refusing to mark [goal-c1b6411c...] COMPLETED — 2 active descendants. Re-pointing currentSubGoalId to next active leaf goal-1b5ecc3f-65ca-4142-8ed5-34823b320984` → `T1-DB: recovered null currentSubGoalId — advancing to active subgoal [goal-c1b6411c-3af3-410a-98eb-2abb20f6af94]`.
  - **Origin (not a 05-24/05-25 introduction, but a 05-24/05-25 exposure):** T1-DD shipped 2026-04-30 (the WARN log line at line 1399 carries the ticket id). It added a refusal-and-re-point guard at the *write site* (`markGoalCompleted`) without migrating its *callers* (`promoteCurrentSubGoal`, `applyGoalProgress`) to consult the new outcome. The loop only fires under a specific shape — parent goal with banked criteria from child merges + T3-BL early-exit firing on the parent. The 00:31 run is the first long-form run *after* T4-BH/T4-BI shipped, and the new gate pressure (probe-time fragmentation reject + bundled pom+source rewrites for the javax cluster) accelerated the rate at which leaves accumulated banked criteria into the parent — which is what surfaced the latent T1-DD migration gap.
  - **Root cause (two cooperating defects, same invariant):**
    1. **`promoteCurrentSubGoal` ignores T1-DD's refusal.** Line 833 calls `markGoalCompleted(completedId)`. When T1-DD trips, `markGoalCompleted` silently early-returns after re-pointing `currentSubGoalId` to a safe active leaf (line 1407). `promoteCurrentSubGoal` does not know this happened — it continues to line 835 (`findNextSiblingOrAncestor(completedId)`) treating `completedId` as terminal, then line 876 (`currentSubGoalId = next`) unconditionally overwrites the leaf T1-DD just set. When `next` is null (no sibling, and `resolveNextActiveLeaf(rootGoalId)` returns null along this post-refresh path), `currentSubGoalId` is clobbered to null, and Neo4j is persisted with null via line 902. The next `getCurrentSubGoal()` call enters T1-DB's null-recovery, which picks `getRemainingGoals().get(0)` — for a `LinkedHashMap`-ordered values stream, that is **the ACTIVE parent itself, not one of its active leaf descendants**. So the pointer flips right back to `c1b6411c`, and the next cycle re-enters T3-BL on the same parent.
    2. **T3-BL fires on a non-leaf goal.** `CycleExecutor:96-133` early-exits with `applyGoalProgress(...FULFILLED...)` whenever `allCriteriaDefinedAndBanked(subGoalId) && mergeCount > 0`. A parent whose criteria are banked (via the children's merges accumulating up) and whose `mergeCount` is non-zero satisfies both predicates — even when it still has ACTIVE descendants. T1-DD downstream refuses the flip, but the early-exit has already committed to closing the cycle without running agents, so the loop spins doing nothing.
  - **Fix — primary (capability):** Change `markGoalCompleted(String id, String resolution)` from `void` to `MarkCompletedOutcome` (new nested record/enum with values `COMPLETED` / `REFUSED_ACTIVE_DESCENDANTS` / `UNKNOWN_GOAL`). T1-DD's early-return returns `REFUSED_ACTIVE_DESCENDANTS` with the re-pointed `currentSubGoalId` carried on the record. Migrate both call-sites:
    - `promoteCurrentSubGoal` (`GoalPlannerService.java:833`): capture the outcome. If `REFUSED_ACTIVE_DESCENDANTS`, **return early** — do not fall through to `findNextSiblingOrAncestor`, `resolveNextActiveLeaf`, the `currentSubGoalId = next` clobber, or `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied`. T1-DD already set the pointer and persisted; nothing more is needed.
    - `applyGoalProgress` non-current FULFILLED branch (`GoalPlannerService.java:2127`): replace the post-hoc status re-read at line 2131-2134 with the explicit outcome (the re-read is fragile and only logs; the outcome carries the truth directly).
    - All other internal callers of `markGoalCompleted` (line 1418 self-recursion, line 1643 inside `markGoalGivenUp` cascade, line 1307 inside `transitionGoal`): default-handle by ignoring the outcome (existing behaviour preserved) but compile-check each site is intentional.
  - **Fix — secondary (T3-BL guard symmetry with T1-DD):** In `CycleExecutor:99-103`, before the early-exit fires, add `&& goalPlannerService.hasNoActiveDescendants(earlyExitSubGoalId)`. A goal whose banked criteria came from child merges should not auto-exit while children are still ACTIVE — defer to ordinary cycle execution so the leaves get worked. New `public boolean hasNoActiveDescendants(String goalId)` on `GoalPlannerService` (~6 lines, mirrors the T1-DD descendant scan).
  - **Fix — tertiary (livelock invariant, defence-in-depth):** End-of-cycle invariant in `CycleExecutor` (next to the existing `assertGoalTreeIntegrity` call at line 219): if ≥3 consecutive cycles end with `mut=null && promoted=true && merged=false` AND `currentSubGoalId` was unchanged across them, log a structured `T1-ET: livelock-suspected (subGoalId=...,n=3)` WARN and emit a one-shot planner-priority signal. Should never trigger once primary+secondary land.

  - **MEASURED 2026-07-26 (user question: "is it possible to separate old graphs from the current graph?").** `purgeAll()` is **`MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n` — every node of every label**, not just goals. The narrow version (only `Goal` + `SystemState`) sits commented out directly above it with a TODO saying exactly that. It fires from `SystemResetConfig.resetSystemForce()`, reached at startup only when `autobuilder.service.reset-on-start=true`, and from the graph browser's manual Reset button.
    - **Consequence, and it answers the question asked:** old lineages are not "linked" to the current graph — they are **destroyed**. Live evidence: after a 4-run series the oldest node in the database was minted 112 ms after the lineage's own `run-identity.json` timestamp. Nothing older than the current lineage exists to be confused with it.
    - **SEQUENCING WARNING for anyone picking this up:** switching to the narrow purge so history SURVIVES must come **after** run-scoped reads (T4-CJ slice 2), never before. Today's unscoped reads (`OrchestrationSnapshotService` 14 queries, 0 run predicates, rendered into agent prompts) are survivable only because the wipe keeps the pool to one lineage. Keeping history first would make the noise strictly worse — every past lineage would join the pool those queries draw from.
  - **SHIPPED 2026-07-26 — reset no longer wipes the graph; old lineages survive as history (user decision: "sever lineage, keep history").** `SystemResetConfig.resetSystemForce()` no longer calls `purgeAll()`. The lineage is severed by `renewLineage()` (already present), the old nodes stay and are told apart by their ORIGIN `lineageId`, and the `SystemState` pointer is a singleton the re-seed overwrites — so nothing had to be deleted to start clean. `purgeAll()` stays on the interface as a deliberate wipe for test isolation and manual admin; it is simply no longer what "start fresh" means. The now-unused `GoalGraphService` dependency was removed from `SystemResetConfig` rather than left as residue.
    - **The sequencing warning recorded earlier proved real, and was paid before flipping the switch.** Keeping history makes previously-safe reads dangerous: `findAllDescriptions` and `findDescriptionsByStatus` feed `GoalSimilarityService`'s duplicate detection and the GIVEN_UP unachievable guard, so an unscoped version would let a PREVIOUS lineage's goals reject or block a fresh one's subgoals. Both are now `lineageId`-scoped against the ON CREATE origin stamp. This is why "scope the reads first" was not bureaucratic ordering.
    - **Attribution completed first** so every node can be told apart: `Neo4jScoreHistoryService` (FileScore, GlobalScore, the `%s` score-event labels — which is why `GoalEvaluation`/`GoalAcceptance` never showed up in a label grep — plus its link-created Goal and Cycle), `SmsCycleIngestor`'s Cycle link, and `Neo4jMergeGraphService`'s Cycle link all stamp `lineageId` + `runId` now.
    - **Growth is a watch, not a subsystem** (measured, per the deliberate choice not to build on speculation): one 4-run lineage was ~9,600 nodes, so a hundred lineages is ~1M — comfortable for Neo4j. Revisit if a single database passes a few million nodes or query latency shows up in run telemetry.
    - **FIELD-VERIFIED 2026-07-26 (run `2026-07-26_19-58-56`), and the verification caught a real defect first.**
      - **Method:** seeded a synthetic prior lineage (`lineage-OLD-0001`: a root goal, a GIVEN_UP subgoal, a planner action) into the graph, then booted a run — whose startup reset is exactly the operation that used to delete it.
      - **T1-D proven:** the log shows `Autobuilder system reset triggered` → `T4-CJ: lineage severed by reset — new lineageId=lineage-b21345d4…` → `Goal stack reset with root goal`, and **all 3 prior-lineage nodes survived**. Two lineages coexist (new run 124 nodes, prior 3) where the old code left zero.
      - **Isolation proven with the counterfactual measured beside it:** goal dedup sees **8 goals, 0 from the prior lineage** (unscoped it would see 9, with 1 leaking in); the GIVEN_UP guard sees **0** (unscoped: **1** — the prior lineage's abandoned subgoal). That second one is the predicted regression: an abandoned goal from a dead lineage entering the unachievable guard and blocking a similar fresh subgoal.
      - **DEFECT CAUGHT BY THE RUN — `GoalPlannerService.syncFromGraph()` loads `goalGraphService.findAll()`, which was UNSCOPED.** With the wipe gone it loaded another lineage's goals at boot and threw `UnsupportedOperationException` from `@PostConstruct` (`ensureAttemptIdsFor` mutating a goal whose metadata deserialised immutable) — **the whole application failed to start**. I had classified `findAll()` as harmless "global" in the read audit; it is the single most load-bearing cross-lineage read there is. Now `lineageId`-scoped (all three consumers are goal-domain logic meaning "this run's tree"; the browser reads history through `OrchestrationGraphExplorerService`, deliberately unscoped). The immutable-metadata path was hardened separately so one odd goal can never again cost a boot.
      - **Honest note on a premature claim:** after the FIRST (failed) boot I read "3 prior nodes still present" as T1-D working. It was not — the crash happened before the reset ran, so nothing had tried to delete them. Only the second run, with reset markers in the log, is evidence.
      - **Held for a full run:** 55 cycles, `PREFLIGHT: PASS`, terminal=deadline. End state 1383 nodes in the new lineage, the prior 3 untouched. `smoke=boot-failed` is a target-quality outcome on a 25-minute cap, not a framework result.
      - **T6-F's reconstruction path fired end-to-end for the first time:** `preserved_source=reconstructed:cycle-1785090237357` with the new wording (`no usable loop-preserved copy (terminal=deadline, copy=absent) — reconstructing from THIS run's snapshots`). The `t6f-stale-loop-copy-ignored` watch stays open — this run had no INHERITED copy to ignore (fresh `meta/`), so the stale-copy branch is still unexercised in the field.
      - **Suite 2126/0 after the two field-caught fixes.**
      - **SECOND FIELD GAP, found by the user looking at the browser: 787 of 2170 nodes (36%) carried NO lineage stamp** — `Relation` 366, `Artifact` 257, `Interpretation` 109, `Episode` 55 — in a run made AFTER the attribution work. My "attribution completed at 4 write sites" claim was wrong: those nodes are written by the **`com.walpro:semantic-memory-substrate` dependency**, not by any Cypher in this repo, which is why a write-site sweep could never find them. Fixed where this repo can reach it — `SmsCycleIngestor` stamps the episode and everything within two hops right after `b.commit()` (measured shape: `Episode -[LINKS_TO]-> Relation -> Artifact/Interpretation` accounts for 100% of them), with `WHERE x.lineageId IS NULL` so it fills gaps and can never re-stamp another lineage's node. Existing rows backfilled; the database now reports **zero** unstamped nodes. **Lesson: "every node is attributable" cannot be established by auditing this repo's write sites alone when a dependency writes into the same database.**

- [x] **T1-BD: REPLAN mode blocks evolution indefinitely** (`DeliberationExecutionGate`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 session):** `DeliberationExecutionGate.allowedRoles(REPLAN)` returns `Set.of("planner", "analysis")`. Evolution is completely excluded. There is no time limit, grace period, or fallback. Once REPLAN_REQUESTED fires and deliberation returns REPLAN, evolution never runs again until the signal decays — which it doesn't (see T1-BE). Observed: cycles 3–11 in the 00:42 session all ran in REPLAN mode; evolution was logged as `"Meta step skipped: DeliberationMode=REPLAN blocks role=evolution"` every cycle. Four subgoals were given up without a single evolution attempt.
  - **Fix:** Add `"evolution"` to the REPLAN allowed-roles set in `DeliberationExecutionGate`. REPLAN's intent is "run the planner first to get a better plan" — not "freeze all forward progress". The planner ranks highest via ROLE_PLANNER signal and executes first. Evolution then runs on whatever active subgoal remains. If the planner removed the current subgoal, evolution has nothing to work on and is naturally a no-op. This is the minimal, lowest-risk fix and does not change planner-first ordering.
  - **Change:** `DeliberationExecutionGate.java`: `REPLAN -> Set.of("planner", "analysis", "evolution")`.
  - **Depends on:** T1-BE (REPLAN_REQUESTED must decay naturally, otherwise evolution still can't break the lock on its own).

- [x] **T1-BE: REPLAN_REQUESTED perpetual reinforcement prevents signal decay** (`AutobuilderService`, `Signal`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 session):** `AutobuilderService` emits `REPLAN_REQUESTED(1.0, decay=0.05)` on every SUBGOAL_EXHAUSTED and STAGNATING result. `Signal.reinforce()` accumulates strength (`1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0 → 3.0 → …`) and takes `Math.min(decayPerCycle, other.decayPerCycle)`, locking the decay to the slowest emitter (0.05). At decay=0.05, the signal would need 20 uninterrupted cycles to die — but it is re-emitted every cycle stagnation continues, resetting the age clock and growing strength. In the 00:42 session, REPLAN_REQUESTED was still alive at cycle 11, never having decayed.
  - **Fix A — raise decay:** Change `Signal.of(BasicSignals.REPLAN_REQUESTED, 1.0, 0.05, "exhaustion-recovery")` and the stagnation-recovery emission to `decay=0.20`. This reduces the decay horizon from 20 cycles to 5 cycles, giving a natural expiry window.
  - **Fix B — conditional re-emission:** Before emitting, check `context.hasStrongSignal(REPLAN_REQUESTED, 0.50)`. If already strong, skip re-emission and let the existing signal decay. Only emit a fresh signal when the prior one has weakened. This prevents strength accumulation.
  - **Recommended:** Apply both. Fix A prevents slow decay; Fix B prevents accumulation on fast cycles.
  - **Changes:** `AutobuilderService.java` lines 200–207 (SUBGOAL_EXHAUSTED) and 240–242 (STAGNATING): raise decay to 0.20 and add conditional-re-emission guard.

- [x] **T1-BH: False GOAL_FULFILLED when planner exhausts all subgoals** (`CycleExecutor.deriveCycleResult`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 log analysis):** `deriveCycleResult` had a secondary GOAL_FULFILLED path: `(leafCompletedNow || goalProgress == PROGRESSING) && mutationState == ACCEPTED && remainingGoals.isEmpty()`. `remainingGoals` is populated from `GoalPlannerService.getRemainingGoals()` (ACTIVE subgoals only). When the planner gave up all remaining subgoals via GIVEN_UP (leaving no ACTIVE ones), `remainingGoals` became empty. Combined with ACCEPTED+PROGRESSING from a concurrent evolution cycle, the `PROGRESSING` branch of the OR fired GOAL_FULFILLED — even though the root goal was still ACTIVE and no subgoal was actually completed.
  - **Fix:** Removed the `goalProgress == PROGRESSING` branch entirely (PROGRESSING is not a completion signal). The `leafCompletedNow` path is guarded with an explicit root goal status check: only returns GOAL_FULFILLED when `root.getStatus() == COMPLETED`. The `rootAutoCompleted()` path (line above) remains the primary completion detection mechanism.
  - **Regression tests:** `runCycle_T1BH_regression_progressingAcceptedWithAllSubgoalsGivenUp_doesNotProduceFalseGoalFulfilled` and `runCycle_T1BH_leafCompletedNow_withRootCompleted_setsCycleResultGoalFulfilled`.

- [x] **T1-BJ: Planner shallow decomposition — FULL_COVERAGE_REQUIRED rule** (`PlannerProtocolContract`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 session):** The planner was given a root goal specifying 10 endpoints across 3 resource types (Books, Members, Loans). Its first `#SubGoalAppend` covered only 2 endpoints (POST /books, GET /books). After those completed, it was re-invoked via `planInto` and attempted to re-add GET /books (duplicate-blocked), causing the root to auto-complete with 8 endpoints unimplemented. Existing rule `GOAL_DERIVED_SUBGOALS` says subgoals must be traceable to the root goal but does not require covering all stated requirements.
  - **Fix A — new protocol rule:** Add `FULL_COVERAGE_REQUIRED` to `PlannerProtocolContract.rules()`: "When the root goal lists N distinct named endpoints or features, your FIRST planning response MUST produce one subgoal per endpoint/feature. Do not submit a partial list expecting to add the rest later — the system considers the backlog done once the first batch completes. Count them explicitly before responding."
  - **Fix B — rewrite the "no active subgoal" NOTE block:** The NOTE at the bottom of `getUserPrompt()` (shown when `currentSubGoalDescription == null`) currently says "If the root goal is fulfilled, respond with: Message: Goal complete. Otherwise, use #SubGoalAppend." Replace with: "Before responding, enumerate every named endpoint and feature in the root goal spec. Compare against completed goals. If ALL are covered → Message: Goal complete. If ANY are missing → #SubGoalAppend them now. Do NOT say 'Goal complete' while any endpoint or feature from the root goal spec lacks a completed subgoal."
  - **Changes:** `PlannerProtocolContract.java` — add rule entry + rewrite NOTE block (~15 lines).
  - **Observed:** 2026-04-09 session (10-endpoint goal, only 2 subgoals planned, root marked complete with 2/10 done).

- [x] **T1-BK: Root auto-completion fires when `planInto` was blocked by deduplication** (`GoalPlannerService`, `PlannerAgent`, `PlanningCallback`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 session):** `promoteCurrentSubGoal()` calls `planningCallback.planInto()` then unconditionally calls `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied()`. In the session, `planInto` proposed "Implement GET /books [2 merges]" — blocked by `GoalSimilarityService` as a near-duplicate of the already-completed "Implement GET /books". Zero subgoals were injected. `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied` saw all descendants COMPLETED → marked root COMPLETED. The system had no way to distinguish "planner said done" from "planner tried to inject work but was blocked."
  - **Fix:** Change `PlanningCallback` from `void planInto(...)` to `int planInto(...)` returning the count of successfully injected subgoals. In `PlannerAgent.planInto()`, return the count from the injection loop. In `GoalPlannerService.promoteCurrentSubGoal()`, capture the return value: if `planInto` was called AND returned 0 (no new subgoals injected, but the planner did attempt injection), skip `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied` and instead raise `REPLAN_REQUESTED` via the stored `currentCycleContext`. This surfaces as a new planning opportunity next cycle rather than a silent false completion.
  - **Edge case:** If `planInto` was not called at all (no `shouldTriggerPlanner` condition met), `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied` still runs as before — this covers the legitimate "planner already ran and there's genuinely nothing left" case.
  - **Changes:** `PlanningCallback.java` (return type), `PlannerAgent.planInto()` (return count), `GoalPlannerService.promoteCurrentSubGoal()` (~5 lines around the `planningCallback.planInto()` call).
  - **Observed:** 2026-04-09 session (root marked COMPLETED after planner produced 0 injected / 1 deduped subgoal under root).

- [>] **T1-BL: T2-BM veto must use criteria progress gate** (`EvaluationAgent`)
  - **Withdrawn (2026-04-10):** This was a workaround for T2-BM's side effects. The correct fix is to remove T2-BM entirely (see T1-BN). With T2-BM gone, partial-progress mutations are accepted naturally and T1-BL is not needed.
  - **Original analysis preserved for reference:** T2-BM forces REJECTED on any ✗ criterion without consulting `cumulativeCriteriaStatus`. For multi-file criteria, this creates a permanent block where alternating `[1] ✓/[2] ✗` and `[1] ✗/[2] ✓` cycles each get rejected, code never accumulates, and the subgoal exhausts. Observed 2026-04-10: `goal-649cb581` (POST /members email uniqueness) stuck for 12+ cycles.

- [>] **T1-BM: `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic` — all-criteria-cumulatively-met fast path** (`SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic`)
  - **Withdrawn (2026-04-10):** This was needed to work around the STAGNATING deadlock caused by T2-BM's repeated rejections driving the LLM to report `goalProgress = STAGNATING`. With T2-BM removed (T1-BN), partial mutations are accepted, the LLM sees forward progress, and `goalProgress = PROGRESSING` — so the existing fulfillment path works without modification.

- [x] **T1-BN: Remove T2-BM hard veto — it is now superseded by T1-BG + T3-BA** (`EvaluationAgent`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-10 analysis):** T2-BM was introduced (2026-04-09) before T1-BG existed, to prevent a specific bug: evaluator outputs ACCEPTED with a ✗ criterion → broken code merged → subgoal closed as FULFILLED. At the time, T3-BA only blocked *subgoal closure* (via `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic`), not *mutation acceptance*; unmet criteria had no binding effect on the merge decision.
  - **Why T2-BM is now redundant:** T1-BG's `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` map tracks which criteria have ever passed. `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic.hasUnmetCriterion()` uses this map to gate FULFILLED: a subgoal cannot close until all criteria are cumulatively `true`. The original T2-BM bug — premature FULFILLED with broken code — is now prevented by T3-BA+T1-BG without T2-BM.
  - **Why T2-BM is now harmful:** The 2026-04-10 session showed it creates a deadlock for multi-file criteria (e.g. "add method to MemberService AND have MemberController call it"). No single-file mutation can satisfy both simultaneously. T2-BM rejects every partial mutation; code never accumulates; the subgoal exhausts. T1-BL and T1-BM were proposed as workarounds — but the right fix is to remove the root cause.
  - **What to do:**
    1. In `EvaluationAgent.java`: delete the T2-BM hard-veto block (the `anyFailed → force mutationState = REJECTED, vetoed = true` block, ~lines 148–158). Keep `criteriaAssessments` parsing, cumulative merge, and `lastCriteriaPassCount` update — those belong to T1-BG, not T2-BM. Remove the `vetoed` flag from `EvaluationAgent` and its callsite in `HeuristicNegotiator.negotiate(...)` if it is no longer needed.
    2. In the roadmap: annotate T2-BM as superseded (see below).
    3. Mark T1-BL and T1-BM as `[>]` withdrawn (already done above).
    4. T2-BN (surface banked criteria in evolution prompt) remains a valid steering improvement independent of T2-BM removal — re-evaluate after T1-BN ships.
  - **Risk and mitigation:** A mutation with a genuinely broken ✗ criterion (e.g. evolution deleted a feature) can now be merged. This is acceptable: T3-BA keeps the subgoal open (cumulative criterion stays `false`), and the next evolution cycle corrects it. The output directory may temporarily contain incomplete code, but that is by design — it is the accumulated partial state that the system converges from.
  - **Run tests:** `mvn test` after removal to confirm no regressions.

- [x] **T1-BG: Cumulative per-criterion pass tracking** (`CycleContextData`, `EvaluationAgent`, `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic`, `CycleContextCoordinator`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 analysis):** `criteriaAssessments` on `CycleContextData` is a fresh snapshot per evaluation cycle. `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic.hasUnmetCriterion()` vetoes FULFILLED whenever *any* criterion in the **current cycle's** assessment has `✗` — including criteria not addressed by this mutation (because evolution only tackles a subset of criteria per cycle). A subgoal with 4 criteria that individually take one cycle each to satisfy will never fulfill: each cycle's snapshot shows at least one `✗`, so the veto fires indefinitely. ACCEPTED merges accumulate but the subgoal never advances — it eventually exhausts and gets GIVEN_UP.
  - **Fix:**
    1. Add `Map<Integer, Boolean> cumulativeCriteriaStatus` to `CycleContextData` (index → passed, serialised in snapshot). A criterion index maps to `true` once it has passed; it never reverts to `false` (a criterion that passed is considered satisfied for the lifetime of the subgoal).
    2. In `EvaluationAgent`, after parsing `criteriaAssessments`, merge each `[N] ✓` into `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` as `true`. A `[N] ✗` only sets `false` if the index was not already `true`. Omitted indices (LLM partial compliance) are left at their prior value.
    3. In `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic.hasUnmetCriterion()`, consult `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` when it is non-null. A criterion is "unmet" if its index is absent from the map or maps to `false`. A criterion maps to `true` if it has ever passed, regardless of this cycle's assessment.
    4. In `CycleContextCoordinator.prepareRuntimeContext()`, reset `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` to `null` when `currentSubGoalId` changes — fresh start for each new subgoal.
  - **Result:** a subgoal is fulfilled when all its criteria have been satisfied across any set of cycles, not in a single snapshot.
  - **Depends on:** T3-AZ/T3-BC (source of machine-readable criterion assessments). T3-BI (graph persistence so this survives restart).
  - **Enables:** T2-BL (exhaustion suppression while criteria are progressing), T3-BJ (snapshot surface).

- [x] **T1-BF: Cascade GIVEN_UP wipes goals with successful merges** (`GoalPlannerService`, `GoalEntity`, `MergeAgent`)
  - **Root cause (2026-04-09 session):** `GoalPlannerService.markGoalGivenUp()` calls `collectActiveDescendants()` which returns all ACTIVE descendants unconditionally. Every child is marked GIVEN_UP regardless of whether it had prior successful merges. No merge history is stored on `GoalEntity`.
  - **Observed failure:** When `goal-4576d23a` (Refactor BookController) was given up after 1 cycle with no merge, its sibling-injected child `goal-98634b9c` was immediately cascade-given-up (`00:43:17.521: "markGoalGivenUp cascade"`), despite having later produced a merge in cycle 4. The parent/child topology meant the cascade reached it.
  - **Fix A — merge history on GoalEntity:** Add `int mergeCount` field to `GoalEntity` (persisted under metadata key `"mergeCount"`). Increment via `GoalPlannerService.incrementGoalMergeCount(goalId)`, called from `MergeAgent` after each accepted merge. Load from metadata in `Neo4jGoalGraphService`.
  - **Fix B — protect goals with merges from cascade:** In `collectActiveDescendants()`, skip descendants where `mergeCount > 0`. Goals that produced real output should not be silently wiped; let them exhaust naturally through the normal exhaustion counter.
  - **Note:** Fix A (merge tracking) is also the infrastructure for T2-BI (planner prompt enrichment). Implement T2-BI first or together.
  - **Changes:** `GoalEntity.java` (add field), `GoalPlannerService.java` (incrementMergeCount + cascade guard), `MergeAgent.java` (call incrementMergeCount), `Neo4jGoalGraphService.java` (persist/load via metadata).

- [x] **T1-BC: Evolution package coherence** (`EvolutionProtocolContract`, `CycleContextCoordinator`, `DefaultProjectStructureSummarizer`)
  - **Observed (2026-04-06 session):** Evolution generated files in `com.example.demo` early in the session, then switched to `com.example.library` in later cycles. Both packages coexist in the merged output — Spring component scan cannot reach both, imports across packages won't resolve. The output is structurally broken Java.
  - **Root cause:** The evolution prompt has no constraint on the output package namespace. The LLM picks a package freely per cycle with no awareness of what's already in `output/`.
  - **Fix:** `DefaultProjectStructureSummarizer.detectBasePackage(Path)` walks `.java` files and returns the common package prefix (null when output is empty). `CycleContextCoordinator` calls it each cycle and stores result in `CycleContextData.establishedBasePackage`. `EvolutionProtocolContract` injects a `--- PACKAGE CONSTRAINT ---` block when non-null, locking all generated files to that base package or a sub-package of it.

- [x] **T1-G: Deliberation fallback when evaluation is infeasible post-merge** (`RuleBasedDeliberationProposer`, `ContextLineageTracker`)
  - Root bug: `lastEvaluatedEvolutionFingerprint` was not carried between cycles in `ContextLineageTracker`.
    Reset to null each cycle → `notYetEvaluated=true` every cycle after any evolution, even post-merge.
    Combined with decaying `EVOLUTION_OCCURRED` (~10 cycles) + `REPLAN_REQUESTED >= 0.50` → T1-G safety
    net fired every post-merge cycle → planner ran repeatedly → goal explosion.
  - Fix A (`ContextLineageTracker`): carry `lastEvaluatedEvolutionFingerprint` from previous context,
    same as `lastEvolutionFingerprint` is already carried. After a successful evaluation+merge, fingerprints
    match across cycles → `notYetEvaluated=false` → EVALUATE/T1-G branch correctly skipped.
  - Fix B (`RuleBasedDeliberationProposer`): T1-G safety net retained — when `projectDiff=null` (diff
    consumed or lost) and `REPLAN_REQUESTED >= 0.50`, fall back to REPLAN instead of silent EVALUATE.
    Now only fires when fingerprints genuinely diverge (true unevaluated pending mutation with no diff).

  - Planner and Evolution had a dead `metaRequest()` helper reading `dr.meta().get("metaRequest")` — a key never set anywhere

- [x] **T1-L: Reinforce `ROLE_EVALUATION` when unevaluated mutation is present** (`RuleBasedDeliberationProposer`)
  - **Root cause (live log 2026-03-09):** After evolution, `ROLE_EVALUATION` decays below the `canExecute`
    threshold (0.10) within 3–4 no-op cycles before evaluation runs. Deadlock: mode=EVALUATE but agent
    cannot execute; meta returns `Stop: true` every cycle; mutation stays uneval'd/unmerged forever.
  - Fix: in the `hasCandidate && notYetEvaluated` branch, add `ROLE_EVALUATION` at strength 0.5 to
    `proposedSignals`. Applied every cycle via the existing `applyProposedSignals` path in
    `AdaptiveExecutionEngine`, guaranteeing evaluation is reachable regardless of decay timing.

- [x] **T1-M: `PLANNING_THROTTLED` never releases in a fresh environment** (`PlanningThrashSignalAnalyzer`)
  - **Root cause (live log 2026-03-09 / deep analysis):** The release condition required BOTH
    `currentInflow <= inflowRelease` AND `currentRatio <= ratioRelease`. In a fresh environment all
    baseline windows are empty → `inflowRelease` clamps to 2. Inflow is an absolute count (4 goals
    added) that never decreases → `4 <= 2` is permanently false → throttle never releases even after
    all 4 goals complete. `planInto()` callback sees the stale throttle, makes the LLM call, then
    returns early without injecting the proposed subgoal. Root goal is immediately marked complete.
  - Fix: added `caughtUp` release condition: if `currentOutflow > 0 && currentRatio <= 1.0`,
    release the throttle. This handles the case where all injected goals have been worked through,
    regardless of absolute inflow count or baseline history.
  - Stagnation case covered by T1-O: GIVEN_UP goals now count toward outflow → `caughtUp` fires correctly.

- [x] **T1-N: Deduplication rework — remove keyword narrowing, restore GIVEN_UP candidates, surface GIVEN_UP to LLM** (`GoalSimilarityService`, `Neo4jGoalGraphService`, `PlannerProtocolContract`)
  - **Fix A — remove keyword narrowing (T1-H/B rework):** Drop `extractKeywords()`, the `STOP_WORDS`
    set, and the `CONTAINS` clause from `findDescriptionCandidates` entirely. Return all goals
    regardless of status (single query, no text filter, limit 200). Run Monge-Elkan against the
    full set. Simple and correct; eliminates stop-word brittleness and keyword mismatch false negatives.
  - **Fix B — restore GIVEN_UP in dedup candidates (revert T1-H/D):** Remove the `<> 'GIVEN_UP'`
    filter. All statuses participate so truly identical re-proposals of failed goals remain blocked.
  - **Fix C — surface GIVEN_UP goals in planner prompt:** Add an "Abandoned Goals" block to
    `PlannerProtocolContract.getUserPrompt()` (after Completed Goals) listing GIVEN_UP goal
    descriptions. Add a protocol rule: "Do not re-propose abandoned goals verbatim."

- [x] **T1-O: `PLANNING_THROTTLED` stuck in stagnation — GIVEN_UP goals not counted as outflow** (`PlanningThrashSignalAnalyzer`)
  - **Root cause (live log 2026-03-09):** `countCompletedSince()` only counts `GoalStatus.COMPLETED`.
    Goals that exhaust without completing (→ GIVEN_UP) are invisible to the outflow counter.
    In stagnation, `outflow` stays 0 indefinitely → T1-M's `caughtUp` release never fires.
  - Fix A: added `Instant givenUp` field to `GoalEntity`, set in `markGivenUp()`, persisted to Neo4j via `save()`, read back in `mapRowToGoalEntity()`.
  - Fix B: replaced `completedInstant()` helper with `resolvedInstant()` in `PlanningThrashSignalAnalyzer` — returns `completed` for COMPLETED, `givenUp` for GIVEN_UP, null otherwise. Both count methods now use it.

- [x] **T1-Q: GIVEN_UP cascade — orphaned active children** (`GoalPlannerService`, `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied`)
  - `markGoalGivenUp()` only updated the single target node; children remained ACTIVE, becoming unreachable
    (resolveNextActiveLeaf skips non-ACTIVE parents so can never descend into them)
  - Fix A: `collectActiveDescendants()` recursively finds all ACTIVE descendants regardless of intermediate
    node status; `markGoalGivenUp()` marks each one GIVEN_UP and saves to graph, then does a single `persist()`
  - Fix B: `autoCompleteRootIfSatisfied()` now counts GIVEN_UP alongside COMPLETED for root auto-completion

- [x] **T1-U: LOW_CONFIDENCE over-emission** (`EvaluationAgent`, `PatternSignalAnalyzer`)
  - Two emitters were too aggressive:
  - **`EvaluationAgent`**: fires at strength 1.0 / decay 0.05 whenever `score < 0.75 || STAGNATING`.
    Scores of 0.70–0.74 triggered it every cycle; `withSignal` reinforces on each subsequent cycle → `LOW_CONFIDENCE=7.60` seen in live log.
  - **`PatternSignalAnalyzer.applyFocusDrift`**: fires when diff doesn't touch ANY path referenced by
    open problems — too sensitive with many open problems.
  - Fix: graduated emission by score distance; raised decay rate; tightened `applyFocusDrift` to require majority-miss.

- [x] **T1-V: Dynamic refinement nesting control** (`PlannerAgent`, `GoalPlannerService`)
  - Removed `createRefinementSubgoal()`, `shouldAutoRefine()`, `chooseRefinementTarget()` entirely.
    Stagnation is already handled by `AutobuilderService`; the auto-refinement added no context and was
    the direct cause of "Refine goal: Refine goal: ..." chains.
  - Also fixed the root re-entrancy bug: `applyGoalProgress(GIVEN_UP)` never advanced `currentSubGoalId`,
    so GIVEN_UP goals kept re-entering the cycle as the active subgoal and exhausting repeatedly.
    Fix: after `markGoalGivenUp()`, if the given-up goal was current, advance via
    `findNextSiblingOrAncestor` → `resolveNextActiveLeaf` fallback (mirrors the FULFILLED path).

- [x] **T1-Y: Fingerprint guard bypassed when stagnating** (`ExecutionEligibilityExplainer`)
