- [x] **T1-FO: `Neo4jDeferredMutationGraphService.ensureSchema()` mixes schema DDL + data DML in one transaction — crashes `@PostConstruct` on a fresh Neo4j** (`graph/mutation/Neo4jDeferredMutationGraphService.java:55-97`) — **filed 2026-07-17, surfaced by the T4-CL verification battery; PROVEN pre-existing (A/B: the pre-T4-CJ file version from `59e5549` fails identically), independent of any 2026-07-17 work.**
  - **Defect:** `ensureSchema()` runs three `CREATE CONSTRAINT/INDEX ... IF NOT EXISTS` statements then a sentinel `MERGE` (the T5-AD preheat write), and they share one transaction, which Neo4j forbids (`Neo.ClientError.Transaction.ForbiddenDueToTransactionType: Tried to execute Write query after executing Schema modification`). It only throws when the `CREATE CONSTRAINT` is a REAL schema modification — i.e. on a database where the constraint does not already exist. Warm databases (production; a reused Testcontainers container that has ever committed the constraint) no-op the DDL so the write proceeds and the bug stays invisible — which is why it went months unseen. **Consequence: a first-ever boot against a brand-new Neo4j (including production's first startup) would throw here and fail context init.** The failed transaction rolls back the constraint too, so a fresh container stays fresh and re-fails deterministically once triggered.
  - **Fix direction:** run the schema DDL and the sentinel DML in SEPARATE transactions (DDL first, committed, then the preheat write) — the sentinel only registers property keys and can safely run after schema settles. Verify against a genuinely fresh Neo4j (drop the constraints on the test container first, or a throwaway db) since a warm db masks the bug. Tier T1: a real correctness defect (startup crash), not a policy tune.
  - **DoD:** `Neo4jDeferredMutationGraphServiceIT.postConstructInvocationIsIdempotent` passes against a FRESH-schema database; `ensureSchema` is idempotent on both fresh and warm databases; suite green.
  - **DONE 2026-07-23 (Opus 4.8).** `ensureSchema()` now runs each schema DDL statement and the sentinel write/delete through the injected Neo4j `Driver` in its own auto-commit transaction (new private `runInOwnTransaction(cypher)`), so schema modification and data write can never share a transaction regardless of any ambient Spring transaction. Root cause confirmed empirically at decision time: the class-level `@Transactional` CGLIB proxy wraps the whole method in ONE Neo4j transaction — the failing pre-fix run's stack was `Neo4jDeferredMutationGraphService$$SpringCGLIB$$0.ensureSchema` throwing `Neo.ClientError.Transaction.ForbiddenDueToTransactionType` at the sentinel MERGE — so on a fresh DB (real `CREATE CONSTRAINT` schema change) the following write is rejected; a warm DB no-ops the DDL and masks it. **Regression-catching test proven both ways** ([[feedback-verify-diff-is-substantive]]): the IT's `postConstructInvocationIsIdempotent` now drops the ledger schema first (new `dropDeferredMutationSchema()`) to force the fresh path — it FAILS on the pre-fix file (reproduces the exact error, verified by stashing the fix) and PASSES on the fixed file. **Verified:** IT 4/4 (fresh + warm + idempotent double-invoke); full unit suite 2121 run / 0 failures / 0 errors / 2 skipped. Added a `Driver` constructor dependency — no manual instantiations exist (Spring-injected only). Deviation from the filed "Fix direction": it suggested SEPARATE `neo4jClient` transactions, but under an ambient `@Transactional` proxy `neo4jClient` still joins the bound transaction, so the fix uses the driver directly to guarantee independence by construction. Committed to main as `32c09af` (2026-07-23). Note: suite was run against a scratch `FILE_BASE_PATH` to avoid rotating the concurrent live run's logs ([[project-tests-rotate-live-logs]]).

    | **survive** | **647** | **exception types, services, repositories — all project-owned** |

- [x] **T1-FP: `LLMClient` read timeout is fixed per attempt — a slow-but-progressing local generation times out identically on every retry, tripping the circuit breaker into an endless pause instead of ever completing** (`client/LLMClient.java` — `init()` fixed-timeout factory + the `ask()` retry loop) — **filed 2026-07-23, from the "runs don't end" investigation ([[project-resume-state]] / [[project-run-lifecycle-runbook]]).**
  - **Observed:** the 2026-07-23 dev-auto run paused on the LLM circuit breaker after repeated `Read timed out` (SocketTimeoutException) on `POST localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions` (qwen3-coder:30b), 120s per attempt. The loop entered `SYSTEM_PAUSED` and never reached a natural terminal (GOAL_FULFILLED/EXHAUSTED) — the "runs don't seem to end" symptom the user flagged. The model itself was healthy (0.2s small-prompt round-trip); the timeouts are real large-prompt / cold-reload generations exceeding 120s under host load, [[project-local-first-constraint]].
  - **Root cause:** the read timeout (`llm.api.read-timeout-ms`, default 120000) is set ONCE in `@PostConstruct init()` on a single reused `RestTemplate` (`SimpleClientHttpRequestFactory.setReadTimeout`), so EVERY retry attempt gets the same 120s. T1-FD escalates the retry BACKOFF DELAY (`retryBackoffMs` — base doubled per attempt, capped 60s) but NOT the timeout, so a generation needing >120s times out identically on all `retryMaxAttempts` attempts; the escalation only spaces the doomed tries before the breaker opens.
  - **Interaction to respect (do NOT regress T1-FD):** when the client-side read timeout fires, Ollama keeps computing the abandoned generation server-side, so an immediate retry stacks fresh load on the backlog. The escalating backoff exists for exactly that and stays. An escalating timeout must not reintroduce request-stacking — a later, longer-timeout attempt still waits out the backoff first; the goal is to give a LATER attempt more time to finish, not to fire sooner.
  - **Fix direction:** make the per-attempt read timeout escalate — base `read-timeout-ms` grown per attempt up to a cap, expressed RELATIVE to the base, never a second fixed constant ([[feedback-relative-thresholds]]) — so a slow-but-progressing generation gets a genuine chance to complete on a later attempt. Needs a per-request timeout instead of the shared-factory one (rebuild the request factory per attempt, or a request-level timeout). New config: an escalation factor + cap that DEFAULTS to reproduce today's flat-120s behaviour (factor 1) so the change is opt-in and behaviour-preserving until tuned.
  - **DoD:** an escalation function (same testable shape as `retryBackoffMs`) grows the read timeout across attempts under a cap; a unit test proves a generation that exceeds the base timeout but completes under the escalated one succeeds instead of tripping the breaker (injected slow factory / controllable endpoint); backoff-before-retry preserved; default config reproduces the current 120s-flat behaviour with escalation disabled; suite green.
  - **DONE 2026-07-23 (Opus 4.8), committed to main as `f748f85`.** `LLMClient.readTimeoutForAttempt(baseMs, factor, attempt, capMs)` = `base * factor^(attempt-1)`, clamped to `capMs` (0 = uncapped), never below base; `factor <= 1.0` (the code `@Value` default) reproduces the flat base timeout, so escalation is opt-in and behaviour-preserving. `clientForTimeout(ms)` reuses the shared base `RestTemplate` and builds a per-request client only when the timeout is escalated (a local, so concurrent callers never mutate shared state); wired into the `ask()` retry loop, and the timeout-error log now reports the per-attempt timeout for observability. **T1-FD preserved:** escalation gives a LATER attempt more time; the backoff still spaces attempts, so a wedged endpoint still opens the breaker on attempt COUNT rather than re-stacking load onto an abandoned generation. **Config (this deployment, `application.yml`):** `read-timeout-escalation-factor: 1.5` + `read-timeout-max-ms: 300000` → 120s / 180s / 270s across 3 attempts. **Tests** ([[feedback-verify-diff-is-substantive]]): escalation-math unit test (flat at factor 1.0, 1.5^n growth, cap clamp, never-below-base) + a real `com.sun.net.httpserver` slow-server test proving a 900ms response the 400ms base abandons is rescued by the escalated attempt-2 timeout (regression-catching by construction — without the escalation logic all attempts use the base and time out). `LLMClientTest` 15/15; full unit suite 2123 run / 0 failures / 0 errors / 2 skipped (scratch `FILE_BASE_PATH`, no live-log rotation). **Origin:** the capped run analysed this session hit the 120s ceiling 5× under host load (loadavg ~15) without tripping the breaker; the prior dev-auto run DID trip it and parked in `SYSTEM_PAUSED` — the "runs don't end" symptom the user flagged. This addresses the timeout ceiling; it does not change the local model's speed ([[project-local-first-constraint]]).

- [x] **T1-FL: A breaker-caused pause is permanent although the breaker is timed — the loop cannot survive a transient model outage** (`AutobuilderService.runAutobuilderCycleLocked` breaker-pause site vs `LlmCircuitBreaker` T1-FD timed opens) — **filed 2026-07-16 from the 19:12 preflight run (corpus `/tmp/preflight_runs/2026-07-16_19-12-13`), first run KILLED by primary-provider failure (the T4-AS trigger condition, now observed).**
  - **Observed:** the local model (ollama) stopped answering 19:15→~19:52 (host under load; runner unloaded). 5 consecutive read timeouts → `LlmCircuitBreaker` OPEN **(timed, 60s)** → `AutobuilderService` set `pausedReason("llm-circuit-breaker")` and the skip branch then short-circuited every future tick. The breaker's cooldown elapsed at 19:26:26 with the model possibly recoverable; the run stayed paused to the cap. 13 min of a 45-min run used.
  - **Root cause:** T1-FD made count-based opens TIMED precisely because "with fail-fast a permanent open could never observe a success" — and the pause site recreates that exact trap one level up: once paused, no tick ever consults `isOpen()` again, so the self-recovering breaker is frozen into a permanent halt. One invariant (when may we retry the LLM?) decided at two sites with contradictory answers — [[feedback-one-invariant-one-home]]; the breaker owns retry timing.
  - **Fix:** at the top of the scheduled tick, a pause whose reason is exactly `llm-circuit-breaker` AND whose breaker reports `!isOpen()` (cooldown elapsed or closed) resumes: clear `pausedReason`, emit a `system_resumed` behaviour event, run the cycle. The tick that resumes skips re-processing the stale `cycleResultState` (it was fully processed on the pause tick, before the breaker check). Permanent opens (401/quota → `isOpen()` stays true) and every other pause reason (user-pause, exhaustion halts) never auto-resume. No new time constants: the breaker's escalating cooldown (60s→600s, `timedOpens` ratchet) is the sole retry policy — a still-dead model re-opens after one failed call and re-pauses with a longer window ([[feedback-relative-thresholds]]).
  - **DoD:** breaker-paused context + closed breaker → next tick runs a cycle and emits `system_resumed`; breaker-paused + still-open breaker → stays paused, no cycle; user-paused + closed breaker → stays paused. Preflight watcher classifies a run with ≥3 consecutive breaker opens (no success between) as `model-unavailable` instead of `silent-Ns`/`deadline`.
  - **Tier T1:** a real logic bug — the T1-FD capability is defeated by its caller. Related: T4-AS (multi-provider fallback) stays a placeholder — its trigger fired, but under [[project-local-first-constraint]] the right response is recover-when-the-local-model-returns, not a hosted fallback.
  - **✅ SHIPPED same day (`d6751bf`, suite 2030/0):** built as filed — resume branch at the top of the tick (reason+`!isOpen()` gated, stale-result-state skip), `system_resumed` behaviour event, preflight `model-unavailable` terminal via consecutive-opens awk (validated against the 19:12 corpus: 1 open → no trigger; synthetic 3-consecutive → triggers). 3 unit tests pin resume / still-open stays paused / user-pause never auto-resumes. Field watch: first live `system_resumed` after a breaker episode.
