- [x] **T3-BG: Enrich planner prompt with subgoal health and project state** (`PlannerProtocolContract`)
  - **Problem (observed 2026-04-08 23:52 run):** When a subgoal is stagnating and REPLAN fires, the planner is repeatedly invoked but generates proposals that are (a) redundant with work already attempted and (b) blocked by the backlog guard. The planner's prompt contains only goal text, evaluation feedback summary, and interpretation context — it has no visibility into how many cycles the current subgoal has been stagnating, which acceptance criteria passed vs. failed, what files currently exist in the project, or persistent heuristic warnings. As a result, each planner invocation starts essentially blind to the actual problem.
  - **Observed failure pattern:** In the 23:52 run, a single broad subgoal ("Establish a Spring Boot application...") stagnated for 4 cycles. The planner was invoked 3 times during REPLAN — each time generating reasonable but context-free proposals that were immediately blocked by "skipping injection — 1 active subgoals already in backlog." All three proposals were discarded. The subgoal eventually exhausted and the session terminated.
  - **Mechanical note:** `PlannerAgent.processRemovals()` runs BEFORE the backlog guard. So if the planner proposes `#SubGoalRemove <stuck-goal-id>` + `#SubGoalAppend <focused replacements>`, the removal empties the backlog before the injection check — the decompose pattern already works mechanically. The planner just needs to know it should use it and when.
  - **Fix:** Add three new sections to `PlannerProtocolContract.getUserPrompt()` (all data already available on `CycleContextData`):
    1. `--- CURRENT SUBGOAL STATUS ---`: stagnating cycle count (`cumulativeStagnatingCycles`), last score + delta, criteria with pass/fail from last evaluation (`currentSubGoalCriteria` × `criteriaAssessments`), persistent heuristic warnings (`persistentHeuristicWarnings`). Shown only when a current subgoal exists.
    2. Decompose coaching note (shown only when `cumulativeStagnatingCycles >= 3`): "⚠ This subgoal has been stagnating for N cycles. Consider decomposing: use `#SubGoalRemove <id>` to remove it, then `#SubGoalAppend` with narrower, file-level replacements. Removal is processed before injection — the backlog will be empty in time for the new subgoals."
    3. `--- PROJECT STRUCTURE ---`: `ctx.projectSummary()` truncated to ~30 lines, so the planner can anchor proposed subgoals to concrete existing file paths.
  - **No logic change outside the prompt.** All data is on `CycleContextData`; the coaching note makes the existing `#SubGoalRemove + #SubGoalAppend` decompose pattern discoverable by the LLM.
  - **Expected outcome:** When a subgoal stagnates past the threshold, the planner proposes `#SubGoalRemove` + focused `#SubGoalAppend` rather than proposals that get blocked. The stuck subgoal is given up voluntarily and replaced with a more granular plan before exhaustion forces termination.
  - **Depends on:** T3-AY (criteria populated), T3-BC (unmet criteria surfaced on context).

- [x] **T3-BH: Plan rationale and sibling coordination context** (`PlannerProtocolContract`, `PlannerResponseParser`, `PlannerOutcome`, `GoalEntity.metadata`, `EvolutionProtocolContract`, `EvaluationProtocolContract`)
  - **Problem (observed 2026-04-08 runs):** When the planner proposes N subgoals as a batch, they share no common rationale. Each subgoal is a standalone description with standalone criteria. Evolution working on subgoal K doesn't know subgoals K+1…N exist — it may implement their scope. Evaluation working on subgoal K penalizes for missing everything that K+1…N are supposed to cover, creating excessive score pressure and forcing each subgoal to over-implement. Concretely: the first plan injected a single broad subgoal covering the entire API, because there was no mechanism to signal that a batch of smaller, ordered, coordinated subgoals is preferred.
  - **Root cause:** The planner response format has no way to express coordination intent across a batch of proposed subgoals. The agents that execute each subgoal have no visibility into the plan's overall structure.
  - **Fix:**
    1. **Planner emits `PlanRationale:`** — a 1–2 sentence field (required when ≥ 2 subgoals are proposed) describing what the batch collectively achieves and how the subgoals relate to each other. Example: "Subgoals 1–3 implement Books, Members, and Loans as separate self-contained resource groups in that order. Each subgoal should be evaluated only for its own resource group — do not penalise for absent sibling groups."
    2. **`PlannerResponseParser`** parses `PlanRationale:` → new field on `PlannerOutcome`.
    3. **`PlannerAgent.injectOutcomeGoals()` / `planInto()`** stores the rationale in parent `GoalEntity.metadata["planRationale"]` when subgoals are injected.
    4. **Evolution prompt** gains `--- PLAN CONTEXT ---` block: plan rationale (from parent metadata) + list of completed siblings (same `parentId`, `COMPLETED` status) + list of upcoming siblings (same `parentId`, `ACTIVE` status, excluding current). Instruction: "Focus ONLY on what this subgoal requires. Do not implement functionality covered by upcoming siblings."
    5. **Evaluation prompt** gains the same `--- PLAN CONTEXT ---` block with an explicit scoring note: "Do not penalise for absent functionality that will be handled by upcoming sibling subgoals (listed above)."
  - **Sibling data source:** `goalPlannerService.getAllGoals()` filtered by `parentId == current.parentId`. Split into completed vs. remaining (excluding current). Already available via `GoalPlannerService`.
  - **PlanRationale in prompt contract rule:** Add a `PLAN_RATIONALE` rule to `PlannerProtocolContract` (alongside the existing `Criteria:` requirement): "When proposing 2 or more subgoals, include `PlanRationale:` explaining how they collectively advance the root goal and what each covers. This rationale will be shown to the agents executing each subgoal."
  - **Depends on:** T3-BG (produces better-scoped subgoal batches for the rationale to coordinate).
  - **Note:** Sibling filtering by `parentId` requires that subgoals produced by the planner in the same batch share a common parent. This is already the case — `injectOutcomeGoals()` passes `context.currentSubGoalId()` as `parentGoalId` for all subgoals in a batch.

- [x] **T3-BB: Persist per-evaluation `CriterionResult` nodes to Neo4j** (`EvaluationActionRegistrar`, `EvaluationGraphFacade`)
  - **Problem:** `criteriaAssessments` from T3-AZ are carried on `CycleContextData` for the current cycle only; they are not persisted and are invisible to the orchestration snapshot, retrospective analysis, and any heuristic wanting to trend per-criterion failure rate across cycles.
  - **Fix:** In `EvaluationActionRegistrar.registerEvaluation()`, write each parsed `[N] ✓/✗` line as a `CriterionResult` node linked from the evaluation action node:
    ```
    (:EvaluationAction)-[:HAS_CRITERION]->(:CriterionResult {
      index: int, text: String, passed: Boolean,
      reason: String,          // ✗ failure reason if present
      cycleId: String, subgoalId: String
    })
    ```
    This schema enables per-criterion queries: "how many times did criterion 2 fail for this subgoal?" and "which criteria have never passed?".
  - **Distinct from T3-BI** (which persists *cumulative* pass status — the rolled-up view per subgoal). T3-BB is the raw event log; T3-BI is the derived summary.
  - **Depends on:** T3-AZ (source of the assessments). T3-BI and T3-BJ can read from this event log.

- [x] **T3-BI: Persist cumulative criteria status to `GoalEntity` / Neo4j** (`GoalPlannerService`, `Neo4jGoalGraphService`, `CycleContextCoordinator`, `GoalEntity`)
  - **Problem:** T1-BG's `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` lives entirely in `CycleContextData` and is lost on restart. If the system restarts mid-subgoal, all accumulated criterion passes are forgotten and the subgoal must re-earn them from scratch — cycling criteria that had already been satisfied.
  - **Fix:** Mirror the `mergeCount` pattern (T2-BI hotfix): store cumulative pass status in `GoalEntity.metadata` under key `"criteriaPassStatus"` as a JSON-serialised `Map<Integer, Boolean>`. Three integration points:
    1. **Write:** `GoalPlannerService.markCriterionPassed(goalId, criterionIndex)` — loads current metadata map, sets `criteriaPassStatus[index] = true`, saves to graph. Called from `EvaluationAgent` after each `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` update (same location as T1-BG's in-memory update).
    2. **Read on startup/sync:** `GoalPlannerService` (or `CycleContextCoordinator`) loads `criteriaPassStatus` from the active subgoal's metadata on context preparation and populates `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` on the context. This restores the accumulated state transparently after a restart.
    3. **Reset:** When a subgoal transitions to FULFILLED or GIVEN_UP, the metadata entry is no longer needed (the goal is closed). No explicit cleanup required.
  - **Graph note:** Metadata is already stored as a JSON blob on the `Goal` node; no schema change is needed. The same pattern is used for `mergeCount`, `cumulativeStagnatingCycles`, `acceptanceCriteria`.
  - **Depends on:** T1-BG (defines `cumulativeCriteriaStatus`), T2-BI (establishes the metadata persistence pattern).
  - **Enables:** T3-BJ (snapshot service reads from here rather than querying T3-BB's event log for the rolled-up view).

- [x] **T3-BJ: Surface criteria progress in orchestration snapshot** (`OrchestrationSnapshotService`, `OrchestrationSnapshotFormatter`)
  - **Problem:** The meta-deliberation agent and interpretation agent currently have no visibility into *which* criteria have been satisfied and which have persistently failed for the current subgoal. They can observe that the subgoal is PROGRESSING, but they cannot distinguish "3 of 4 criteria satisfied — one stubborn criterion remaining" from "0 of 4 criteria ever passed — subgoal is fundamentally stuck." These require completely different steering responses (targeted evolution vs. replanning), but the snapshot gives the agents no data to reason from.
  - **Fix:** In `OrchestrationSnapshotService`, for the active subgoal:
    1. Load `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` from `GoalEntity.metadata["criteriaPassStatus"]` (T3-BI) — the rolled-up per-criterion pass/fail across all cycles.
    2. Query the N most recent `CriterionResult` nodes for this subgoal (T3-BB) to determine *how long* each unmet criterion has been failing (streak count).
    3. Build a `criteriaProgressBlock`: per-criterion summary formatted as `[✓/✗/–] <text> (passed N cycles ago | failed M consecutive cycles | never assessed)`.
  - **Surface in `OrchestrationSnapshotFormatter`** under `--- CRITERIA PROGRESS ---`, between the evaluation summary and the signal list. Visible to the meta-deliberation agent, interpretation agent, and the planner's `CURRENT SUBGOAL STATUS` block.
  - **Expected steering impact:** Meta-agent proposes targeted evolution when 3/4 criteria pass (one remaining). Interpretation agent emits `REPLAN_REQUESTED` when a criterion has failed 5+ consecutive cycles with no improvement. Planner's coaching note becomes criterion-specific ("criterion 2 has never passed — the implementation of X is missing").
  - **Depends on:** T3-BB (event log for streak counts), T3-BI (cumulative status for rolled-up view). Can be partially implemented with T3-BI alone (no streak counts) and upgraded to full streaks when T3-BB is ready.

- [x] **T3-BK: Partial graduation — force-fulfill at high criteria pass rate** (`SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic`, `GoalPlannerService`, `PlannerAgent`)
  - **Problem:** A single stubborn criterion can hold an otherwise-complete subgoal hostage indefinitely. If 3 of 4 criteria have passed across multiple cycles but criterion 4 has failed N consecutive times (likely due to a structural gap in evolution rather than a solvable incremental problem), the subgoal will exhaust and be GIVEN_UP — discarding the real progress made on the other three.
  - **Fix:** In `SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic.decide()`, after the normal fulfillment path fails (unmet criterion veto), check graduation: if `passedCount / totalCount >= GRADUATION_RATIO` (default 0.80, configurable via `autobuilder.criteria.graduation-ratio`) AND the remaining unmet criteria have each failed for at least `GRADUATION_MIN_FAIL_STREAK` cycles (default 3, read from `cumulativeCriteriaStatus` + `lastCriteriaPassCount` history), return `FulfillmentDecision.yes(score, "graduation: M/N criteria satisfied, remaining injected as micro-subgoal")`.
  - **On graduation:** `CycleExecutor.applyCompletion()` detects the "graduation" rationale and calls `PlannerAgent` (or directly `GoalPlannerService`) to inject one micro-subgoal per unmet criterion, each with a single-criterion `Criteria:` block. The parent subgoal is then marked FULFILLED.
  - **Effect:** Progress is banked; the system moves forward rather than exhausting. The micro-subgoal is a focused, smaller target that evolution can hit in fewer cycles.
  - **Configurable:** `autobuilder.criteria.graduation-ratio: 0.80`, `autobuilder.criteria.graduation-min-fail-streak: 3`.
  - **Depends on:** T1-BG (`cumulativeCriteriaStatus`), T3-BI (streak history), T2-BL (exhaustion suppression should fire before graduation is needed — graduation is the last resort).

- [x] **T3-BP: Capture goal/subgoal completion and give-up rationale**

  - **Problem:** When a subgoal transitions to COMPLETED or GIVEN_UP, no reason is recorded. The graph shows the final state but not why — was it fulfilled by criteria? Abandoned after N stagnating cycles? Given up because the planner replaced it? This information is available at transition time but currently discarded.
  - **Fix:**
    1. Add a resolution string field to GoalEntity (Neo4j) and the JSON goal stack. Populated at transition time via GoalPlannerService.
    2. In promoteCurrentSubGoal / wherever COMPLETED / GIVEN_UP is written, pass a short rationale string. Call sites to cover:                                                                       
       - COMPLETED via SubGoalFulfillmentHeuristic → e.g. "all criteria passed, score 0.88"                         
       - GIVEN_UP via stagnation exhaustion → e.g. "given up after N stagnating cycles"
       - GIVEN_UP via planner replacement → e.g. "superseded by replanning"
       - GIVEN_UP via GOAL_EXHAUSTED signal
    3. Surface resolution in OrchestrationSnapshotFormatter under the goal/subgoal header so the LLM meta-agent can see it.
  - **Why:** Without this, post-hoc analysis (and the deliberation agent) can't distinguish a subgoal that cleanly passed from one that was silently abandoned. It also aids debugging when goals are given up prematurely.
  - **Depends on:** None — purely additive metadata.

- [~] **T3-BX: The validation layer is decorative — every collaborator exists except the one that arms it, so bad input becomes a 500 instead of a 400** (`analysis/structure/WiringFactsAnalyzer`) — **filed 2026-07-27 from run `2026-07-27_13-29-30`, raised by the user's "odd, I think we have plenty of code in there preventing this".**
  - **They were right that the code is there, which is what makes it interesting.** The artifact carries a full `@RestControllerAdvice` mapping `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → 400, `ConstraintViolationException` → 400, `IllegalArgumentException` → 400, the domain's not-found → 404, its rule-violation → 409, and a catch-all → 500. All three controllers annotate their request bodies for validation. **And the model package declares ZERO constraint annotations** (measured: 3 `@Valid` usages, 0 constraints across every model type).
  - **So the mechanism is complete except at exactly one link.** Nothing can throw the validation exceptions the advice handles, an empty body deserialises to a type whose fields are all null, the service dereferences one, and the catch-all reports **500** — the runtime failure that blocked root closure (`T4-BV`: *"POST /loans answers 500 when exercised with body {}"*). The spec asks for 400/404/409 there.
  - **Why this is worth a rule and not a shrug:** wrong status codes are this project's most persistent artifact defect — the 2026-07-18 stability check traced false completions to *"Loans collapses all to 400"*, the 21/23 measurement's residual was a wrong success code, and this is the same family with a **mechanical, statically visible cause**. It is not a model-capability limit; the loop can see it.
  - **Derivable without naming a framework** ([[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]]): *a parameter carries an annotation from package P, and the project-local type of that parameter declares no annotation from package P.* The family is read off the annotation's own import, so the rule holds no opinion on a project that never imports one — the self-gating [[feedback-ecosystem-gated-heuristics]] requires. Same shape and same home as `T3-BW`'s peer-consistency rule, which is already vocabulary-free and already reaches the evolution prompt.
  - **DoD:** the fact is derived from the project's own code and reaches the evolution prompt, proven by a test using invented annotation names; and a run whose model types gain constraints answers the malformed-body probe with the spec's status rather than 500.
  - **Gate before building** ([[project-pattern-recognition-design-note]] §7): one field sample. Confirm the shape recurs on the next runs' artifacts (cheap: count `@Valid`-style usages vs constraints in a run's `output/`) before adding the rule.
  - **✅ GATE MET the same day — second sample, different run, different resource, and it SHARPENS the rule.** Run `2026-07-27_14-42-19` (GOAL_FULFILLED, `SMOKE: 21/23`) fails check **`[10] POST /members missing name` → 201, spec wants 400**, while the Book checks `[2] [3] [4]` all pass with 400. So `Book` DOES carry constraints and `Member` does not: the defect is not "no constraints anywhere" (run `13-29-30`'s shape) but **constraints present on one type and absent on its peer** — which is exactly the odd-one-out relation `T3-BW`'s `peerAnnotationAnomalies()` already computes, on types instead of controllers. Both shapes are the same rule read at different densities: *a type reached by a validated parameter that carries none of the annotation family its peers carry.*
  - **Ready to build, and it is the cheapest item with a met gate in the queue.** Expected yield is directly measured: `[10]` is 1 of the 2 checks between run 4's 21/23 and 23/23. The other, `[22] POST return absent` → 409 where the spec wants 404, is a status-code MAPPING defect (not-found routed to the rule-violation handler) and belongs with `T4-CO`, not here.
  - **BUILT 2026-07-30 (field half of the DoD still open — see the residual below); the defect was NOT a missing rule. The rule already existed and its output never reached the agent that could act on it.**
    - **What I found before building anything:** `WiringFactsAnalyzer.collectValidationSurfaceObservations` — shipped long ago, listed in the class javadoc — already emits exactly this fact, including the exact sentence this ticket describes. Run over the real output trees of **six** recent corpora it produced a status-path fact on **all six**, among them *"LoanController.createLoan() requests validation of Loan but Loan declares no field constraint annotations"*, which is precisely why `POST /loans` answered 500 where the spec asks for 400. Meanwhile `peerAnnotationAnomalies()` — **the only analyzer path that reaches the evolution prompt** — returned **0 on all six**. So `analyze()` goes to the criteria verifier and nowhere else: the loop could see the cause of its most persistent artifact defect every single run and never told evolution.
    - **Built:** `statusRiskFacts(outputFiles)` — a deliberate SUBSET of `analyze()` (validation surface + throw/mapping coverage, not stub bodies or unread parameters, which are real facts but not about statuses and would be the raw-payload passthrough T2-EP removed elsewhere) — rendered into the evolution prompt as a conditional block, absent on a healthy artifact.
    - **Plus the sharpening the gate note asked for, in the EXISTING single home:** the "declares no field constraint annotations" fact now names the peer body types that DO declare them — *"It is the only request-body type here without them — Member, Book declare them."* Verified firing on run `2026-07-28_23-16-15`'s own tree. Peer evidence is omitted when no peer carries the family, so the run `13-29-30` shape (none anywhere) is still reported as a gap without falsely calling it an anomaly.
    - **🔴 I FIRST BUILT THE WRONG THING AND DELETED IT.** My initial cut added a second, vocabulary-free detector (`inertParameterAnnotationFacts`, 132 lines) deriving the annotation family from the project's own imports. It worked — it produced the peer-named sentence on the real tree — and it was **a second home for an invariant that already had one**, which [[feedback-one-invariant-one-home]] forbids. Deleted before committing. The vocabulary-free derivation stays an unbuilt idea, recorded here: two annotations are one family when one's import package is a prefix of the other's, which needs no framework name; it is only worth building if `AnnotationVocabularies` is ever shown to miss a real project's constraints.
    - **DoD status:** the "reaches the evolution prompt" half is **MET** and test-covered (6 new tests: the gap fact, the peer naming, the no-peer case, the subset boundary, silence on a consistent artifact, silence on a project with no request bodies). Suite 2267/0/5. **The field half — a run whose model types gain constraints and answers the malformed-body probe with the spec's status — is NOT met** and needs a run; watch it on the next runs' `[10]`-class checks.

- [x] **T3-BW: `WiringFactsAnalyzer` misses the request-mapping-without-stereotype defect — a controller that compiles, registers nothing, and 404s everything** (`analysis/structure/WiringFactsAnalyzer`) — **filed 2026-07-27 from field evidence, run 2026-07-26_22-41.**
  - **Observed:** the run merged `LoanController.java` carrying `@RequestMapping("/loans")` but **no `@RestController`**. Spring never registers it, so every `/loans` path 404s. `BookController` has both annotations and works. The file compiles cleanly — it simply is not a bean, so no compile gate, probe or build can see it.
  - **Cost, measured:** 8 of 23 smoke checks failed on it, and it corrupted the score in BOTH directions — checks [14] and [15] ("bad book → 404", "bad member → 404") **PASSED for the wrong reason**, because a missing endpoint 404s everything. A smoke pass that depends on the endpoint being absent is a false pass, which is this project's recurring false-completion shape at check granularity.
  - **Why this analyzer:** `WiringFactsAnalyzer` already owns exactly this family — stub bodies, never-assigned fields, missing persistence, **unmapped throws** (`@ControllerAdvice`/`@ExceptionHandler` absent), unread parameters, missing validation surface. "A mapping annotation with no stereotype annotation" is the same shape of structural fact and belongs beside them; this is completing an existing rule set, not new machinery.
  - **Ecosystem gating** ([[feedback-ecosystem-gated-heuristics]]): the rule must self-gate on the target's own markers and hold no opinion on a project with no web-framework marker, and the annotation names belong in the existing ecosystem data path, not baked into the analyzer ([[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]]).
  - **RESCOPED 2026-07-27 before any code, on the user's constraint ("the system shouldn't hardcode any toycase prompts like endpoints into it — it should state what is missing derived from the results").** As originally filed this ticket said "a request-mapping annotation without a registering stereotype", which names ecosystem concepts in framework logic. **Build it as a PEER-CONSISTENCY check instead**, which needs no ecosystem knowledge at all:
    - Group the target's types by a structurally-evidenced peer relation (shared annotation shape, name suffix, package). Compute the annotation-set distribution within each group. Report a member whose set is a strict subset of its peers' common set.
    - On this run that yields, with nothing hardcoded: *`BookController` and `MemberController` carry {`RestController`, `RequestMapping`}; `LoanController` carries {`RequestMapping`} — it is the only peer missing `RestController`.* The finding, and the words in it, are **derived from the project's own code**, not from a table of framework names.
    - **This also pays down existing debt rather than adding to it:** `WiringFactsAnalyzer` currently hardcodes `"Entity"`, `"ExceptionHandler"`, `"ResponseStatus"`, `"HttpStatus"` as string literals ([[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]]). A peer-relative rule is the model for migrating those too.
    - **Generalisation worth noting:** an odd-one-out detector over structural facts is a *derived* pattern, not a hand-written one per defect class — which is the half of `T4-C` that is still unmet ("patterns DERIVED, not one detector class per pattern"). Scope this ticket to the annotation-set case; record the generalisation there.
  - **Honest limit, established 2026-07-27:** criteria are verified by an LLM pass over the SOURCE (`CriteriaVerificationService`), with structural facts optionally injected (T4-BS). There is **no per-cycle runtime observation** — execution evidence exists only at the completion edge (T4-BV). So a behavioural criterion that fails for a reason invisible in source is not observable mid-run at all. Peer consistency catches THIS defect (the anomaly is visible in the source); it would not catch a correct-looking handler with wrong runtime semantics. That broader gap belongs to whichever ticket brings execution evidence earlier, not here.
  - **DoD:** a type whose annotation set is a strict subset of its peer group's common set produces a wiring fact naming the specific missing element, derived from the project's own types, with a regression test built from this run's verbatim `LoanController`/`BookController` shapes — **and no new ecosystem identifier introduced into framework code.**
  - **✅ SHIPPED 2026-07-27, DoD met.** `WiringFactsAnalyzer.collectPeerAnnotationOutliers` + `peerAnnotationAnomalies()`, 10 tests, suite 2137/0.
    - **Verified against the REAL run output** before the fixtures were written — the analyzer, pointed at `firestarter/output` from run `2026-07-26_22-41`, emitted: *"LoanController is the only one of the 3 types annotated @RequestMapping that does not also carry @RestController (MemberController, BookController do) — if @RestController is what registers or activates these types, LoanController is inert."* Every identifier in that sentence comes from the target's own code.
    - **Zero ecosystem identifiers added.** The rule reads no vocabulary table; `AnnotationVocabularies` is untouched. Proved by a test using invented annotations (`@Zorp`/`@Quux`) that fires identically — genericity demonstrated rather than asserted.
    - **Epistemically honest wording:** the analyzer does not know what an annotation MEANS, so it hedges — "if @X is what registers or activates these types" — instead of claiming a defect it cannot verify.
    - **Errs toward silence, on a RELATIVE bar** ([[feedback-relative-thresholds]]): a peer group needs ≥2 other members before its shape counts as a norm, and only a UNANIMOUS peer set counts — one dissenter makes it a style choice. Tests pin silence for: non-unanimous sets, too-few peers, no annotations at all, fully consistent artifacts, and duplicate suppression when two markers reach the same anomaly.
    - **Reaches the agent that can act on it.** The analyzer was previously consumed ONLY by `CriteriaVerificationService` (the verifier), so a fact there could not change what evolution writes. `peerAnnotationAnomalies()` exposes just this signal, and `EvolutionProtocolContract` now renders it as a conditional block — absent entirely on a consistent artifact, which is the lean shape [[project-t4ap-prompt-audit]] favours over an unconditional payload.
    - **Residual:** the block tells evolution the difference exists; it does not yet ROUTE a stuck subgoal to look at it — that is `T2-ES`, still open.
  - **FIELD TEST IN FLIGHT — prediction stated BEFORE the run (2026-07-27, 90-min cap, continuing the broken tree with `reset-on-start=false` so the defect is present at cycle 1 rather than hoping the model reproduces it):**
    1. the anomaly block appears in evolution prompts **from the first cycle**;
    2. `@RestController` is added to `LoanController` **within a few cycles**, instead of the 27 `#NoDiff` repeats the same tree produced before;
    3. smoke rises from the measured **11/23** — the 8-check `/loans` cluster clears, leaving the 4 validation failures, so **~17–19/23** is the realistic ceiling for this run.
    - **Decision rule:** if (1) holds and (2) does NOT, the fact was delivered and ignored — that is the case FOR `T2-ES` routing, and the honest reading is that delivery alone is insufficient. If neither holds, the block is not reaching the live prompt path and T3-BW's closure is wrong.
    - **Known confounds:** the prior run ended by host FREEZE, not a clean halt, so `meta/` may carry mid-cycle state; and the 4 validation failures are a separate defect that this change cannot touch.
  - **✅ FIELD TEST RESULT (run `2026-07-27_01-01-01`) — prediction 1 CONFIRMED, prediction 2 REFUTED for a reason that exonerates this ticket and indicts another.**
    - **(1) CONFIRMED:** the anomaly block reached live evolution prompts **19 times in 35 cycles**, verified inside an `EvolutionAgent → [USR]` prompt naming the file and the missing annotation.
    - **(2) The model ACTED on it — my first reading was wrong and I record it as such.** A grep of the output file said "no `@RestController`", which looked like the fact being ignored. Checking the PROPOSED mutations instead: of 17 proposed `LoanController` variants, **several carry `@RestController`**, and one was scored **0.85 ACCEPTED and MERGED**. The information changed the model's behaviour exactly as intended.
    - **(3) The loop then threw the fix away — three times.** Merges touching that file oscillated `with → without → with → without → with → without` inside three minutes, every merge ACCEPTED, none a rollback. Root cause is a missing merge-regression guard → **`T2-CI`, reopened with this evidence.**
    - **Consequence for `T2-ES`:** routing a stuck subgoal to structural investigation would NOT have helped here. Nothing was stuck for want of information; the loop had the fact, acted on it, and discarded the result. T2-ES remains worth doing for the case where no structural trace exists, but it is NOT the fix for this failure mode — recorded so nobody builds it expecting this outcome to change.
    - **Smoke prediction (3) is untestable from this run** until the oscillation is fixed: the artifact's score now depends on which side of the flip the run happens to stop on.

- [n] **T3-G: Complexity-adaptive regression tolerance — Phase 2 (lines changed composite + calibration)** (`ScoreRegressionHeuristic`, `Neo4jScoreHistoryService`, `CycleContextData`)
  - **CLOSED 2026-07-16 (Opus 4.8) — PREMISE FALSIFIED on 1151 samples; won't-do, G1 not built.** The ticket rests on "file count is a crude proxy; lines changed correlates more directly with LLM evaluation variance." Tested the coarse half against the existing behaviour corpus (file count + final score are both already recorded per merged cycle — no G1 plumbing needed for the check): across **1151 merged cycles**, score is flat across every file-count bucket (mean 0.79/0.81/0.79/0.78 for 1 / 2-3 / 4-6 / 7+ files) and **score stdev is constant at ~0.05 in every bucket** — Pearson **r(fileCount, score) = −0.076**, i.e. no relationship. Diff size does not predict score or its variance in this corpus, so a calibrator (G2) has nothing to fit, and G1 exists only to feed G2. Consistent with the T4-J finding that score-regression calibration is not a live surface, and with the measured-variance regime that killed batch gating (score noise is dominated by model nondeterminism, not diff complexity). **Re-entry condition:** a future model/regime where merged-cycle score variance visibly tracks diff size (re-run the same corpus check; it is cheap). Note the finer proxy (line count) could in principle differ from file count, but the coarse proxy showing exactly zero — flat means AND flat variance — makes a hidden line-count signal implausible enough not to build speculative persistence for. Sub-tickets G1/G2 closed with the parent.
  - **Status (2026-04-21):** Split into two sub-tickets. Reassessment found the core infrastructure exists — `Neo4jScoreHistoryService` persists per-file scores, global scores, and per-goal evaluation/acceptance events linked via `Cycle` nodes; `DefaultMutationHeuristicAnalyzer` already computes `linesAdded`/`linesDeleted` per file from `diffReport`. What's missing is the linkage (diff size isn't persisted alongside the cycle's score) and the calibration algorithm (current T2-AJ constants are hand-picked).
  - **Core motivation (unchanged):** File count is a crude proxy. A 1-line change to 4 files is not complex; a 500-line rewrite of 1 file is. Lines changed correlates more directly with LLM evaluation variance.
  - **Design options for composite:** (A) replace file-count breakpoints with line-count breakpoints; (B) composite score combining both; (C) weighted product. Decide based on calibration outcome.

- [x] **T3-BL: Criteria-banked FULFILLED early exit** (`CycleExecutor`, `AdaptiveExecutionEngine`, `GoalPlannerService`)
  - **Origin:** T1-CO Part A (demoted 2026-04-14 — scaffold exists via T1-BG, needs wiring).
  - **Problem:** When all acceptance criteria have been individually confirmed (banked as `true` in `cumulativeCriteriaStatus`) across prior evaluation cycles, the subgoal is functionally done — but the loop continues trying to generate new mutations because there is no early-exit path that consults the banked state before entering the diff/evaluation flow.
  - **Fix:** At the start of each cycle in `CycleExecutor` (or `AdaptiveExecutionEngine`, before meta steps execute), call `goalPlannerService.allCriteriaDefinedAndBanked(currentSubGoalId)`. If all criteria are banked as `true` AND `mergeCount > 0` (at least one real merge occurred — prevents a brand-new subgoal from self-fulfilling), call `applyGoalProgress(FULFILLED)` and skip the rest of the cycle. Guard: criteria list must be non-empty (criteria-less subgoals are handled by T2-CD).
  - **Changes:** `CycleExecutor.java` or `AdaptiveExecutionEngine.java` — add early-exit check (~10 lines). `GoalPlannerService.java` — expose `allCriteriaDefinedAndBanked(String goalId)`: criteria list non-empty AND all indices in `criteriaPassStatus` are `true`.
  - **Tests:** (a) all criteria banked + mergeCount > 0 → FULFILLED, rest of cycle skipped; (b) all criteria banked + mergeCount == 0 → no early exit; (c) criteria list empty → no early exit (falls through to T2-CD path).
  - **Depends on:** T1-BG (cumulativeCriteriaStatus persisted in GoalEntity). T1-CF (the FULFILLED promotion mechanism this reuses). T1-CN (prerequisite — stale REPLAN must be cleared first or it masks the fulfilled state).
  - **Enables:** T2-CC's `#NoDiff` evolution path can shortcut to this check when evolution self-reports no change needed.

- [>] **T3-BM: Stateless LLM criteria verification on repeated no-diff cycles — SUPERSEDED by T3-BR** (`StatelessCriteriaChecker`, `CycleExecutor`, `AutobuilderService`)
  - **Deferred 2026-04-21:** Reframed rather than implemented as originally designed. The ticket proposed a NEW `StatelessCriteriaChecker` component — a parallel LLM call reading current output + criteria — whose sole purpose is to bypass the evaluator's `already evaluated current evolution fingerprint` guard when criteria exist but aren't all banked. On re-analysis this is a redundancy-layer smell: the evaluator *already* scores against criteria (T3-AZ/T3-BC); the root cause is that the fingerprint-repeat guard is too coarse, not that a second verifier is needed.
  - **Root cause (correctly identified):** The fingerprint guard decides "skip the evaluator — same fingerprint, nothing new." But fingerprint identity is not a sufficient cache key — the *completeness* of the evaluator's prior result also depends on (a) the set of currently-defined criteria (which can grow via T3-BE analysis injection mid-subgoal) and (b) which of those criteria have been banked so far. If criteria are defined but not all banked on the same fingerprint, the evaluator's prior result is incomplete, and re-running against the unbanked criteria is warranted.
  - **Supersession path:** See **T3-BR** — criteria-aware fingerprint-repeat guard. This removes the need for a parallel verifier and keeps the evaluator as the single authority on criteria satisfaction.
  - **Preserved for reference (original design):** Add `StatelessCriteriaChecker` that, on fingerprint-repeat with unbanked criteria, runs a minimal LLM call to confirm/deny each criterion and promotes FULFILLED if all pass. The concern that killed this approach: it introduces a second LLM-call path with its own prompt/parser for work the evaluator already knows how to do, and leaves the evaluator's gating bug unfixed for all other consumers.

- [x] **T3-BR: Criteria-aware fingerprint-repeat guard — let the evaluator re-run when unbanked criteria exist** (`EvaluationAgent`, `ExecutionEligibilityExplainer`, `ContextLineageTracker`, `CycleContextData`, `GoalPlannerService`) *(supersedes T3-BM, 2026-04-21; implemented 2026-05-02)*
  - **Problem:** The fingerprint-repeat guard (`already evaluated current evolution fingerprint`) currently skips evaluation whenever the evolution output hash matches a prior cycle's — treating fingerprint identity as a sufficient cache key. It isn't. The evaluator's prior result can be *incomplete* relative to the criteria that are currently in force: criteria may have been added via T3-BE analysis injection after the first evaluation, or the first evaluation may have failed to assess some criteria (LLM partial compliance). In both cases the cumulative-status map still has unbanked criteria for this subgoal, but the guard blocks the evaluator from re-checking them. The subgoal stalls and eventually exhausts even though the needed verification was cheap.
  - **Fix:** Replace the boolean fingerprint-identity guard with a conjunction:
    - skip evaluation if `fingerprintRepeats && allDefinedCriteriaBanked`
    - otherwise run evaluation (the fingerprint may be the same but the open questions are not).
    `allDefinedCriteriaBanked` is already computable via `goalPlannerService.allCriteriaDefinedAndBanked(currentSubGoalId)` (introduced by T3-BL). Subgoals with no criteria defined fall through to T2-CD's existing criteria-less handling — unchanged.
  - **Effect:** Once the evaluator re-runs and banks the remaining criteria, T3-BL's early-exit fires naturally on the next cycle and promotes FULFILLED. No new LLM-call component, no new prompt/parser, no parallel verifier. The evaluator remains the single authority on criteria satisfaction.
  - **Edge cases:**
    - **Evaluator keeps returning partial results (LLM non-determinism):** Could produce repeated re-evaluations on every cycle with no progress. Guard with a per-subgoal `evaluatorRetriesOnSameFingerprint` counter; cap at N (e.g. 3) and then fall through to T2-CD or emit `REPLAN_REQUESTED`. **BUILD_FIX carve-out (2026-05-04):** for subgoals with `metadata[blockerType]=BUILD_FIX` (see `BlockerTypes` from T5-K/T1-DN), do NOT emit `REPLAN_REQUESTED` at the cap — replanning injects new subgoals that also cannot be evaluated positively while the build is red, causing goal explosion. Detect via `isActiveBuildFixSubgoal()` (same helper T1-DN adds) and fall through to stagnation-only instead. The stagnation/signal-decay path is the correct resolution for this structural deadlock.
    - **Evaluator says "everything fails" repeatedly:** Handled by the existing stagnation/exhaustion machinery — criteria that legitimately cannot be satisfied should time out through normal paths, not be force-banked.
  - **Test plan:** (a) fingerprint repeats + all criteria banked → skip evaluation (unchanged); (b) fingerprint repeats + some criteria unbanked → evaluator runs; (c) evaluator runs and banks remaining criteria → next cycle T3-BL fires FULFILLED; (d) evaluator runs 3× on same fingerprint without progress → fall through with REPLAN_REQUESTED.
  - **Depends on:** T3-BL (`allCriteriaDefinedAndBanked` helper). T1-BG (`cumulativeCriteriaStatus`). T3-BE (analysis-injected criteria are the primary consumer — they are the main reason criteria can appear mid-subgoal).

- [x] **T3-BO: Audit T3-BH (plan rationale / sibling context) — empirical effectiveness of the evolution-side PLAN CONTEXT block** (`EvolutionProtocolContract`)
  - **AUDIT DONE + DECISION EXECUTED 2026-07-16 (Opus 4.8, `e55766f`, suite 2005/0) — decision output: REMOVE the evolution-side block, keep the evaluation-side block.** Method was corpus-grounded, not the filed live paired A/B (paired live runs under measured variance are exactly what [[feedback-replay-over-batches]] forbids). Evidence: (1) the block renders heavily — 25-62 "upcoming siblings — do not implement" directives per recent run; (2) under depth-first decomposition (T2-EI, now the operative mode) the planner hands evolution one dependency-ordered subgoal at a time, so those "upcoming siblings" are precisely the not-yet-built dependencies the model must build to compile — hypothesis 2's net-harmful regime; (3) the 2026-04-21 motivating case shows the model correctly IGNORING the directive on a required 14-file cross-resource merge (hypothesis 2 confirmed harmful-or-inert); (4) the naming-consistency A/B (0/6, [[project-t4bq-naming-consistency-ab]]) established this local model ignores evolution-prompt scope directives regardless, so the block cannot be reliably beneficial (hypothesis 1 fails). The evaluation-side block (do-not-penalise-for-absent-upcoming-sibling-work) is the validated-useful half (2026-04-21: evaluator scored accurately without penalising) and is UNTOUCHED. This is decision-output "Remove evolution-side block entirely (keep evaluation-side only)".
  - **Scope narrowed (2026-04-21):** Originally bundled empirical audit + mechanical cleanup. Cleanup items split into **T3-BQ** because the audit outcome gates what cleanup is needed — if the evolution-side block is removed entirely, dedup and reload-simplification collapse to "delete, don't refactor."
  - **Motivation (2026-04-21 log analysis):** T3-BH is shipped but its real-world impact is ambiguous. The evaluation-side PLAN CONTEXT (do not penalise for upcoming siblings) appears correct — the evaluator in cycle-1776735068286 scored the return-endpoint mutation accurately without penalising for absent validation. The evolution-side instruction is restrictive: "Focus ONLY on what this subgoal requires. Do not implement functionality covered by upcoming siblings." Its purpose is to prevent scope bleed — evolution implementing work reserved for later subgoals. But in the 2026-04-21 session a 14-file merge happened because `LoanService` already `@Autowired BookService` and `MemberService` (which didn't exist); the LLM had to create them for the code to compile. It ignored the restrictive instruction — which is the *correct* behaviour here, because the cross-file work was structurally necessary.
  - **Core tension:** The evolution-side instruction is only beneficial in the subset of cases where (a) subgoals are genuinely self-contained (no inter-subgoal file dependencies) AND (b) the LLM would otherwise over-implement without being told to stop. If either condition fails — dependencies exist, or the LLM stays in scope naturally — the instruction is either ignored (neutral) or obeyed at the cost of blocking required cross-cutting work (harmful). There is no middle ground where it "slows" convergence; it either helps, is inert, or blocks.
  - **Hypotheses to test:**
    1. **Self-contained case (no inter-subgoal deps):** Does the instruction reduce over-implementation observably (fewer files touched per mutation, less work belonging to other subgoals)? Or does the LLM already stay in scope without it?
    2. **Dependency-carrying case:** Does the instruction ever successfully suppress a cross-file creation that was actually needed? If yes, the instruction is net-harmful in this regime — it leaves the code uncompilable until a later subgoal fills the gap.
    3. **Rationale sentence alone vs. full sibling lists:** Is the "Plan rationale: …" line the useful part (carries intent), and the sibling lists the redundant/harmful part (triggers the restrictive reflex)?
  - **Method:** Run paired sessions on the same root goal with and without the evolution-side `--- PLAN CONTEXT ---` block (two branches differ only in whether `planContextBlock()` is appended in `EvolutionProtocolContract`). Compare: cycles-to-first-merge, count of mutations per subgoal, whether cross-resource files were created during "wrong" subgoals, and frequency of uncompilable interim output states. Use **T3-BP**'s resolution rationale to measure give-up reasons per subgoal — a subgoal given up as "stagnation" when its dependencies were missing is evidence for the harmful-obedience case.
  - **Decision outputs:**
    - **Keep as-is** (only if hypothesis 1 confirms benefit AND hypothesis 2 finds no harm).
    - **Remove evolution-side block entirely** (keep evaluation-side only).
    - **Keep rationale sentence, drop sibling lists** (if hypothesis 3 isolates the useful part).
    - **Weaken wording** (e.g. "prefer to focus on this subgoal" instead of "do not implement"), making it a suggestion rather than a restriction.
    The decision determines T3-BQ's scope.
  - **Depends on:** T3-BH (precondition — shipped). **T3-BP** (resolution rationale enriches the audit data — ship first).

  - **CLOSED 2026-07-16 (Opus 4.8, `e55766f`) — collapsed to the "evolution-side block removed" branch.** Per this ticket's own gating: with the evolution-side `planContextBlock` deleted (T3-BO decision), the block deletion IS the whole cleanup — (1) no shared-helper extraction needed, only the evaluation-side copy remains; (2) the `planRationale` reload continues to serve the surviving evaluation-side block, which runs later in the cycle after `CycleContextCoordinator` has populated the field, so no reload-simplification is available or needed; (3) the rationale-scope decision (Options A/B/C) is moot — only the evaluation-side consumer reads it now, and it already gets the first-wave rationale it needs. `GoalEntity` import retained (still used by `formatGoalList`). 218 protocol tests green.
  - **Gated by T3-BO outcome.** Scope depends on whether the evolution-side `planContextBlock()` survives the audit:
    - **If evolution-side block is removed:** no dedup needed (only one copy remains in `EvaluationProtocolContract`); `PlannerAgent.refreshGoalState()` no longer needs to reload `planRationale` for bootstrap evolution — only for the evaluator, which runs later in the cycle after `CycleContextCoordinator` has already populated the fields via the graph. Reload drops from three sites to zero.
    - **If evolution-side block is kept:** do the full cleanup below.
  - **Cleanup items (assuming block is kept):**
    1. **Extract shared helper.** `planContextBlock()` is copy-pasted verbatim between `EvaluationProtocolContract:527` and `EvolutionProtocolContract:577` with only the final instruction sentence differing. Extract to `ProtocolContextBlocks.planContextBlock(CycleContextData, PlanContextRole)` where `PlanContextRole` is `EVOLUTION` or `EVALUATION` and controls only the trailing instruction.
    2. **Simplify `PlannerAgent` same-cycle reload.** Currently `refreshGoalState()` reloads `planRationale` (line 497) by re-querying the parent goal from the graph. This is needed because bootstrap-cycle evolution runs after the planner in the same cycle and `CycleContextCoordinator` only populates `planRationale` at cycle start. Simplify by making `setPlanRationale()` directly mutate the in-memory `CycleContextData` the planner holds (or by having `injectOutcomeGoals()` return the rationale so the caller wires it into the context). Goal: eliminate the three-places reload pattern.
    3. **Rationale scope for single-subgoal replans.** Current behaviour: `setPlanRationale` is only called when `injected >= 2`. The rationale on the parent goal therefore reflects the FIRST planning wave that injected ≥2 subgoals, and subsequent stagnation-replan single-injection waves inherit it silently (good: first-wave intent persists; bad: a later narrower replan has no way to override with its own rationale). Decide:
       - **Option A:** Leave as-is. First-wave rationale is the durable intent; single-subgoal replans are recovery, not a new plan.
       - **Option B:** Let single injections supply a rationale too (parser accepts `PlanRationale:` for `injected >= 1`). Downside: noisy overwrites.
       - **Option C:** Only set rationale on the first-wave (lowest `planningRunId`) batch; ignore later overwrites entirely. Makes intent immutable for the subgoal's lifetime.
       - Recommendation pending audit: Option C aligns with the "first-wave is special" pattern already established by T1-CQ.
  - **Depends on:** **T3-BO** (audit outcome determines scope). Do not start before T3-BO concludes.

- [>] **T3-BS: Output-structure summary in evolution prompt — surface unused types and dangling references** (`EvolutionProtocolContract`, new `OutputStructureAnalyzer`, `CycleContextData`, `CycleContextCoordinator`) — **PARKED 2026-06-12 with the structural-awareness stack (T2-CM/CN/CP; same baseline evidence — no orphans/dangling refs in current terminal artifacts).** The dangling-references half is subsumed into **T4-BQ**'s evolution-prompt consumer (symbol-solver-backed, strictly better than the regex approach here); if T4-BQ ships, close this ticket as subsumed. Re-enters with the stack otherwise.
  - **Observed (2026-04-29 22:24 run):** End-of-run `firestarter/output` contained two structural holes the evolution prompt never told the LLM about:
    1. `CreateLoanRequest.java` — declared but unreferenced anywhere else in output. Multiple later mutations on `LoanController` and `LoanService` referenced it (visible in `firestarter/mutations/cycle-*/...`), but those mutations were rejected (T2-CJ band edge) and the type stayed orphaned. The LLM proposing those mutations had no signal that there was a *waiting consumer hole* it should be filling.
    2. `MemberService.java` line 18: `private BookService bookService;` — references a type that is not in output. `BookService.java` was proposed in cycle-1777495275437 (ACCEPTED but orphaned by T1-DC pre-fix) and never re-proposed because the planner moved on. The LLM working on adjacent subgoals had no signal that there was a *missing declaration* the project required.
  - **Root cause:** The evolution prompt currently includes the project structure summary (`DefaultProjectStructureSummarizer`) and the previousOutput contents per file, but no derived structural-integrity view. The LLM has to infer "what's missing" by reading every file end-to-end. With 17 output files this is unreliable; the LLM either misses the holes or invents work that does not match them.
  - **Fix — primary (`OutputStructureAnalyzer` + prompt block):** New service computes three lists from the *output* directory (regex on identifier boundaries — no AST):
    - `unusedTypes`: every `class|record|enum|interface X` declared in any output `.java`, where the simple name `X` has zero textual occurrences in any *other* output file. Exclude package-private utilities used only internally (require ≥1 declaration with `public`/`protected`).
    - `danglingReferences`: every PascalCase identifier used as a type position (field type, parameter type, return type, `new X(...)`, `extends X`, `implements X`, `throws X`, `@X(...)`) where `X` is not declared in any output `.java` and is not in a JDK/Spring stdlib whitelist (`String|Integer|Long|Double|Boolean|Object|List|Map|Set|Collection|Optional|...|@RestController|@Service|@Repository|@Autowired|@Valid|@Validated|...`).
    - `passiveOnlyTypes`: types declared in output where every external reference is *passive* (annotation argument `@Annot(X.class)`, class literal `X.class`, type-position-only generic `Class<X>` / `List<X>` without iteration, `import` statement) — no *active* site (`new X(...)`, `throw new X(...)`, method call on an X-typed value, instance-of check, cast). The 2026-04-30 run had four examples: `DuplicateEmailException`, `LoanAlreadyExistsException`, `MaxLoansExceededException`, `LoanAlreadyReturnedException` — each declared, each registered via `@ExceptionHandler(X.class)` in `GlobalExceptionHandler`, none ever thrown. The LLM sees them as "in use" because the handler exists and never proposes wiring the throw sites.
    Surface in the evolution prompt as a `--- STRUCTURAL HOLES ---` block when non-empty:
    ```
    --- STRUCTURAL HOLES ---
    Unused types in output (declared but no consumer):
    - CreateLoanRequest (src/main/java/com/example/demo/CreateLoanRequest.java)
    Dangling references in output (referenced but no declaration):
    - BookService (referenced from src/main/java/com/example/demo/MemberService.java line 18)
    Passive-only types (registered but never actively used — no `new`/`throw`/method-call site):
    - DuplicateEmailException (registered in GlobalExceptionHandler but no `throw new DuplicateEmailException(...)` anywhere)
    Resolving any of these reduces structural debt; prefer mutations that consume an unused type, supply a missing declaration, or activate a passive-only type.
    ```
    Cache the analyzer result on `CycleContextData.outputStructure` so the same computation feeds T2-CM (`StructuralIntegrityHeuristic`) and the prompt.
  - **Fix — secondary (compute frequency):** Run the analyzer once per cycle in `CycleContextCoordinator` (after the previousOutput is hydrated) — not on every prompt build. Cost is bounded by output file count, not LLM call frequency.
  - **Fix — tertiary (also in evaluation prompt, optional):** A "Structural integrity unchanged / improved / worsened by this diff" summary line in the evaluation prompt. Lightweight follow-up; not required for the primary value (which is at evolution time, the moment the LLM picks what to do).
  - **Changes:** New `analysis/structure/OutputStructureAnalyzer.java` with `analyze(Map<String,String> output) → OutputStructure(List<UnusedType>, List<DanglingReference>, List<PassiveOnlyType>)` (~150 lines). New `model/OutputStructure.java` record. `CycleContextData` — add `outputStructure` field. `CycleContextCoordinator` — call analyzer after `previousOutput` populated. `EvolutionProtocolContract.buildPromptBody` — append `structuralHolesBlock(ctx.outputStructure())`. Tests: `OutputStructureAnalyzerTest` covering (a) typed reference detection (field/param/return/extends/throws/annotation), (b) stdlib whitelist, (c) self-reference excluded, (d) inner classes, (e) generics — `List<Foo>` triggers Foo lookup, (f) passive-only — annotation-arg-only and class-literal-only references do not count as active use, (g) passive-to-active flip — adding a `throw new X(...)` removes X from `passiveOnlyTypes`.
  - **Depends on:** Nothing structurally — orthogonal to existing prompt blocks.
  - **Enables:** T2-CM (`StructuralIntegrityHeuristic`) reuses the same analyzer output. T4-AN-1 (compile gate) will catch the same problems with stronger evidence; T3-BS is the cheaper preventative that fires *before* the mutation is generated.
  - **Risk:** Regex-based reference detection has false positives on PascalCase identifiers that are not type references (e.g. method names like `findByEmailContaining` would not trigger but constants like `MAX_LOAN_LIMIT` could be misread by a sloppy regex). Mitigation: type-position-only detection (only scan after `:` `(` `extends` `implements` `throws` `new` `@` tokens), unit tests pinned to representative misclassifications. Long-term: replace with the AST in `analysis/diff/`.

  - **Fix — two complementary paths:**
    1. **Explicit skeleton (preferred for known projects):** if `firestarter/bootstrap/build/` exists, copy its contents (`pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `package.json`, etc.) into `output/` during bootstrap. User declares the build system explicitly by populating that directory. Zero LLM cost.
    2. **LLM-detected skeleton (fallback for goal-only seeds):** when no explicit skeleton exists, a small `BuildSystemBootstrap` LLM call ingests the seed text and root goal description, returns `{ buildSystem: "maven" | "gradle" | "npm" | …, skeletonFiles: [{path, content}] }`. Generated skeleton is written to `output/` before cycle 1.
  - **Configuration:** `autobuilder.bootstrap.build-system: auto` (default — try explicit first, fall back to LLM), `autobuilder.bootstrap.build-system: maven|gradle|npm|none` (override).
  - **Why T3 not T4:** the scaffolding (bootstrap service, file copy machinery) all exists; T3-BT just adds a build-system-aware path. Not new infrastructure — feature wiring.
  - **Acceptance:** sessions starting from a Java/Maven seed produce a working `pom.xml` before cycle 1's evolution runs; `BuildExecutor.execute` returns `COMPILE_OK` on the first invocation. Removes BUILD_FIX from session bootstrap unless the LLM seeds a wrong skeleton (caught by T4-AN-1 normally).
  - **Trade-off vs Chain H:** if T3-BT ships first, Chain H sees fewer BUILD_FIX cycles in real use — its per-cycle correctness work is still right, but the urgency drops. Doesn't replace Chain H (mid-session BUILD_FIX from a bad mutation still happens), just reduces frequency.
  - **Depends on:** T4-AN-5 if using LLM-detected path (`BuildToolProbe` for filename → tool mapping). Independent if explicit-skeleton-only.

## Tier 4 — New systems

- [ ] **T4-DE: parts of one graph as distinct IDENTITIES that talk to each other — agents with their own narrative and voice, and a view showing which part is speaking** (no code surface yet; successor to the cross-graph chain `T4-CN`/`T4-CM`/`T4-CS`) — **filed 2026-08-06 at the user's request, explicitly as VERY FAR FUTURE. Recorded so it is not lost, not queued.**
  - **The idea, in the user's framing:** connecting separated knowledge graphs was the earlier goal. A level beyond that is one graph whose REGIONS are identities — each bound to an agent, carrying its own narrative and voice — which then communicate with one another, with the browser showing which region is currently acting as the speaking identity.
  - **Why it is a real successor rather than a restatement:** the cross-graph chain asks how two graphs from different runs can be RECONCILED into one truth. This asks the opposite — how one graph can hold several standing viewpoints that stay distinct, disagree, and negotiate. Reconciliation collapses difference; this preserves it and makes it productive.
  - **What already exists that it would build on:** lineage separation (`T1-D`, 0 cross-edges, a lineage is a selectable subgraph), the orchestration-graph explorer and 3D browser (`T5-BG`, `T4-AM`), per-agent provenance on every node, and the narration work (`T5-BI` wants the loop to speak the model's own words rather than event templates — the nearest thing to "a voice" the project has).
  - **⚠ The obvious failure mode, recorded now so it is not discovered late:** giving regions names and voices is cheap and produces something that LOOKS alive while changing no decision. This project has a standing rule that a mechanism firing is not the same as it helping ([[feedback-activity-not-progress]]) and that prose relayed into a prompt is not an actuator ([[feedback-instrument-needs-an-actuator]]). An identity that cannot change an outcome is set dressing. **Any first slice must name what an identity DECIDES that the undivided graph would decide differently.**
  - **Preconditions, none currently met:** layer D of wave 2 is empty — nothing in the running loop consults cross-run knowledge at all yet (`T4-CT`), and `T6-I` has never tested whether accumulated experience improves outcomes. Identities that negotiate over knowledge nobody consults would be a second storey on an unbuilt ground floor.
  - **Status: PARKED.** No design, no slice, no gate. Re-entry belongs after `T4-CT` has one consumer and `T6-I` has a verdict.

Full design in [[project-target-domain-plugin-design]] — read it before touching this.**

- [ ] **T4-DC: A controller catches exception types its service never throws, so every domain error falls through to the handler of last resort** (`analysis/wiring/WiringFactsAnalyzer` — same home and prompt path as `T3-BX`'s `statusRiskFacts`) — **filed 2026-07-30 from run `2026-07-30_18-39-00`; ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED the same hour after comparing against the 23/23 artifact of `2026-07-24_10-24-15`.**
  - **🔴 THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS THE SYMPTOM.** I filed this as "a catch-all `@ExceptionHandler(Exception.class)` flattens every domain outcome to 500". The catch-all is real and it IS where the 500s are produced, but it is the last stop, not the cause. The controller in that run *does* map statuses — it catches and branches to 404/409/422/400. **Those catch blocks are unreachable.**
  - **The cause, in two lines of the artifact:** `LoanService` throws `RuntimeException` for all six domain errors; `LoanController` catches `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`. Both are SUBCLASSES of what is thrown, so neither catch can ever match, every domain error propagates, and the handler of last resort answers 500 with the correct message in the body.
  - **Measured across four artifacts, and the invariant discriminates cleanly:**

    | run | smoke | thrown | caught | thrown covered? |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | `20260724_10-24-15` | **23/23** | 8 specific domain types | the same 8 | yes |
    | `2026-07-30_04-56-38` | 18/23 | `IllegalArgumentException`, `IllegalStateException` | the same two | yes |
    | `2026-07-30_08-00-00` | 18/23 | 6 specific domain types | `Exception` only | yes, but collapsed to one status |
    | `2026-07-30_18-39-00` | **14/23** | `RuntimeException` | `IllegalArgumentException`, `IllegalStateException` | **NO — zero overlap** |

  - **What the 23/23 run did differently, concretely.** Eight named exception classes (`NotFoundException`, `BookNotAvailableException`, `MemberHasTooManyLoansException`, `DuplicateEmailException`, …), each thrown by a private validate method and each caught explicitly in the controller with its own status. **No global handler at all, no `@ResponseStatus`** — the mapping lives beside the logic that raises it, so there is nothing to fall through to and nothing to get out of step.
  - **Capability — a statically checkable structural fact, no framework knowledge required:** for each caller/callee pair, compare the exception type NAMES thrown against those caught. A callee throwing a type no caller catches means the catch blocks are dead and the outcome is decided elsewhere. Name comparison alone (no type hierarchy) fires on `18-39-00` and on `08-00-00` — the two artifacts whose status mapping is architecturally broken — and stays silent on the two whose sets match. Self-gating: a project that throws nothing yields no fact.
  - **Why this is a DETECTION gap, not a model-quality one:** the loop wrote correct domain logic, correct messages, a service, a controller with per-status branches, and an error handler. Every part looks right in isolation. Nothing anywhere asks whether the parts agree.
  - **Pairs with `T4-DB`, does not duplicate it.** T4-DB makes the loop OBSERVE a wrong status at runtime; this says WHY. The probe reports "expected 404, got 500"; this reports "the catches are unreachable, so nothing maps it". The repair needs both.
  - **BUILT 2026-07-30 (`ac3a651`) — and the build was NOT the detector, because the detector already existed.** Running the shipped `statusRiskFacts` over the 14/23 artifact returns, verbatim: *"Status mappings exist, but thrown exception type(s) [RuntimeException] are not covered by any mapped type — those failures bypass the handlers and surface as 500s."* It is correct, it discriminates, and **T3-BX had already wired it into the evolution prompt.** Grepping the run's log: the block rendered 3 times and that fact appeared once.
    - **🔴 THE DEFECT WAS TIMING, AND THE NUMBER IS STARK.** `statusRiskFacts` ran the type-level comparison only `if (anyThrow && anyStatusMapping)`. The service threw `RuntimeException` from early on, but no mapping existed until a `GlobalExceptionHandler` was written — **at cycle 24 of 25**. The fact then reached an evolution prompt whose subgoal was literally *"the application runs, but spec-named endpoint(s) fail at runtime: GET /loans answers 500"*, **one cycle before the deadline**. So "the loop was told and shipped it anyway" is too harsh for this run: it was told, correctly and precisely, with one cycle left.
    - **The same split as T3-BX, one branch deeper in the same method.** `analyze()` has always emitted the mapping-free half (*"Exceptions are thrown but no HTTP status mapping was found"*), but `analyze()` feeds the criteria verifier. Both halves now reach evolution, sharing one constant so they cannot drift apart again.
    - **A naive version would have misread the BEST artifact in the corpus.** Counting only annotations as "a mapping" makes the 23/23 run — no advice class, no `@ResponseStatus`, eight named types each caught in the controller beside the logic that raised them — look entirely unmapped. A catch clause that yields a status now counts; one that swallows does not. Fixing that also turned `04-56-38` from a false positive to silent.
    - **MEASURED FIRING PATTERN, which is NOT the one this ticket predicted.** The DoD guessed "fires on `18-39-00` and `08-00-00`, silent on the other two". Actual, over the four real artifacts: **the 14/23 tree with its handler removed (its pre-cycle-24 state) now fires where it previously produced nothing** · `04-56-38` silent · `08-00-00` silent (its types ARE covered — by a mapping to 500, which the positive fact already reports) · **the 23/23 fires once, on a true but behaviourally inert fact** (an `IllegalArgumentException` thrown in model setters whose controllers validate and throw a named type first, so the path is never reached). Recorded rather than tuned away: the statement is accurate and acting on it costs nothing.
    - 7 tests, suite **2351/0/5**.
  - **🔴 FIELD RUN `2026-07-30_21-25-43` — THE TIMING HALF IS MET AND IT EXPOSES THAT TIMING WAS NOT THE ONLY PROBLEM.** Status-path facts reached the evolution prompt by **cycle ~5–7** (against cycle 24 of 25 in the previous run), rendered 3 times carrying 9 validation-trigger facts. Evolution then ran at cycles 6, 7 and 8 — each producing an ACCEPTED mutation — and the artifact still has **zero** `@Valid`/`@Validated` in any controller while `Book`, `Member` and `Loan` all declare field constraints. The constraints are inert and the loop has been told so nine times.
    - **But the honest reading is NOT "the loop ignored it".** The active subgoal across all four cycles was *"Implement POST /books returning 201 with the created book"*. The fact concerns `BookController.createBook()` — the same endpoint — but a different requirement: `@Valid` is not needed for the 201 happy path. **The agent behaved correctly within its mandate.** The fact was relevant to the code in front of it and irrelevant to the outcome it was asked for.
    - **So two runs now show the same gap through two different facts.** Run `18-39-00`: the fact arrived at cycle 24 with a subgoal that DID match it, and there was no time. Run `21-25-43`: the fact arrives at cycle 5 with time to spare, and no subgoal matches it. **Neither run had a work item for the fact.** A structural fact with a named cause is advisory prose in a prompt written for a differently-scoped task, and prose does not survive the agent moving on.
    - **This is precisely what `T4-DA`'s consumer 2 was designed for and deliberately left unwired**, and it is the same shape as `T2-ET`'s replan half: the loop's problem is not seeing or being told, it is that nothing DURABLE is created from what it sees. Recorded here rather than acted on — wiring an actuator on two observations would repeat the mistake this project has reverted twice.
  - **DoD:** ~~the fire/silent pattern in the table~~ — superseded by the measured pattern above. The **timing half is MET** (facts at cycle ~5 vs 24). The remaining half — a status check flipping after the fact fires — is **blocked on there being a work item to carry it**, which is the finding above rather than a defect in this change.

This, not `T4-CO`, is the measured 18→23 gap.**

    | failing check | requirement | why no probe exists |
    |---|---|---|

    | `[15]` `POST /loans` unknown `memberId` → 404 | same | same |
    | `[19]` 4th concurrent loan → 422 | bounded-count rule | abstains by design — reaching the limit needs N valid loans and a bound stated only in prose |

    And every check that passes is one it CAN build: 400 by empty body on a non-parameterized POST (`[2]`,`[3]`,`[4]`,`[10]`), 404 by an unused id on a parameterized GET (`[7]`,`[12]`), 409 by a repeated POST (`[9]`). `[16]` (409 on `/loans`) moves between pass and fail, consistent with a collision probe that depends on a derivable Loan body.

Harder and it must be honest about the setup: each loan needs a DIFFERENT book or the collision rule fires first and the probe reports a false contradiction, which is the harm class that got two steering changes reverted in July. Abstain unless the whole setup is derivable.

  - **✅ GATE ANSWERED 2026-08-04, and it named a different slice than this ticket did.** Over 186 criteria in one run: **probed 55.9% · unprobeable 29.0% · transport 15.1% · unparsed 0.0%**. `unparsed` at zero across every firing settles it — the gap is entirely missing/declining shapes, not authoring, so `T2-EX`'s premise has largely dissolved.
