    - **Comparing a BROKEN run (11/23) against the 23/23 run separates state from capability.** The `404 POST` abstentions (checks 14/15's shape) are **3 on the broken tree and 0 on the healthy one** — correct abstention while the model class does not yet exist, not a missing feature. What survives on a healthy artifact is **10 creates · 3 × 422 · 3 × 409-on-a-parameterized-path · 2 × 200-on-a-parameterized-POST**.
    - **🔴 AND ~15 OF THOSE 18 HAVE ONE ROOT CAUSE: no body the application will accept.** The creates are the exclusion I made today (`derivedBody` yields `{"email":"value"}`, which a correct app refuses); the two parameterized shapes need a valid body for the same reason. **So the remaining verification gap is not many missing shapes — it is one missing ingredient.**
    - **The mechanism for it already exists and is deliberately off.** `autobuilder.build.criterion-probe.llm-fallback-enabled` (default false) covers "the shapes the deterministic path abstains on"; `T4-CY` disabled it after measuring 29.5 and 14.9 minutes of a 90-minute run consumed by synchronous calls inside cycles, and recorded the condition for using it safely: **"affordable at the completion edge, and not inside a cycle."** That is the next move for this ticket — not the bounded-count probe, and not more deterministic shapes.
  - **✅ BUILT 2026-08-05 — AND THE FIRST RUN TO EXERCISE IT DIED, which is what bought the mitigation.** The per-call permission was threaded through `BootGate` (four callers: `GoalPlannerService` is the edge; the other three run per cycle and keep the deterministic-only path). Then run `2026-08-05_20-58-50` reached the edge with **49 criteria, 30 unprobed**, fired 30 synchronous calls at a local model already returning timeouts since 21:52, and: **the first network error is timestamped in the SAME SECOND as the sweep (22:07:17) → five consecutive failures → circuit breaker open → run dead at 22:07:32.**
    - **T4-CY had measured this exact hazard and switched the path off.** I read *"affordable at the completion edge"* as permission and never asked how many calls the edge would make. It is true of a handful and false of thirty.
    - **Capped at 5 consultations per sweep** (`MAX_MODEL_FALLBACKS_PER_SWEEP`). Not a tuning knob — the number was bought with a run. The fallback exists to recover a few high-value criteria the deterministic path cannot express, not to re-ask the model about everything it declined.
    - **⚠ TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN MITIGATION, both caught before shipping.** The first cut decremented the budget only when the model FAILED to return a probe, leaving successful calls unbudgeted — the cost is the call, not its outcome; the deterministic path is now tried explicitly first and the budget spent on the consultation itself. And the original change logged the fallback at DEBUG only, so the dying run could not answer whether the mechanism had fired at all; it is at INFO with its latency now, which is also the number T4-CY cared about.
    - **The run still scored 18/23 (strict 18/23, nothing discounted)** before the breaker ended it — the damage was to its length, not its work.
    - **Open:** whether 5 calls is survivable, and whether the fallback converts abstentions into probes at all. Needs a run that reaches root closure.
- [ ] **T4-DA: Nothing ever asks whether the subgoals, taken together, still solve the seed — and the agents are never told** (`analysis/coverage` new bundled comparator, `protocol/*` prompt blocks for planner/evolution/analysis, `goal/GoalPlannerService` as a secondary consumer) — **filed 2026-07-30 (user's framing, and the framing is the ticket).**
  - **THE POINT IS COMMUNICATION, NOT GATING.** The reason to compute this is to *tell the agents what the situation is, so they know what to do*. The readout into the prompts is the deliverable; raising work items from it is a secondary consumer that may or may not be wired. A version of this that only injects goals and renders nothing has missed the ticket.
  - **This is the T3-BX shape again, pre-empted.** There, a rule had been computing the right fact for months and its output reached no agent that could act on it — `analyze()` went to the criteria verifier and nowhere else, while the only analyzer path into the evolution prompt returned 0 on all six corpora. The 2026-07-30 frozen series generalised it: *the loop was told and shipped it anyway*; the constraint on this codebase is connecting and acting on facts it already computes, not acquiring new ones. So the design order here is **readout first, actuator second** — the same order [[project-t4bz-design-note]] imposed on the signal work.
  - **The gap, measured 2026-07-30 (not asserted — the code and three frozen runs were read):**
    - `CoverageRetrospectiveService` is the ONLY domain-neutral seed-vs-plan comparator, and it filters to `COMPLETED || GIVEN_UP`, capped at 25. **The active plan is invisible to it.** It answers "did the work I finished cover the seed", never "does what I am planning cover the seed". A run that terminates no goals asks nothing at all.
    - Its two call sites are both terminal edges: `GoalPlannerService:2842` (root closure, behind `if (anyActive) return`) and `:3228` (give-up). Never periodic, so drift has no detection latency shorter than the run itself.
    - **Criteria are not in the comparison at all** — the prompt is seed text against goal DESCRIPTIONS. Nothing anywhere asks whether each seed requirement has a criterion that would prove it. The nearest thing was `T4-CO` consumer 1, never built. So "do all the criteria exist" is unowned.
    - **Direction.** `SpecTraceability.classify` maps subgoal → seed (*is this work justified?*), one subgoal at a time. Nothing maps seed → whole subgoal set (*is every part of the seed claimed by something?*). Drift lives in the second direction and it is the one nothing computes.
    - `EndpointSurfaceQuery` does compare seed to built code, but it is category-specific (REST endpoints) — the same objection that got `T4-CO` sent back for a redesign, and not a substitute for a general check.
    - **Field measurement:** across the three frozen runs (`04-56-38`, `06-28-19`, `08-00-00`, 122 cycles), `coverage-review` fired 8/8/6 times and **every single firing was T4-CZ's entry-point item**. Zero seed-coverage comparisons in three complete runs, because all three ended on the deadline with an active backlog.
  - **Capability:** one bundled check taking the root description, **all** subgoals regardless of status, and their acceptance criteria. It answers two questions and renders both: **the unclaimed question** — which parts of the seed no subgoal claims — and **the unprovable question** — which claimed parts carry no criterion that would prove them. Domain-neutral by construction — it reads the seed as text and the plan as text, and holds no opinion about endpoints, status codes, or any other category ([[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]]). A seed it cannot decompose yields an empty readout and no opinion.
  - **Consumer 1 (the point):** a compact block in the planner, evolution and analysis prompts stating the coverage situation — what is unclaimed, what is unprovable. Enumerated name-anchored lines, not a payload dump ([[project-t4ap-prompt-audit]]). This is what lets an agent *choose* differently rather than be corrected afterwards.
  - **Consumer 2 (secondary):** unclaimed seed parts as ordinary work items through `injectCoverageGaps`, so T1-DE dedup and T1-FG per-gap idempotency come free. Recorded-not-applied first, per the T4-CC principle; wire it only after the readout has been seen in the field.
  - **Timing:** periodic on an interval like T4-CY, not bound to an edge. The whole defect is that today's version only speaks when the run is already trying to finish.
  - **Two hard constraints from the record, both paid for:**
    - **Plan-and-text only — no build, package or boot dependency.** That distinction is exactly why `T4-CZ` survived (a pure in-memory scan of sources already on the cycle context) and `T2-EQ` was reverted twice (a whole-project property demanded of a partial skeleton). Early cycles are a partial skeleton by design.
    - **The finding text must be stable across firings or it mints twins.** Run `04-56-38` produced two ACTIVE copies of one goal from findings 1286 characters long differing in about forty — timestamp, pid, thread name, ephemeral port — which defeated the suppression guard, T1-DE paraphrase filtering and T1-FG idempotency at once, all three keying on that text. Backlog inflation is the one property separating every good run from every bad one.
  - **Relation to `T4-CO`:** T4-CO's consumer 1 ("every endpoint with a spec-stated code carries a spec-stamped criterion") is the category-specific instance of this ticket's **unprovable question**. If this is built general, T4-CO's steering half likely folds into it and only the extraction half remains distinct — check before building both ([[feedback-one-invariant-one-home]]).
  - **DoD:** the comparator + the prompt readout landed and rendering on a real run; the readout's content verified against that run's actual GoalStack by hand (not merely "it fired" — [[feedback-activity-not-progress]]); finding-text stability pinned by a regression test; suite green. Field watch: a run where the readout names an unclaimed seed part and the next planner response claims it. Consumer 2 stays unwired until then.
  - **🔴 SCOPING MEASUREMENT 2026-07-30, taken right after filing — THIS TICKET IS NOT THE 18→23 GAP, and whoever builds it must not carry that expectation.** The frozen series' GoalStacks were read directly. In all three runs the status-code requirements **exist as live work items at the deadline**: `The endpoint returns HTTP 409 when POST /loans attempts to loan an already-loaned book` (ACTIVE), `… HTTP 422 when a member tries to loan more than 3 books` (ACTIVE), `… HTTP 404 when POST /loans has non-existent bookId` — **10 / 5 / 6 status-code items still ACTIVE** across the three runs. The probes fired and contradicted them (run 1: 5 probe passes, `contradicted` 3/3/1/1/2), the contradictions became goals of their own (`the application runs, but acceptance criteria fail when exercised against it: "POST /loans returns H…"`), and T3-BX rendered the static cause into the evolution prompt. **Nothing was uncovered, unclaimed, unprovable or unsaid.** The runs ended on the 90-minute deadline with the right work queued and unfinished.

But it is insurance against a recurrence, not the current ceiling.

Rendered block on run `08-00-00`'s plan: 13 unclaimed, 1 unprovable, ~1900 characters.

Recall was preferred because the consumer is a prompt a reader can dismiss in a glance; were this ever to gate anything, that trade would have to be revisited.

      - Ordering by how far the plan already engages with a clause does lift half-articulated requirements above framing prose, but **not into any fixed number of leading places**. It orders; it does not filter. The Javadoc claiming otherwise was written before the measurement and corrected.
      - Exact token matching made `list` and `lists` disagree, **manufacturing findings out of morphology alone**. Terms now reduce to a canonical form applied to both sides.
    - **🔴 THE FIRST FIELD FIRING FOUND A DEFECT OF MINE IN UNDER FIVE MINUTES, and it was the silent kind.** Run `2026-07-30_17-32-12` logged `0 unclaimed` against a tree holding only the root. Cause: `getAllGoals()` returns the root ALONGSIDE the subgoals and **the root's description IS the seed**, so every seed term was in the plan vocabulary by construction and nothing could ever be reported unclaimed. The check would have answered "no drift" for the rest of the project's life while looking healthy in the log — the same instrument-reporting-confidently-about-the-wrong-subject shape as T6-A, T6-C, T6-E and T6-F. Fixed in `1dc6521` by keying on the description rather than on `GoalType` (a resumed run's adopted root, or an item pasted from the spec, has the same effect); a plan that is only the specification restated now yields no opinion rather than false reassurance. Two regression tests. **The offline validation had missed it because the Python prototype excluded the root by array index — the production call did not.**
    - **FIELD-VERIFIED after the fix (run `2026-07-30_17-37-09`):** `15 unclaimed, 1 claimed-but-unprovable` against 6–7 goals, and the block renders into the prompts with its truncation announced (`3 further clause(s) omitted here, least-engaged first`). Content checked by hand against the run's own goal tree.
    - **🔴 THE SECOND FIELD FIRING FOUND A WORSE DEFECT OF MINE, and this one made the run sterile (`86b6055`).** Run `2026-07-30_17-37-09`: **9 mutations ACCEPTED, 0 merged, 38 `mutation_meta_persist_failed`.** `SeedCoverageReadout.isEmpty()` is serialized as a property `empty` and the record's canonical constructor has no parameter for it, so reading `meta.json` back threw — and `MutationSnapshotService` does not merely lose the file, it falls back to writing a fresh one with **`mutationState=REJECTED`**. Every acceptance became a rejection. Any run carrying this could not merge anything.
      - **The convention already existed and I did not follow it.** All four other records on `CycleContextData` carry `@JsonIgnore` on exactly such an accessor, and `T1-EV` is a closed ticket for this same defect class on `CompileAuthorErrors`. What was missing was anything that ENFORCED it, which is why the fifth was free to reintroduce it — the shape where the invariant has a home but no guard.
      - **So the fix is the annotation plus the enforcement.** `CycleContextDataRoundTripTest` walks the context's record components by reflection and fails on any accessor Jackson would write that the constructor could not read — keyed on the TYPE, not on a remembered list, so a record added later is covered without editing a test. **Verified non-vacuous** by removing the annotation and watching it fail with the offending accessor named ([[feedback-verify-diff-is-substantive]]).

Registered as `t4da-clause-claimed-after-readout` with the **decision rule stated in advance**: three or more readout-enabled runs averaging ≥1 closed clause supports the mechanism; averaging 0 refutes it and **this readout should be re-read as inert prompt weight** ([[feedback-coverage-guard-experiment]] shape).
    - **🔴 THE COST SIDE IS MEASURED AND IT IS NOT FREE.** `scripts/prompt_block_report.py` on the first readout-enabled run: the `SPECIFICATION COVERAGE` block is **~665 est tokens per call, 23% of the evolution prompt** (though only 2.3% of the run's total prompt tokens, which are dominated by evaluation). Its median cycle was **162s against 130/135/140s** for the three controls — **+16–25%**, n=1 and confounded by ordinary model variance, but the direction is consistent and the mechanism is plausible. the watch records median cycle time alongside closed clauses and judges NET effect. This is the T4-CY lesson applied before rather than after: that mechanism was proven useful and still had to be switched off on cost.
      - **🔴 CORRECTION, same day, from the token accounting — I ATTRIBUTED THE SLOWDOWN TO THIS BLOCK AND THE NUMBERS DO NOT SUPPORT IT.** Over that run: total prompt tokens **200109**, of which **evaluation is 144910 (72%)** and evolution only 19362 (10%). The block is **4658 — 2.3% of the run's prompt tokens**. A 2.3% increase cannot plausibly produce a 16–25% cycle-time increase. The observed slowdown is far more likely ordinary generation variance, and the run confirmed the mechanism directly minutes later by stalling in `LLMClient` timeout retries (readTimeout escalating 120s → 180s) with the model server alive, loaded and at 85% GPU — a long generation, not a wedge.
      - **What survives the correction:** the block is genuinely 24% of the EVOLUTION prompt, which is a real dilution risk for the agent that writes code, and that is worth watching. What does not survive is the framing that it costs the run eight cycles. **The cost side now looks small; the benefit side is still n=1.**
      - **Deliberately NOT tuned on this evidence.** The obvious reduction — give evolution only the clauses near what it is working on, since its stated use is narrower than the planner's — is a design change on n=1, and the block is already the shape the T4-AP audit found earns its tokens (enumerated, name-anchored) rather than the shape that loses.
    - **✅ THE WATCH HAS ITS THREE RUNS AND MEETS ITS OWN DECISION RULE (2026-07-31).** Clauses closed against the `df2a907` control, whose per-run baseline is **0 of 11**: run 1 **1**, run 2 **2**, run 3 **4** — mean **2.3**, and the rule fixed in advance was *"three or more readout-enabled runs averaging ≥1 supports the mechanism; averaging 0 refutes it."* **Supported.** The trend also runs the right way as the loop gets more cycles to act with.
    - **AND THE SUSPICION THAT THIS MECHANISM COST 3 SMOKE POINTS IS RETIRED BY THE SAME RUN.** The two runs that scored 14 and 15 had T4-DA enabled and 25 and 35 cycles; run 3 had it enabled and **114 cycles, scoring 18/23** — the frozen-series baseline. Same flag, same build family, three times the cycles, and the score recovered. **The 14/15 scores were throughput-starved, not readout-caused** — which is what `T6-J` independently established and is why the switch was added rather than the mechanism removed. Keeping the switch anyway: it is what made the question answerable.
    - **Residual:** none for the watch. The remaining DoD half — a planner response acting on a clause the readout named — is now supported by the clause-closure trend rather than a single observation. **Watch also that the readout is nearly all-unclaimed in the first cycles** (an early plan articulates almost nothing, which is true but low-information); if it proves to be noise rather than steering at that stage, the answer is a floor on plan size, not a change to the comparison.
    - **What the same read points at instead:** backlog convergence on a known defect. Run `04-56-38` ended with **23 ACTIVE goals**, five of them reading `Implement a single behaviour of [Fix LoanController error handling for POST /loans to return HTTP 40…]` — **one repair split five ways, none finished** (the T2-EJ divide-and-conquer fallback). It had the fewest merges (16 vs 20/20) and fewest COMPLETED (8 vs 11/13) of the three and scored the same 18. Runs 2 and 3 ended with 11 ACTIVE and zero such splits. Backlog inflation on a single defect is the mechanism to measure next; it is the one property that has separated every good run from every bad one.

- [n] **T4-CP: Internal drift reflection — the loop notices mid-run when it is regressing from its best state and acts to stop burning later-stage tokens** (`core/lifecycle` + `core/persistence`; a periodic internal self-check, NOT an external smoke call) — **filed 2026-07-24** from the T6-A conversation (user idea, sharpened over several turns). Squarely the [[project-introspection-as-north-star]] direction made concrete: a loop with a self-model it consults before spending more effort.
  - **The idea (user's own framing):** not "which snapshot to keep" — a periodic internal reflection asking "are we still on track, or drifting significantly from where we were?" The payoff is EFFICIENCY: catch a trajectory that peaked early and has been sliding, and course-correct (preserve the peak / flag / consider early-stop or replan) instead of pouring tokens into a late stage that has wandered off. Explicitly internal reflection, NOT external results.
  - **Why NOT external smoke (settled at filing):** the smoke yardstick (`smoke23`) is deliberately outside the loop — the independent referee that catches the loop fooling itself (the whole false-completion history). If the loop SELECTS by the smoke score, smoke stops being independent (Goodhart). So the reflection must trend an INTERNAL signal.
  - **First design question (open — decide on evidence):** what is the trustworthy internal "promising" measure? Lead candidate = **criteria-pass count trend** (how many grounded goal criteria hold, over cycles — the most absolute internal signal, already computed at some edges via `CriteriaVerificationService`). Alternatives: evaluation/heuristic score trajectory (per-mutation, noisier), `RootConvergenceTracker`. KEY RELAXATION: drift detection needs only the TREND ("peaked, then sliding K checks"), not an accurate absolute — a weaker, more achievable ask than scoring the artifact correctly, and it sidesteps the known unreliability of the loop's internal measures at the finish line.
  - **Net-token-saving is the whole justification, and it is UNPROVEN — this is the reason for the gate.** Saves tokens only if (a) the check is cheap (reuse already-computed signals, NOT an extra LLM reflection call — spending tokens to save tokens defeats it) and (b) late-stage drift-into-waste is a real, common pattern. (a) is a design choice; (b) is empirical and currently unknown.
  - **EVIDENCE-GATED on T6-B (hard):** T6-A's per-run drift fields + the T6-B batch view exist to establish exactly (b) — whether runs systematically peak early and burn a long drift tail. This ticket is the natural CONSUMER of that data: the drift shape decides what to trend, how far a drop before acting, and which action (preserve-peak / replan / early-stop). Building the mechanism before the drift data is guessing thresholds — do not start until T6-B shows a drift-and-waste pattern worth acting on. If the data shows late cycles are productive-but-slow (not drifting), this ticket does not get built.
  - **DoD (when unblocked):** a cheap per-cycle-or-periodic internal drift signal (reusing existing computed quality signals); a stated regression trigger (relative, per [[feedback-relative-thresholds]]) validated against the T6-B drift corpus; a chosen action on trigger; unit tests; suite green; a field run showing a drifting trajectory caught earlier than the current halt would. Residual "generate executable acceptance tests from accumulated knowledge" idea stays a NOTE pointing at `CriteriaGroundingService` / the deferred cross-run KB — the research-grade frontier, not this ticket.
  - **EVIDENCE GATE RESOLVED **NEGATIVE** 2026-07-25 (Opus 5) — DEFERRED `[>]`, do NOT build as filed. The gate did its job: it cost one scripts-only session instead of a mechanism.** T6-B shipped the same session and measured the drift shape over **237 substantial runs**; full data in the T6-B closure append + `~/Documents/autobuilder/analysis_T6-B_T4-CP-gate_20260725`. Marked `[>]` not `[x]` per [[feedback-capability-gap-not-prohibition]] — a revisable gap, not a permanent ban. Four findings against this ticket's own stated decision rule ("if the data shows late cycles are productive-but-slow (not drifting), this ticket does not get built"):
    - ① **The premise is not the common shape.** "Peaked early and has been sliding" — the median run stays productive to **95%** of its length (p90 = 1.00, i.e. productive to the last cycle), and GOAL_FULFILLED runs have a median tail of **1 cycle** with 3/36 churning. There is no population of early-peaking runs to catch.
    - ② **The saving ceiling is too small to justify the mechanism.** Post-productivity tails hold **7.3%** of all tokens (6.1% counting injections as productive; 14.6% under the strictest `merge` reading), and **100% of that burn sits in runs that never fulfilled** — drift reflection would not have saved a single fulfilled run's tokens. A trend needs K confirmation checks before acting, so realized saving is a fraction of the ceiling, minus the check's own cost. Net-token-saving — this ticket's whole justification, explicitly flagged UNPROVEN at filing — does not clear.
    - ③ **It would duplicate a working mechanism.** `RootConvergenceTracker` (T4-I root slice) already is the run-level no-progress brake and currently fires correctly (four most recent corpora: bounded resets, max counter 19, no runaway; 07-15/07-16 long-tail runs both reached the stall halt). The residual tail is that brake's **designed detection cost** — 20 cycles per stall window, reopened by verify-before-pause — not a missing capability. Historical runaway tails (298/252 cycles) trace to two reset defects both already fixed in wave 1.
    - ④ **Half the tail population is the wrong pathology.** 43% of tails are `idle` (livelock: ticking, barely attempting) — cost is wall-clock, not tokens, and it belongs to the brake/stagnation family, not to a quality-trend reflection.
    - **RE-ENTRY (any one of):** (a) token telemetry coverage grows well past the current 36 runs AND tail burn holds above ~15% of tokens **on runs that do fulfil** — i.e. the waste stops being confined to already-failing runs; (b) a field run shows the existing brake failing to bound a tail again (reset paths regressing); (c) if token efficiency becomes the target anyway, the cheaper move is **tuning the existing brake's window** — a T2/config question with a measurable knob, and note its limit is a fixed `20` while the data says tail cost is proportional to the run's own cycle cost, so [[feedback-relative-thresholds]] applies to it.
    - **Instrument survives regardless:** `scripts/drift_aggregate.py` re-answers this in one command on any future batch, so re-entry is a measurement, not a re-investigation.

- [x] **T4-CC: Self-verifying blocker work items — a gate-born BUILD_FIX carries its originating gate as the decisive acceptance check** (`goal` blocker-creation sites / `BlockerTypes` metadata, `agent/evaluation/EvaluationAgent` + `HeuristicNegotiator` decisive path, `core/build` PackageGate/BootGate/TestRunGate/BuildExecutor against the candidate workspace) — **filed 2026-07-16** from the afternoon run: the run halted GOAL_EXHAUSTED **90 seconds after the model produced the correct fix**. The packaging gate had created `[BUILD_FIX] Make the application packageable… Unable to find main class`; evolution (after a noDiff-forced divergence that WORKED) proposed exactly `DemoApplication.java` with `@SpringBootApplication`+`main`, the compile probe passed — and the LLM evaluator rejected it at 0.35 with a self-contradictory criteria line ("the build failure is due to missing main class declaration, which is not resolved by this change" — the change IS the declaration). Zero heuristics contributed (`heuristic_result` 0× that cycle; DeterministicScoreHeuristic abstains below the soft-band floor on LLM REJECTED). Two cycles later the injection budget exhausted. **A false REJECT at the completion edge — the evaluation-precision ceiling in the reject direction, the inverse of false-completion #3.**
  - **Principle:** the blocker was BORN from a deterministic command whose pass/fail is the ground truth — yet acceptance was delegated to a static LLM opinion. Counter hallucination by narrowing where the assessment applies, not by improving the assessment: where a perfect actuator exists, the actuator decides. ([[project-completion-edge-gates]] "every diagnosis needs an actuator" — here every gate-born blocker already HAS one and doesn't use it.)
  - **Build:** when a gate/probe creates a blocker work item, stamp the originating check's identity on the goal (metadata, template-single-homed in `BlockerTypes` like the T1-FF prefixes). During evaluation of a mutation on such a subgoal whose compile probe is green, re-run the originating gate against the candidate workspace: PASS → decisive ACCEPT (the LLM assessment recorded, not applied — the exact mirror of T4-BW's defect-marked decisive REJECT); FAIL → decisive REJECT carrying the gate's actual output as the reason (replacing the LLM's guess with evidence, which also upgrades what T4-BX relays). Cost is bounded: one extra gate run only on gate-born blockers that already probe green.

A work item was raised from that contradiction and decomposed into one child — **the very subgoal that had closed falsely**, *"Implement input validation for Book model…"*, still marked COMPLETED. With its only child claiming success the parent produced no merge and was retired: `resolution: exhausted after 1 cycles without merge` → **GIVEN_UP**.
      - So the loop observed correctly, raised correctly, decomposed correctly, and then **abandoned the repair because a leaf lied to it**. Every link works except the one that closes a leaf on a model's reading of the source.

      - *STATUS-PATH FACTS: "Request body Book declares field constraints, but `BookController.createBook()` binds it without a validation trigger — the declared constraints are not enforced"*.
      - One says the work is done; the other says it does not work. A reader resolving that will reasonably trust the bookkeeping and treat the fact as stale — which is exactly the observed behaviour, 42 renderings with `@Valid` never added.
      - **Note what this exonerates.** The domain-specific fact is CORRECT, and the loop demonstrably acts on this class of fact: later in the same run it built a five-handler `GlobalExceptionHandler` (`BusinessRuleViolationException`→409, three `*NotFoundException`→404, `IllegalArgumentException`→400) mapping every type it throws — the 23/23 architecture. **The confusion is not the ecosystem knowledge; it is the loop's own bookkeeping asserting something false beside something true.**

    - **A CHEAP FIX EXISTS AND I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD IT — recorded so the reasoning is available, not lost.** No boot is needed to catch this closure. The static fact (*"Book declares field constraints, but BookController.createBook() binds it without a validation trigger"*) and the criterion (*"POST /books with title longer than 120 characters returns HTTP 400"*) are in **direct contradiction, statically**, and both were already computed — the fact 27 times. A check that refuses to mark a subgoal COMPLETED while a status-path fact contradicts its criteria costs milliseconds and needs nothing running.

Building it now would deepen exactly the debt that direction is meant to stop, to save one ticket's wait. **This belongs on the far side of the plug-in seam — it is a good candidate for the first thing the "structural risk facts" and "requirement extraction" seams are asked to support together**, which also makes it a useful test of whether that boundary is in the right place.
    - **Re-entry condition for this ticket's DoD (which reads "needs a field firing"): this is the firing, in the negative** — it shows the capability's value by the cost of its absence at the subgoal edge. Design constraint before anyone builds it: probing every subgoal closure needs a booted artifact, exactly the mid-run expense `T4-CY` was disabled for once already. The cheap form is to probe only criteria the parser can already turn into a request, and only when the artifact is booted for another reason.

- [ ] **T5-BJ: No index on `Goal` — every dedup call full-scans every goal of every lineage** (`graph/goal/Neo4jGoalGraphService`, schema DDL alongside `Neo4jDeferredMutationGraphService.ensureSchema`) — **filed 2026-07-28 from the user's "could the other lineages be affecting progress negatively?".**

Cost is also fine at present scale — of **86,626 node lines across 13 lineages only 558 are `Goal`**, the rest `Action` and friends, and cycle times show no trend (63s → 61s → 88s → 72s across the day, LLM-dominated).
  - **The latent defect the check surfaced:** `ensureSchema()` creates a uniqueness constraint and index for `DeferredMutation` and a constraint for `Blocker`, and **nothing for `Goal`**. So `MATCH (g:Goal) WHERE g.lineageId = $lineageId` is a full label scan, and since the 2026-07-26 lineage separation stopped purging, that label grows monotonically — every run adds ~40-60 goals and never removes any. Dedup runs per proposed subgoal per replan, so the scan is on a hot path.
  - **Trigger to watch, not a deadline:** free at 558 goals; at a few hundred runs (~30-50k goals) it is a scan per proposal. Bodies come from `RequestBodySynthesizer` (the artifact's own model fields); a parameterized `400` creates the resource first so the refusal is attributable to the body and not to absence.

Only `400` is now treated as "the input itself is refused" — the spec says so in as many words. ② **A refused SETUP request is now an abstain** (`BootGate.executeSequence`): the duplicate-loan probe's first POST is refused when the book and member it references do not exist, and without the guard the second POST's `404` would have been reported as "409 expected, got 404". This is general — any non-final request answering ≥400 means the asserted request is about a situation that was never created. ③ **The server-assigned `id` is dropped from creation bodies** — it is the same field the executor reads back to ground `$1.id`, and on a collision probe supplying it would collide on the supplied value instead of on the rule under test.
    - **A real defect the tests caught before the field did:** `ground()` used `String.replaceFirst`, so the replacement `$1.id` was read as a regex group reference and threw. Every parameterized `400` probe would have failed at construction.
    - **Coverage is pinned at the composition, not per stage:** `SpecRequirementProbeCoverageTest` runs the real pipeline (spec text → `SpecEndpointBehaviourQuery` → parser → synthesizer) over the verbatim seed spec and asserts the majority-probeable claim, that 400/404/409 are reachable and 422 deliberately is not, that no sequence carries an unresolved `{}`, and that every sequence ends on its own requirement's endpoint. Unit tests on each stage would all have passed while the composition covered nothing — the failure mode that held `criterion_probe_runs=0` for fourteen runs.
    - **DoD still NOT met** — it requires a FIELD firing: a run where the self-check raises a real defect and the loop repairs it at normal throughput. Cost is removed and coverage is measured; the run is next.

  - **Premise:** two lineages evolve the same seed differently (exactly what sits in the database now). Each may have solved parts the other did not. A merge would produce a THIRD tree taking the better parts of both, with provenance back to each parent — the code-layer form of the "child graph" idea.
  - **Depends on a measure of "better", which is thin today:** the T6-E ledger gives a per-RUN outcome (smoke/terminal) and criteria give per-criterion verdicts, but nothing scores a SUBTREE. Without per-part outcome attribution a merge is guesswork dressed as synthesis.

  - **GATE (measure before building, and the fixture now exists):** quantify what two same-seed lineages actually share — criteria overlapping by `codeDigest`, goal descriptions matching semantically, shared resolved ecosystem facts, and outright contradictions (15 contradictory (criterion, digest) pairs were measured INSIDE a single run on 2026-07-26, so cross-lineage contradiction is expected, not hypothetical). **If the overlap is thin, the honest close is that merging two runs of one seed buys little — recorded as evidence rather than assumed.**

Of the 87 criteria that ARE shared, **59 (67.8%) carry opposite verdicts**. On the original two-lineage fixture: **0 of 25 discovered goals shared**. Ecosystem facts turn out not to be per-lineage at all (one shared on-disk cache), and `codeDigest` — the identity axis this chain was to be built on — is set on 2.4% of criterion results.
  - **So the premise fails:** two runs of one seed redo the same skeleton (which regenerates for free) and then diverge into work that is 99% unique, disagreeing two times out of three where they meet. There is no accumulated common ground for a merge to reconcile. **Re-entry condition:** a fixture of lineages from DIFFERENT seeds (none exists), or a semantic-equivalence pass showing the exact-match floor understates `analysis` overlap by an order of magnitude. Full numbers and caveats on T6-G.

- [ ] **T4-CJ: Graph run/lineage identity — end purge-per-run; distinguish the current run from reference history** (`graph/*` services, `SystemResetConfig.purgeAll` call site, new run-identity mint at boot) — **filed 2026-07-17 (user direction: "maybe we'll come into the territory where we need to change this relatively soon… we need some distinction to address the current run and old runs (for reference)"). Phase I — Internalization. DESIGN + slice 1 buildable; the flip itself is trigger-gated.**
  - **The hazard this designs against:** every graph query today silently assumes the store holds ONLY the current run — keeping history without scoping the reads would contaminate snapshots, score baselines, and heuristic streaks with other runs' actions (subtle wrongness everywhere, no crash).   - **Survey (2026-07-17): ~87 query sites across 10 services, but the exposure is small.** Most reads are anchored by ids that are already globally unique across runs (goal UUIDs, timestamp-derived cycle/attempt ids) — they cannot contaminate. The dangerous minority are the UNSCOPED/aggregate reads (latest-action-by-timestamp, all-goals scans, recurring-heuristic tallies, score histories). Writes funnel through few chokepoints (`registerAction` for all Actions; the goal persist path; per-service CREATE sites ≈ 6–10 total).
  - **Identity model (two ids, matching the T4-CD vocabulary):** `lineageId` — stable across resume boots, minted on RESET, persisted in `meta/` (survives with the flags resume keeps); `runId` — minted every boot. Both stamped as properties on every node at the write chokepoints. Resume inherits lineage; fresh mints both.
  - **Slice 1 (buildable now, non-breaking):** mint + stamp only. Query behavior unchanged (a single-run graph is trivially scoped); T5-BD dumps start carrying ids, so history accumulated from now on is already distinguishable when the flip comes. This is the future-proofing move — cheap before the flip, archaeology after it.
  - **Slice 2 (the flip; audit-first):** classify all ~87 reads id-anchored vs unscoped; add lineage scoping to the unscoped ones ONLY; then reset stops purging (archive semantics — old lineages remain, `purgeAll` becomes an explicit operator action). Equivalence: snapshot/prompt renders byte-identical on a single-lineage graph before/after (the T4-BZ harness pattern).

So this is no longer an observation problem — the information arrives and the repair does not stick. Considered options: (1) extend coverage-review to claim granularity (audit → author missing criteria, output = ordinary criteria, NOT a new "claim" layer); (2) don't — treat it as observable in the data. **User chose (2): "we can sort it out by the data itself (e.g., graph queries)."** Grounding: the 38/12/21 asymmetry that started this was itself FOUND by querying the data (GoalStack grep). Measured twice now (2026-07-28 at n=15, restated 2026-07-29), **no run-level process metric predicts a good run** — reaching the package gate is necessary but not sufficient, plan-inflation ranges overlap, stagnation rate shows no separation. The one discriminator found is coarse ("~40% never empty their backlog"). A plausible reading is that run-level aggregation is the problem, not the features: a run is a mixture of subtrees that went well and badly, and averaging them destroys the signal. That is a testable claim and this ticket is what would test it.

    - **NOT ACTED ON MID-RUN.** A schema change while a run is live is exactly the class of thing this session already got wrong once.
  - **A/B RESULT — INDEXES HELP BY 21%, AND ARE NOT THE MAIN CAUSE.** Same build, same graph, 15 indexes instead of 3 (`.id` on every label the ingest path writes; all ONLINE before launch).     - *missing indexes* — **partially confirmed**: −21%, above.
    - *the T4-CJ lineage-stamp query* `MATCH (e)-[*1..2]-(x)` — **eliminated**: its 2-hop neighbourhood reaches **16 nodes**. The undirected variable-length pattern looked alarming and is not the cost.

    - **PER-COMMIT SERIES (6 samples, one run): 92.9 · 94.8 · 93.5 · 93.5 · 121.3 · 97.3 s** — median ~94.2s, roughly stable with one outlier. **No within-run growth trend**, contrary to a reading I made from two commits averaged together before separating them. The graph moved only 65,360 → 65,987 during this run, so the cross-run hypothesis (a larger graph makes `commit()` slower, which would explain 77s on 2026-07-28 against 153s now) remains plausible and **is not tested by this run**. Testing it needs the same build against graphs of very different sizes.
    - **PER-CYCLE, NOT A WARM-UP — checked, because the counter briefly suggested otherwise.** The first readout showed `sms-commit=…/1` after three cycles, which would have meant a one-time cost and a wrong headline. It was the readout lagging by one cycle (it is emitted at cycle end, before that cycle's ingest runs). The next readout resolved it: `sms-commit=187695ms/2` — commit #1 **92,861ms**, commit #2 **94,834ms** — matching the measured gaps of **93.0s and 95.0s**. Recurring, twice confirmed.
  - **~95s per cycle REMAINS UNEXPLAINED inside `ingestCycle`, and pinpointing it needs in-process timing rather than more reading.** *(Superseded by the line above — kept because the elimination sequence is the useful part of the record.)* The next slice is to time the batch build, `b.commit()`, the lineage-stamp query and the Cycle merge separately, under the existing category tracker. Bytecode archaeology has reached its useful limit.

    | | s/cycle | cycles per 90 min | post-cycle gap |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | before (synchronous ingest) | 153 | 35 | 120–153s |
    | the 23/23 run, 2026-07-28 | 79 | 62 | — |
    | **after** | **40** | **~134 projected** | **0.0s** |

    - **3.8× the previous throughput and ~2× the run that scored 23/23.** At 27 cycles the run had already done 12 merges — comparable work to the previous build's ENTIRE 90 minutes (35 cycles, 13 merges) in about 20.
    - **The cost is now countable instead of invisible, which was the point of bounding the queue.** First drops appeared at cycle ~24, exactly where the arithmetic said: the loop produces ingests at ~1.7/min and the substrate absorbs them at ~0.45/min (~134s each), a shortfall of ~1.25/min. **So roughly three of every four cycles' observations are dropped once the queue saturates.**
    - **This converts complete observational memory into SAMPLED observational memory, and that is a real change, not a free win.** It is strictly better than the previous state — where the loop paid ~94s per cycle to guarantee a completeness whose value had never been measured — but whether sampling is acceptable depends on what the memory is FOR, which is a substrate question rather than a throughput one. **Recorded as an open consequence, not settled.**
    - **Reversible:** `autobuilder.memory.sms.async=false` restores the synchronous path exactly, pinned by a test.
    - **🔴🔴 THE MOST IMPORTANT RESULT OF THE RUN, AND IT QUALIFIES THE WIN: 3.8× THE CYCLES BOUGHT 3.8× REPETITIONS OF THE SAME REJECTED MUTATION.** By cycle 42 the loop had spent **33 cycles** on variants of one subgoal ("Implement the Book repository"), proposing 13 mutations of which **11 were REJECTED**, every time for the same reason — a `BookRepository` that drops `@Repository`. `MergeRegressionHeuristic` fired **29 times** and was RIGHT each time: the artifact still holds 3 `@Repository`, 3 `@Service`, 4 `@RestController` **because** of those rejections.
      - **The loop was told, in its own prompt, 28 times.** The rejection prose reached 28 distinct evolution prompts through T4-BX's path. It regenerated the same defect anyway.
      - **So the binding constraint was never cycles.** Making the loop 3.8× faster made it fail 3.8× faster. This is the third independent confirmation of the session's structural finding — the loop's problem is acting on what it already knows, not seeing more or having more time — and it is the one that should govern what gets built next. **A throughput fix is a multiplier on whatever the loop actually does; it is not itself progress.**
      - **What it does NOT mean:** the throughput fix was still worth making (cycles were being spent on a 94s write nobody read back, and now they are not), and the heuristic is not at fault (it protected real invariants 29 times). The gap is between "a correct rejection with a stated reason" and "a different next proposal".
  - **DoD: MET.** Gate wall-clock in `summary.txt` and the ledger ✅; unaccounted fraction reported ✅; **the 77s→153s regression attributed to a named component with numbers ✅ — `GraphWriter.Batch.commit()`, 92.9s/cycle, 99.8% of the SMS ingest and ~78% of the loop's wall clock.**
  - **THE DECISION IS NOW SOMEONE'S TO MAKE, and it is not a tuning question.** Three options, in increasing order of commitment: ① take the ingest OFF the cycle's critical path (it writes observational memory; nothing in the cycle reads it back), ② make `commit()` cheaper, which means changing a dependency this repo does not own, ③ gate the ingest behind a switch and measure what the loop loses without it. **Option ① is the one the evidence points at** — a synchronous 93-second write of observations nobody consults during the cycle is on the wrong side of the loop.
  - **What this is worth:** removing it from the critical path would roughly **double the loop's throughput** — 35 cycles per 90 minutes back toward the 62 the 23/23 run managed. That is larger than any mechanism built this week, and it was invisible because nothing timed a library call.

  - **Where it leans, stated without calling it:** mean delta **-20%**, **3 of 9 positive**, against a baseline that was worse in **19 of 19** runs at **-43%**. Both criteria point at "moved it" — but the mean is AT the threshold rather than past it, and per-run deltas range from **-70% to +22%**, so the run-level measure is noisy enough that one more sample can move the mean several points. That volatility (-18 → -26 → -35 → -20 across the sample's growth) is the whole reason the rule named ten.
  - **✅ VERDICT AT n=10 (2026-08-04) — THE RULE FIRES "MOVED IT", ON ONE LEG OF TWO.**

    | | baseline (pre-2026-08-01) | window |
    |---|---|---|
    | loan work converted worse | **19 of 19 runs** | 7 of 10 |
    | mean delta | **-43%** | **-23%** |
    | positive deltas | 0 | **3 of 10** |

    The rule was an OR — *mean beats -20%* **or** *≥3 of 10 positive*. **Only the second leg fired**: the mean is -23% and does NOT beat -20%. Honouring the rule as written means the verdict stands; saying so plainly means recording that it rests on the weaker criterion. The run that completed the sample swung **-58%** and pulled the mean from -20% to -23% — the sample-completing run moved it AWAY from the stronger leg, which is the clearest possible illustration of why a fixed N beats stopping when the number looks right.
    - **🔴 THE RULE'S OWN FRAMING OVER-ATTRIBUTES, and the verdict must not inherit that.** It was written as "T2-EZ moved this", but the window is defined by a DATE, not by an isolated change: everything shipped since 2026-08-01 sits inside it — `T2-FB`, `T2-EY`, `T1-FQ`, `T1-FR`, `T2-FD` (both shapes), `T2-FE`. **What is established is that the loan-conversion gap narrowed after 08-01. Which mechanism did it is not established by this test and cannot be.** Same lesson as T6-L's third DoD clause the same day: reaching a number by an unattributed route is not the same as the predicted cause working.
    - **🔴 AND THE A/B I NAMED CANNOT SETTLE IT — measured 2026-08-04, after recommending it twice.** The per-run delta has **sd ≈ 31 points** (range -70 to +22 over this very window). Detecting a 20-point effect needs **~39 runs PER ARM**, a 10-point effect **~155** — five days and nineteen days of continuous 90-minute runs. The experiment was never viable at any realistic budget, and building its apparatus would have been the expensive way to learn that.
    - **✅ WHAT REPLACES IT: `scripts/steering_followthrough.py` — attribution per FIRING, not per run.** When a block names a specific defect, is that defect gone by the next `T1-EC` probe? N is an order of magnitude larger and run-level noise never enters. It is the question `CompileFixInjector` already answers about itself ("removed its targeted diagnostic"). First reading over the corpus:

      | block | firings | fully cleared | items cleared |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | missing-member | 53 | **50/53 (94%)** | 52/55 |
      | missing-type | 3 | 3/3 | 4/4 |
      | unwrapped-value | 40 | **6/39 (15%)** | **15/115 (13%)** |

      **"Add this member to that class" is followed almost always; "make the producer and the consumer agree" is followed about one time in seven.** A real difference between two mechanisms built on the same day, invisible to any score-level comparison.
    - **⚠ It shows the advice was FOLLOWED, not that following it helped** — and a high follow-through beside a flat score would itself be worth knowing, because it would mean the blocks work and the theory behind them is wrong. Keeping those two claims apart is the point.
    - **Checked and deliberately NOT acted on:** the 31% missing-METHOD share is `T4-BQ`'s subject, and its usage-derived member synthesizer has fired **0 times in 224 skeleton creations** across these 25 runs — because `synthesize-members: false` in `application.yml`, held off on a recorded 2026-06-16 field A/B (no outcome benefit, plus an `incompatible types` cascade from conservative `Object` typing). That is a decided question with a written reason, not an oversight; re-opening it needs the Object-typing fix the note names, not a flag flip.

- [ ] **T6-I: Does accumulated knowledge actually improve outcomes? — the falsifiability yardstick for the whole wave** (paired runs, `scripts/outcome_ledger.py`) — **filed 2026-07-26. See [[project-wave2-structure]]; this ticket exists to stop the wave from becoming a museum.**
  - **The problem it guards against:** layers A–C of wave 2 (retention, portability, reconciliation) are all plumbing. They assume that accumulating experience improves what the loop does. **Nothing measures that assumption**, and [[feedback-activity-not-progress]] is the standing warning that a mechanism firing is not the same as it helping. Without this, a knowledge base is unfalsifiable — always defensible, never demonstrated.
  - **Design:** paired runs on one seed — one with the accumulated base available to the consuming path, one without — compared on the ledger's own outcome measures (terminal, smoke, merges, criteria moved). [[feedback-replay-over-batches]] forbids small-N live batches EXCEPT for a rare strategic question with N and a decision rule fixed in advance; this is such a question, so both must be written down before the first run.
  - **Sequencing:** this GATES the expensive half of the chain. Build one thin consumer first (layer D), measure with this, and only then invest in `T4-CR`/`T4-CN`/`T4-CM`/`T4-CS`.
  - **DoD:** a stated N, a stated decision rule, the paired runs executed, and the verdict recorded — including the negative case, which would be the most valuable outcome the wave could produce.

- [x] **T6-A: The smoke test scores a run's final files, never the best compiling version it saved along the way** (`scripts/preflight.sh` + smoke reporting; scripts only — the Java loop is not touched) — **filed 2026-07-18; FIRST NATIVE T6 (harness & yardsticks — tier added same day, see `tier_definitions.md`). Body reworded to plain language 2026-07-24 at user request; original 2026-07-18 wording ("smoke yardstick"/"external kills") retired and preserved in git history.**
  - **Plain summary:** The smoke test (`scripts/smoke23.sh`) grades a run by starting the artifact as it stands when the run ends and counting how many of its 23 REST checks pass. Two problems. (a) When the loop stops itself, it has already saved the best *compiling* version of the artifact (the T4-CA save hook), but the smoke test ignores that saved copy and grades the final files — which may be a later, broken state. (b) When a run is stopped from outside — the preflight watcher hitting its time limit — the save hook never runs, so a run that merged a lot of working code can leave nothing saved at all. Net effect: the score can be worse than the run's actual best work, and we can draw false conclusions from it.
  - **Concrete case (same-day proof):** run `2026-07-18_09-21-56` scored `smoke=artifact-build-failed` because its final files include a model-written `MemberServiceTest` that calls a `Member` constructor that doesn't exist (the test won't compile). But `preserved-artifact-provenance.json` in that same run's output shows the loop had saved a version that *did* compile (`verifiedBuildResult=COMPILE_OK`, chosen from 81 snapshots, saved 2 minutes before the run stopped). The good version was on disk; the score never looked at it — so "extra time didn't rescue this run" was partly just a measurement mistake. This is not a loop bug: the save hook worked, and `quarantine=0` here is correct (that check only applies when a run claims completion, which this one never did).
  - **The time-limit gap (3+ sightings):** runs stopped by the time limit never trigger the in-process save hook. Series-1 run 2 (21 merges) and series-2 run 2 (23 merges) both stopped at the time limit with nothing saved — and these large-merge runs are exactly the kind that dominate on harder targets.
  - **What to build (scripts only, loop untouched):**
    1. **Reconstruct the saved artifact when a run is stopped by the time limit.** Each snapshot already carries the facts needed to pick the best compiling one — that is what the stamps are for. Do that selection offline in preflight, the same way the in-process hook would have, so a time-limit run still gets a "best compiling version" even though the hook never ran. (Reuse `PreservedArtifactService`'s selection logic.)
    2. **Report two smoke scores.** Keep `smoke=` meaning "score of the final files" so past runs stay comparable, and add `smoke_preserved=` for the score of the best saved/compiling version. Which one becomes the headline number is decided later, once we have a batch of runs scored both ways — not now.
  - **Done when:** both changes are in the preflight/smoke scripts; a replay over saved run corpora shows the dual score (a run with a compiling saved copy scores it; time-limit runs get an offline-selected artifact when a snapshot qualifies); the new ledger/summary fields are documented. *(Note 2026-07-24: the original 2026-07-18 corpora this DoD named were since lost to a `/tmp` clear — validation now needs a freshly captured run or another surviving corpus.)*
  - **SHIPPED 2026-07-24 (scripts only; the Java loop is untouched, as filed).** Two pieces: (1) `scripts/select_preserved.py` — an offline replica of `PreservedArtifactService`'s selection (run-relative entry-point bar incl. lineage-provenance escalation, recorded-failure disqualification, newest-first-then-merged probe order); it emits the probe order and the caller compile-verifies, because a stamped `buildResult` can be stale (the T4-CA field defect). (2) `scripts/preflight.sh` — the smoke block refactored into a reusable `build_boot_smoke` + a `compiles` (`mvn compile` == `JavacDirectProbe` COMPILE_OK) helper, plus a T6-A block that reports **two** scores: `smoke=` (final files, meaning unchanged) and `smoke_preserved=` with `preserved_source=`. `preserved_source` is `loop-preserved` when an honest halt left `meta/preserved-artifact/` (score it directly), or `reconstructed:<cycle>` when a time-limit/external kill left none (select offline over `$target/snapshots`, compile-walk to the first compiling candidate, copy it to `$corpus/preserved-reconstructed`, then score it). Fidelity note: selection is by **compile**, not packageability — a tree can compile (so the hook would preserve it) yet fail `mvn package` at repackage (no main class); `smoke_preserved` then honestly reads `artifact-build-failed`. New summary fields + `preserved_source` legend documented in the preflight header. **Validation:** replayed against the live 45-snapshot corpus of a real deadline run (`terminal=deadline smoke=artifact-build-failed`, restructured to `com.example.library.*` and destroyed its entry point everywhere): reconstruction selected the newest snapshot `cycle-1784831586745` (compiles clean), `smoke_preserved=artifact-build-failed` — the correct **negative** (this run never had a packageable saved copy). **Tests:** `scripts/test_select_preserved.py` — 9 stdlib-unittest cases pinning the selection semantics against `PreservedArtifactService` (run-relative bar, lineage-provenance escalation, recorded-failure disqualification incl. null/SKIPPED not disqualifying, newest-then-merged order, nullsFirst timestamp ordering, unstamped-snapshot skip, both abstain edges); runs in ~4ms with no maven/model/network (`python3 scripts/test_select_preserved.py`). **Coverage boundary (honest):** this is the FIRST test for any `scripts/*.py` helper — the repo had no convention, so the other helpers (`run_profile.py`, `watch_report.py`, `diagnosis_replay.py`) remain untested too. The preflight bash glue (`build_boot_smoke`, `compiles`, the loop-preserved/reconstructed/abstain branch selection) is NOT automated — it needs maven + a booting JVM and there is no bash test harness in-repo; it is covered only by the one manual end-to-end replay above. **Deviations:** none from the filed body. The compile-vs-package fidelity point above was discovered during validation and is captured in-code. **Watch item open:** a genuine *rescue* (`smoke_preserved` > `smoke`, i.e. a run whose final files broke but that saved a bootable copy) has not been demonstrated — the surviving corpora all destroyed their entry point, so no positive number was reachable; the first field run showing it closes that observation.
  - **FIELD-VALIDATED 2026-07-24 (two live preflight runs, BOTH branches exercised):** (1) **loop-preserved** — run `2026-07-24_10-02-09`, `terminal=honest-halt:empty-backlog-injection-limit` (in-process halt, ~21 min, before its 25-min cap): the T4-CA hook fired, `preserved_source=loop-preserved`, preflight scored the hook's copy directly (`verifiedBuildResult=COMPILE_OK`, 40 snapshots considered). `smoke=smoke_preserved=artifact-build-failed` — honest, not a rescue: the preserved tree compiles but has no entry point (`com.example.library` restructure) so `mvn package` fails at repackage. (2) **reconstruction** — run `2026-07-24_10-24-15`, `terminal=GOAL_FULFILLED`, `smoke=23/23` (only the 2nd perfect smoke on record; a full-length natural run converged at 25 merges): the reconstruction path fired (`preserved_source=reconstructed:cycle-1784884638429`, `entryPointRequired=True`, 13 eligible of 78) and produced a fully working artifact scoring **23/23** — the reconstruction branch validated POSITIVELY in situ, with the run-relative entry-point bar correctly applied. Both branches now field-confirmed; the rescue watch (smoke_preserved > smoke) stays open (neither run diverged: run 1 both failed, run 2 both 23/23). **Surfaced a T4-CA gap (filed separately):** the `GOAL_FULFILLED` pause branch (`AutobuilderService` ~L564) does NOT call `preserve()` — only the `DerivedFacts.systemPaused` branch (L526) does, and fulfilled runs carry no `pausedReason` so they skip it. T6-A's reconstruction backstopped the missing hook cleanly, which is exactly its purpose beyond deadlines.
  - **RICHER RECORDING added 2026-07-24 (scripts-side, T6-A follow-on):** the dual score's *point* is the final-vs-best gap (drift). `scripts/drift_report.py` computes per run, folded into `summary.txt`: `score_delta` (preserved − final; positive = the run ended worse than a state it saved), `run_duration_min`, `total_cycles`, `peaked_at_cycle` (best-saved cycle + position k/N), `drift_tail_cycles` / `drift_tail_min` (the stretch spent drifting after the peak). Validated on both field corpora (both peaked at their final cycle → drift_tail=0) + a synthetic mid-run-peak case; durable test `scripts/test_drift_report.py` (6 cases incl. the peaks-midway drift). (umbrella; successor to the T4-J audit; user design steer 2026-07-10). **READ FIRST: [[project-t4bz-design-note]]** (as-built map, family map with target carriers, findings F1-F5, invariants I1-I12, open questions Q-a..Q-e) **+ its evidence base [[project-signal-dispositions]] + [[project-t4j-perturbation-lab]] — every claim below is measured there.**
  - **The problem, in the audit's numbers:** the signal layer is three different things wearing one abstraction. (1) *Messages between agents* (event-like family: REPLAN_REQUESTED, DIVERGENCE_REQUEST, ... — cleared by consumers; decay is a backstop for missed clears). (2) *Cached views of context state* (state-like family: BUILD_BROKEN mirrors buildOutcome; the healthiest members — BUILD_FIX_LOCUS_STUCK, TEST_REPAIR_FOCUS, RECURRING_DEFECT_DOMINANT — are ALREADY re-derived every cycle and only pretend to be stored). (3) *Attention weights* (ROLE_* identity family — the only place continuous strength/decay dynamics measurably matter, as participation windows). Meanwhile the analog machinery is mostly costume: strengths pinned at the 3.0 cap 80-93% of the time, decay decision-inert except the ROLE windows, ranking largely decorative (exact analysis/planner ties resolved by jitter; eligibility, not rank, picks the executor), mutate() never used.
  - **The user's model (the design bet):** a "signal" should not be a first-class stored object with its own coded manifestation. The mechanisms — with their occurrences and urgencies — ARE the signals; the signal *map* is a derived, grouped readout over those events and facts (the meta-benchmark the system and its LLMs consult: snapshots, analysis/interpretation prompts, observability). Control flows through the mechanisms directly; the readout cannot go stale because it is computed, not stored.
  - **Migration safety net (this is why the ticket is buildable now):** the T4-J instruments are the equivalence harness. FrozenCycleObserver + the 28-state library + SignalOutcomeProbeTest pin the CURRENT selection behavior; each slice must reproduce the recorded decisions (or justify each divergence explicitly) before its old machinery is deleted. AgentPromptRenderer pins the prompt surface. No behavioral cliff, slice by slice.
  - **Ordering (hard):** 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5, strictly sequential; 2 and 3 are independently shippable after 1 but 2 lands first (smaller, pattern already exists in-repo — F5). Nothing lands as a coexisting second path ([[project-t4ai-design-note]]'s operative lesson: delete the duplicate, don't keep both). Sub-tickets below are the six slices; each is its own DoD and its own commit(s) — see [[feedback-ticket-definition-of-done]].
  - **Honest risks, stated up front:** the loop currently converges (fastest fulfilled run on record post-meta-deletion) — this is elegance+truthfulness work whose OUTCOME benefit is unproven; the LLM-facing channel changes prompt text (needs the prompt-pin + a layer-2 check before/after); T4-scale with regression risk, so slices land individually behind the equivalence harness, never as one rewrite.
  - **Umbrella done when:** every signal type is represented as what it is (message / derived view / attention window); the stored-Signal control path is deleted (T4-BZ-5); snapshots + prompts render an equivalent-or-better readout; equivalence harness green across the state library at every slice; suite green; one confirming field run per major slice. Residual design questions (analysis/planner tie-break Q-e, evaluation-prompt signal-blindness) stay NOTES inside T4-BZ-4/5, not new tickets.

See [[project-introspection-as-north-star]]: the derived readout IS the self-model surface.

- [x] **T4-BX: When one agent rejects work, tell the next agent WHY — not just that it happened** — **SHIPPED 2026-07-06 (suite 1803).** Scope was CORRECTED by the user mid-build: the filed "structured value, not a pasted sentence" line below mis-applied a code-path rule to a prompt-path problem (two wrong turns: an invented `TEST_ONLY_CHANGE` enum, then a redundant ProblemContext duplicate — both reverted). What shipped is the simple thing the ticket was actually about: **relay the authored reasons verbatim, as prose, for the downstream LLM to read.** `EvaluationAgent.collectRejectionReasons` gathers the evaluator's `feedbackMessage` + every REJECTED/STAGNATING heuristic's rationale (author-prefixed) on a semantic rejection (build failures excluded structurally via `BuildResult` — they have their own channels); `CycleContextData.rejectionFeedback` retyped `List<String>` (was a dead always-null String); `ContextLineageTracker` carries it one cycle, clears on merge; `RejectionFeedbackPromptBlock` renders a WHY-THE-PREVIOUS-ATTEMPT-WAS-REJECTED block into the **evolution** prompt (previously received nothing) and the planner prompt (deduped against its existing evaluation-feedback line). Same channel for the analysis agent: `AnalysisObservationsPromptBlock`. See [[feedback-string-consumption-path]] for the per-consumer discriminator this earned.
  - **Field validation (run 17, 2026-07-06, 121 cyc / 33 merges): ACTIVATION confirmed** — 28 relay firings, 112 WHY-REJECTED blocks, 188 ANALYSIS-OBSERVATIONS blocks, correct authored content in the prompts. Outcome effect NOT claimed (single run, no A/B) per [[feedback-activity-not-progress]].
  - **NOTE (not built, by design):** the filed "give-up brake reads them" slice presumed structured carriers; under the corrected prose design, a brake parsing prose for control flow is exactly the string-consumption anti-pattern. The run-17 false give-up was a different mechanism anyway (born-broken tests, see the field note on T4-BN-3). Revisit only if a run shows the brake halting while an unaddressed structured blocker (ProblemContext) is open.
  - **What breaks:** when the evaluator rejects a mutation it writes the reason ("this only edits a test file, it doesn't implement the rule"). That sentence is logged and thrown away. The next time the evolution agent writes code it doesn't know why the last try was rejected, so it guesses the same wrong way again. Same for the analysis agent's finding "LoanRepository doesn't exist yet" — it reaches the prompt as a bare fact, not as "and that's what's blocking you." Between cycles the only thing passed is a name and a number (e.g. `REPETITION_DETECTED = 3.0`); a number can't say "stop editing tests, write the repository."
  - **The proof it's a real hole:** there's already a field meant to carry the reject reason to the next cycle — `CycleContextData.rejectionFeedback` — and it's always set to `null` (`CycleContextCoordinator:130`). An earlier version *did* pass the reason (`EvaluationOutcome.feedbackMessage`), but T4-BD deleted it because it worked by fragile text-matching, and nothing replaced it.
  - **Where it bit (2026-07-05 stall):** loop kept rewriting Loan tests while `LoanRepository` was the actual missing piece. The analysis agent knew the symbol was missing, the evaluator knew the mutations were test-only, the planner saw it was going in circles — but each only had its own piece, none reached the agent that could act, and the give-up brake saw only "7 cycles, no merge" and stopped. Build compiled fine the whole time, so the problem was aiming at the wrong file, not a broken build.
  - **The fix:** fill in `rejectionFeedback` (and the analysis finding) with a small **structured** value — *what kind of problem* + *which class/file it's about* — and put it into the evolution agent's prompt and the planner's input. Any agent can add one, any agent can read one; no central list of agents to maintain. Before the give-up brake halts, it checks these: if something is still marked missing and nobody has addressed it, that means "wrong target, replan" rather than "repeating myself, stop."
  - **Keep it structured, not a pasted sentence** — pasting the reason back is exactly the text-matching T4-BD deleted. Carry a kind + a name (a class/symbol), not a paragraph; keep the framework's own strings free of target-project and ecosystem names.
  - **Done when:** the reject reason and the missing-symbol finding reach the evolution and planner prompts as structured values; the give-up brake reads them; re-running the 07-05 stall aims at `LoanRepository` instead of halting; `rejectionFeedback` is wired up or removed; tests green.
  - **Size:** wiring `rejectionFeedback` is small and could ship alone; the give-up-brake change is the next slice. Write a short design note first and check for an existing pattern before adding anything new. **Filed 2026-07-06.** See [[project-agent-diagnosis-not-shared]], [[project-introspection-as-north-star]].

  - **CLOSED 2026-07-15 — design note delivered; recommendation: DEFER, with a stated evidence-gated re-entry condition.**

The dominant missing-package shapes are the target's OWN packages (declared-but-misplaced/not-yet-written types, thousands of hits) and malformed LLM tokens — recipe catalogues address neither. The recipe set's breadth (servlet/ws/mail/annotation...) solves a problem this corpus does not have.
  - **2. SPI sketch (recorded for re-entry):** `RewriteRecipeRunner` slots between the registry and the LLM lookup in `SymbolImportResolver`'s chain, same `FixProposal` contract as today's rewrite mode. Recipes register as DATA rows (recipe id + trigger predicate over classified diagnostics + GAV effect); the runner names no ecosystem ([[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]]); T3-BU's `replacementFor`/`manifest` API (closed 2026-07-15) is the precondition and is now met. Write-then-probe interplay is fine in principle (runner emits FileMutations), but the parse cost lands on every consult. Contrast: the current rewrite mode is a string prefix substitution — proportionate to the observed 2-family need.
  - **4. Recommendation: DEFER.** Re-entry condition (revisable capability gap, not a ban, per [[feedback-capability-gap-not-prohibition]]): adopt when the corpus shows a migration shape the prefix-rewrite map cannot express (method/type-level API migration), or ≥2 distinct NEW legacy-prefix families beyond the registered rows within one corpus generation. The registry today covers `javax.validation` / `javax.persistence` → jakarta equivalents as a hand-curated stopgap. OpenRewrite's `org.openrewrite.java.migrate.JavaxToJakarta` recipe set covers the entire javax→jakarta surface (servlet, annotation, ws, mail, ...) plus many other ecosystem migrations the registry would otherwise grow into.
  - **Scope (design only, ~300 word note delivered as the ticket body — no code):**

    2. Sketch a `RewriteRecipeRunner` SPI that fits the existing resolver chain (registry → recipe runner → LLM lookup). The SPI must respect [[feedback-no-ecosystem-jargon-in-framework-code]] — recipes are registered as data; the runner names no specific ecosystem.
    3. Estimate adoption cost: dependency size, classpath isolation, runtime budget per recipe (recipes can scan the whole source tree — needs bounding), interplay with `CompileProbeService`'s write-then-probe model.

  - **The three failure modes the hardcoded tables guarantee:**
    1. **Version drift.** Registry says `mockito-core:5.7.0`; project pulls in `5.11` via spring-boot-starter-test. Resolver edit adds `5.7.0` → version conflict on the next build, registry-emitted fix marked failed via `markResolutionFailed`. Cascade closes only after the LLM happens to remove the offending version literal.
    2. **Incomplete coverage.** Registry has `assertThat` but not `assertThatThrownBy`; `containsExactly` but not `containsExactlyInAnyOrderElementsOf`; covers AssertJ but not Hamcrest. Each missing entry produces a "false rejection" cascade identical in shape to the ones we've already closed — the cascade-shape is the system-level failure mode and row-adds don't address it.
    3. **Authoritative-but-wrong.** Even when the project's own pom declares `mockito-core:5.11`, the registry's `5.7.0` row "wins" because the resolver consults the registry first. The registry's worldview overrides the project's. There is no error-correction path that updates the registry from observed project state.
  - **Discovery sources, ranked (cheap → expensive):**
    1. **Project's own pom dependency tree.** Already on disk. Parse `pom.xml` (and transitively-resolved deps via `mvn dependency:list` or just-in-time on first need), reverse-index each artifact's exported package roots → GAV. Hits the hot path for the common case (the project already declared what it imports) at zero LLM cost. Subsumes the `replacedBy(missingPackage, pomXml)` SB2/SB3 detection — discovery sees what's actually on the classpath, not what the registry assumes.
    2. **Project's own source.** `import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;` in a test file already says which simple-name comes from which source. Index `import` statements across `src/test` (and `src/main`) on bootstrap; the index is authoritative for "what does this project consider the resolution of `when`?". Covers the `STATIC_METHOD_TO_PREFIX` use case without any hardcoded map.
    3. **Maven Central REST.** For the long-tail case where the symbol is genuinely missing from the project: `https://search.maven.org/solrsearch/select?q=fc:org.mockito.Mockito&rows=5` resolves an FQN-prefix or class to candidate artifacts. Network-bound — cache aggressively. Budget per resolution; degrade gracefully.
    4. **OpenRewrite recipe catalogue.** For *migration* shapes (legacy → modern prefix), OpenRewrite recipes already enumerate the equivalences (`JavaxToJakarta`, `Mockito1to4`, …). Consume them rather than re-enumerating in our own table. Belongs under T4-BJ if/when that adopts. Don't re-implement.
    5. **LLM lookup.** Last resort, with the `failedResolutions` set still used as bypass. The existing `LlmSymbolImportLookupService` covers this layer.
  - **Migration plan — registry becomes a fallback, not a source of truth:**
    - **Step 1:** new `PackageDiscoveryService` with `lookup(symbol)` consulting discovery sources 1–3 in order. Returns `Optional<Gav>` with provenance (which source resolved it). Behaviour event `package_discovery_hit` carries the source.
    - **Step 2:** `WellKnownPackageRegistry.lookup(symbol, pomXml)` rewires to ask discovery first; falls back to the hardcoded TABLE only when discovery returns empty. Existing TABLE entries become *short-term-fallback* entries with a single Javadoc note: "Kept as fallback for `<symbol>` because discovery doesn't cover this case yet — file a discovery improvement instead of adding more rows here."
    - **Step 3:** the three hardcoded maps shrink to zero. `SIMPLE_NAME_TO_PREFIX`, `STATIC_METHOD_TO_PREFIX`, `PACKAGE_REPLACED_BY` become discovery-driven indexes, populated at bootstrap from the project's pom + source + (optionally) Maven Central warmup. `TABLE` keeps Spring Boot starter coordinates only as long as we can't resolve them from the SB BOM (Step 4 below).
    - **Step 4:** Spring Boot BOM resolution — parse `<parent><artifactId>spring-boot-starter-parent</artifactId><version>X.Y.Z</version>` and pull the actual managed-versions table from the BOM POM (network or cached). Removes the last "we picked a version because we had to" literals from autobuilder framework code.
    - **Step 5:** delete the no-longer-needed maps. Per [[feedback-ship-full-scope]] — the ticket includes the delete.
    - **Step 6 (scope extended 2026-06-11) — `SymbolImportCache` is a fourth frozen-worldview table.** `firestarter/cache/symbol-imports.json` keys by bare simple name and survives `reset-on-start` (`SystemResetConfig` wipes output/mutations/snapshots/meta but **not** `cache/`). Inspected 2026-06-11: 25 entries, 22 of them LLM-said-NONE nulls for the *target project's own domain types* (`Loan`, `Book`, `Member`, every exception) plus method/field tokens (`isPresent`, `orElseThrow`, `getMemberById`, `memberRepository`) that should never reach an import lookup; `JpaRepository` pinned to `spring-data-jpa:2.7.0` (SB2-era) inter-run.
